x: The 4Runner started life in 1983 as a Hilux pickup with a removable fibreglass top, sold in the US from the 1984½ model year. It has been body-on-frame ever since, through six generations, which in this segment makes it something close to a living fossil — and that is exactly why people buy it. N60 A Hilux pickup with a removable fibreglass lid — solid front axle until the 1986 switch to independent front suspension. A Hilux pickup with a removable fibreglass hat, a four-cylinder that refuses to die and — for 1984–85 only — a solid front axle. Slow, rusty, uncomfortable and utterly charming, which is exactly why the prices went up.

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: Owners' consensus is 31x10.50R15 — Toyota-4Runner.org members say 31s fit with no lift and you can get away without regearing. 33x12.50s on a stock truck rub the front valance, wheel-well corners and rear pinch weld; IH8MUD owners estimate about 1.5 in of lift (plus some trimming) for 33s, and say the 22R-E will want lower gears.

t: Which years have the solid front axle?
x: 1984 and 1985. Toyota switched to independent front suspension with a three-inch-wider track for 1986, so 1986–89 trucks are IFS. Solid-axle trucks are the off-roader's favourite; IFS trucks ride better on the road.

Most enthusiasts prefer the 22R-E four-cylinder — Hagerty says so, and Expedition Portal members advise skipping the V6. The 3.0 V6 (1988–89) has more power but carries the 3VZ-E's head-gasket reputation and is harder to work on; the 22R-E is slow but famously simple.

t: Can I take the roof off?
x: Yes. The rear fibreglass top is held on by 14 bolts, and a rear roll bar was standard. Owners note the open-top experience mostly benefits rear passengers — and that ageing tops are a common leak point.
Not in the US. Diesel engines were offered in Hilux pickups, but Wikipedia records that no diesel 4Runners were imported to the US.

The 22R-TE turbo four arrived for 1986 with 135 hp, mostly paired with the four-speed automatic in SR5s. It's much rarer than the 22R-E, and LC Engineering still sells dedicated 22R-TE short blocks and turbo parts.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: Not much. Wikipedia records an EPA city rating of 17 mpg for the 22R-TE turbo truck and 14.5 mpg in period testing; Trail4Runner quotes 19 city / 23 highway for a stock four-cylinder, which looks optimistic. Expect less with bigger tyres, a lift or a tired engine.

t: Is a 1988–89 V6 covered by Toyota's head gasket campaign?
x: Not any more. An October 1996 Special Policy Adjustment extended head-gasket coverage for 1988–1994 V6 trucks; the later V06 campaign covered 1/90–10/94 production and expired on 24 September 2018. Today a blown 3VZ-E head gasket is on you.

Hagerty's write-up on rising 1984–89 values gave averages of $8,400 (#3 Good), $13,700 (#2 Excellent) and $21,100 (#1 Concours), and cited Bring a Trailer sales of $19,250 for a 100,000-mile 1984 SR5 and $17,500 for a 168,000-mile 1986 SR5. Expedition Portal members reckoned a maintained 22R-E truck under about 170,000 miles could still be found for under $5,000.

t: Should I solid-axle swap an IFS truck?
x: IH8MUD members are split. Some say the 1986–95 Toyota IFS is 'pretty stout' unless you rock-crawl hard; others who broke IFS shafts say to 'spend the money on a SAS and never look back'. Kits for 1979–85-style solid axles, long-travel IFS and stronger axles are all still sold.

Mechanical parts, yes — the 22R family is shared with Toyota pickups and LC Engineering runs a dedicated 1984–1989 4Runner catalogue. Body panels, floors and interior trim are the hard part; Hagerty notes reproduction seats and floors generally don't exist.

x: Flexier leaf packs, longer shocks and high-steer turn a solid-axle truck into a proper crawler — Trail-Gear claims up to 20 in of articulation from its Classic kit.

t: Ifs Lift & Steering (1986–89) — ToyTec 2 in ball joint spacer kit (via LC Engineering), Total Chaos Caddy idler arm
x: Ball-joint spacers and torsion bars are the classic budget lift; a stronger idler arm takes the slop out on bigger tyres.

x: Bumpers and skids protect the parts that are hardest to replace — and the 1st gen market is small, so buy from people who still make it.

x: Bigger tyres and a 22R-E need help: transfer-case reduction gears and a rear locker are the traditional answers.

x: Birfields and CVs are the weak links once you add tyre size and a locker.

Overshadowed by the cult 3rd gen, haunted by the V6's head gaskets — and quietly one of the cheapest ways into an old-school Toyota.

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: 31s — IH8MUD members call 31s the right size for a stock 2nd gen, and Toyota-4Runner.org owners agree 31x10.50R15 fits without a lift or regear. A narrow 33x10.50R15 can be squeezed in with some pounding and trimming, but expect rubbing at the valance and pinch weld; about 1.5 in of lift is the usual recommendation for 33s.

t: Was my V6 covered by Toyota's head-gasket campaign?
x: Special Service Campaign V06 covered 3VZ-E trucks, 4Runners and T100s built from 1/90 to 10/94, replacing head gaskets regardless of whether they leaked. Forum owners report completed trucks got a label on the left front door hinge post. The campaign expired on 24 September 2018, so any repair now is at your cost.

The V6 makes 150 hp and 180 lb-ft against the four's 116 hp and 139 lb-ft, which matters in a heavier four-door. The 22R-E is simpler, more durable and outside the head-gasket saga. Owners generally say a maintained 3VZ-E is fine — but it must never overheat.
Yes, built from 1989 to May 1993. US sales ended in August 1992 and Canada continued through 1993. They cost more than the four-door because of the US chicken tax, so they're rare.

t: How often does the timing belt need doing?
x: A 4Runners.com member recalls four years or 96,000 km (about 60,000 miles) as the typical interval for the 3VZ-E. Do the water pump at the same time and use a quality kit.

t: What fuel economy does it get?
x: Not much. Wikipedia lists an EPA city rating of 15 mpg for the V6 with the four-speed automatic, with observed testing at 14.28 mpg. Bigger tyres and a lift make it worse.

t: Does it have ABS or a locker?
x: Rear-wheel ABS was standard on the SR5 V6 from 1990 and four-wheel ABS was optional. There was no factory locker in the US — differentials were open, with a limited-slip only offered in Japan and Europe. Aftermarket lockers are the usual fix.

The common recipe is a 2 in lift: ToyTec sells a kit with rear coils for 1990–95 4Runners, Old Man Emu sells 2 in rear coils in standard and HD rates, and ball-joint spacers or torsion-bar adjustment lift the front. Total Chaos makes long-travel IFS kits for 1986–95 trucks if you want more.

t: Should I do a solid-axle swap?
x: Only if you need it. IH8MUD members describe the 1986–95 Toyota IFS as 'pretty stout' unless you rock-crawl hard; those who break IFS shafts tend to go solid axle. Long-travel IFS and SAS conversions can cost similar money.

t: Can I get a diesel one?
x: Not from a US dealer — US trucks were 22R-E or 3VZ-E only. Japan's Hilux Surf offered the 2L-TE, 3L and 1KZ-TE diesels, and every 2nd gen is now old enough for the US 25-year import exemption.
By modern standards, not very. Wikipedia lists a one-to-two-star frontal crash rating for the driver; side-impact door beams were only added for the 1994 and 1995 model years.

t: Spare-tire crossmember and frame rust repair
x: Flaking scale where crossmembers meet the frame, holes behind the rear axle, a spare carrier that won't release or sags. Welder · angle grinder · Rust Buster crossmember · rust paint · inhibitor spray

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: The Toyota-4Runner.org consensus is 265/75R16 (roughly a 31.6-inch tire) on stock suspension. Some owners see rubbing at full compression off-road with wide, aggressive tread or wheel spacers; if you want zero drama, 265/70R16 or 265/70R17 are the conservative picks. Anything bigger is lift territory.

t: Does my 4Runner have the factory rear locker?
x: Only if it's a 1996–2000 4WD truck that was ordered with it — it was an option on Base, SR5 and Limited 4WD models, never standard, and it wasn't common. For 2001–02 the rear E-locker was dropped in favour of VSC, traction control and a centre diff lock.

t: How should I use the E-locker?
x: The owner's manual guidance quoted on the forums is to engage it only in 4Lo and keep speed below about 5 mph. It locks both rear wheels together, so it'll fight you in turns on high-traction surfaces — use it for the obstacle, then switch it off.

t: When does the timing belt need doing — and is the 3.4 an interference engine?
x: Plan on about every 90,000 miles, and do the water pump, thermostat and seals while you're in there. The 5VZ-FE is non-interference, so a broken belt shouldn't destroy valves, but it will leave you stranded.
Up to 5,000 lb when properly equipped — a big jump from the 3,500 lb of the previous generation. Owners on Expedition Portal report fuel economy dropping to roughly 11–13 mpg when towing.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: EPA ratings were around 17 city / 19 highway for the 1996 V6 and 16/19 for a 2002 SR5 4x4; owners typically report 16–18 mpg. The 18.5-gallon tank and a notoriously inaccurate fuel gauge mean range is modest, so carry a jerry can on long trips.

Per Toyota-Club's US-spec 180-series data: 5VZ-FE oil with filter 5.2 L (3RZ-FE 5.4 L); front diff 1.15 L of GL-5 80W-90; rear diff 2.45 L (2.75 L with diff lock) of GL-5 80W-90; transfer case 1.0–1.2 L of 75W-90; automatic transmission drain-and-fill about 2.0 L (4WD) of Dexron II/III.

t: Which years should I buy or avoid?
x: Forum favourites are 1999–2000 trucks, especially Limiteds or SR5s with the Multi-Mode case and E-locker. 1996–98 trucks are simpler and cheaper to fix. 2001–02 get VSC and traction control but lose the locker and manual, and some owners prefer the simpler earlier drivetrain. Condition and rust matter far more than model year.

Most owners steer you toward the 3.4 V6: 183 hp and 217 lb-ft versus 150 hp and 177 lb-ft for the 2.7 four, for similar running costs. The four is a durable engine, but it'll struggle with big tires and a loaded roof rack.

The classic is an Old Man Emu kit of about 2–3 in, with ICON, Total Chaos and others offering springs, coilovers and control arms. As a lift grows, aftermarket upper control arms help restore alignment range; Total Chaos makes both UCAs and a bolt-on lower ball joint conversion for this truck.

t: How long will a 3rd gen last?
x: With maintenance, a long time. SlashGear notes it consistently ranked among the SUVs most likely to pass 250,000 miles, and 8020 Automotive puts a well-maintained 5VZ-FE at 300,000–400,000 miles. Frame rust and neglected ball joints usually kill these trucks before the engine does.

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: 265/70R17 (about 31.6 in) is the size the GX 470 community — same chassis and fitment — says fits with no modification, and owners on both platforms report no rubbing on factory wheels. 255/75R17 may need a front fender-liner bolt repositioned. 285/70R17 (about 33 in) needs a body-mount chop and fender-liner work even with a small lift.

The V8 is the reason many buy a 4th gen: about 270 hp and 315 lb-ft from 2005, full-time 4WD and up to 7,000 lb of 4WD towing. The V6 has a timing chain instead of a belt, part-time Multi-Mode 4WD and better EPA numbers (17/20 vs 15/19). The V8's air-injection pump and exhaust manifolds are its known expensive faults.
All 4WD trucks have a lockable Torsen centre differential. A factory rear locker only came on the 2009 Trail Edition, along with an A-TRAC switch and Bilstein dampers.

t: What is X-REAS, and should I keep it?
x: It links diagonally opposite shocks through hydraulic lines and a centre valve to reduce body roll. It was standard on the Sport Edition and optional on SR5 and Limited. It works, but the shocks are costly and replaced in pairs, so many owners swap to conventional shocks such as Bilstein 5100s when they wear out.
5,000 lb with the V6; 7,300 lb with a rear-drive V8 and 7,000 lb with a 4WD V8.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: Wikipedia lists EPA estimates of 17 city / 20 highway for the V6 and 15/19 for the V8. A 4Runners.com owner reported 17–18 mpg combined and 18–19 on the highway from a stock 2003 V8 4WD over 12 years, less when towing.

t: What fluids do the diffs and transfer case take?
x: GL-5 hypoid gear oil: 75W-90 in the front diff and transfer case and 80W-90 in the rear, per Toyota-Club's owner's-manual data (front 1.5 L V6 / 1.4 L V8, transfer case 1.4 L, rear 3.05 L). A 4Runners.com write-up gives roughly 1.5 qt, 1.5 qt and 3.2 qt; fill each until it drips from the fill hole.

t: Why are my VSC and TRAC lights on?
x: Often nothing is broken: after a battery disconnect, alignment or sensor work the system can need a zero-point calibration, done on level ground with a paper clip across the diagnostic connector. If the lights stay on, scan for codes.
Not a safety recall. Toyota's ZE6 warranty enhancement covered cracked or sticky dashboards on 2003–2005 4Runners, but coverage was time-limited and has expired. A dash cover is the usual fix now.

t: Which years should I look for?
x: 2005-on trucks get the five-speed automatic on the V6 and the VVT-i V8; 2006-on have the refreshed styling and projector headlamps; 2008–09 add standard curtain airbags; and 2009 offers the Trail Edition with a rear locker. Condition, rust and maintenance history matter more than any model year.

t: Does it have a third row?
x: It can. A third-row seat became optional on SR5 and Limited from late 2003 (the 2004 model year), making the 4th gen the first 4Runner offered with seven seats.

t: Suspension — Bilstein 5100 set for X-REAS trucks (ShockWarehouse), Total Chaos 2003–2009 4Runner upper control arms, ReadyLIFT SST 3 in lift (via LC Engineering)
x: Conventional shocks replace tired X-REAS, and aftermarket upper control arms restore alignment range once you lift.

t: Rear Air Delete — Metal Tech 4x4 rear coil conversion kit
x: Swap failing height-control air springs for coils and forget about it.

t: Tire Clearance — Metal Tech 4x4 2003–2009 4Runner body mount chop kit
x: A body-mount chop is what lets 285/70R17s (33s) live on a 4th gen.

t: Armor — Coastal Offroad 2003–2023 4Runner kickout rock sliders, Coastal Offroad 4th gen high-clearance front bumper, Coastal Offroad 4th gen / GX 470 skid plate kit
x: Rock sliders and skids protect the rockers and the low-hanging V8 bits; a steel bumper adds a winch mount.

t: Roof Rack — ARB roof rack, 2003–2023 4Runner (via LC Engineering)
x: A flat rack for a tent, recovery boards and a spare that won't fit underneath with bigger tyres.

t: Drivetrain — LC Engineering dual-axle diff breather relocation kit
x: Raised diff breathers are cheap insurance before water crossings.

There's no dipstick on later trucks — level is checked at a set fluid temperature, so owners use a scan tool to read ATF temp.
GL-5 75W-90 · 1.4 L 24 mm drain/fill plugs; break the fill plug loose first. Fill until it drips from the fill hole.
GL-5 75W-90 · 1.5 L (V6) / 1.4 L (V8) 10 mm hex plugs behind the 12 mm-bolted skid plates; new washer 90430-24003 on the drain.
GL-5 80W-90 · 3.05 L Toyota-Club lists 80W-90 for the rear (some owners run 75W-90 throughout). 2009 Trail Editions have the factory rear E-locker — cycle it in 4Lo after the service.
ATF Dexron II/III While you're there, check the inner rack boots for fluid — a TacomaWorld-flagged 4th gen weak point.
Type [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Listen for the ABS accumulator pump cycling constantly — a sign the brake actuator is failing.

t: Timing belt & water pump (2UZ-FE V8 only)
x: Belt, tensioner pulley, idler, hydraulic adjuster, water pump The 1GR-FE V6 uses a timing chain and needs no belt service.
Inspect for leaks and sag Leaking X-REAS shocks are replaced in pairs; many owners convert to conventional shocks and coils instead.

t: CV boots, sway-bar bushings & front hubs
x: Inspect TacomaWorld members flag leaking CV boots past ≈100,000 mi and clunking front sway-bar bushings; replace the knuckle dust seal if you do a hub.

N280 1GR-FE Fifteen model years on the J150 Prado/GX/FJ Cruiser platform with the 4.0 V6 — TRD Pro from 2015. Fifteen model years with the same V6, the same five-speed and roughly the same dashboard — and it sold better at the end than at the start. The most successful act of automotive stubbornness of the century.

Due on mileage or unknown history; dark or burnt-smelling fluid. There is no dipstick — the level is set at temperature through a check plug. 10/12/14 mm and 24 mm sockets · 5 mm Allen · fluid pump · jumper wire · torque wrenches · Toyota ATF WS 00289-ATFWS · filter 35330-60050 · filter O-ring 90301-31014 · pan gasket 35168-60010 · plug gaskets (Trail4R and readers cite 35178-30010 for drain/check

t: Front and rear differential + transfer case fluids
x: Due at 15,000 miles under severe service (towing, roof loads) per Toyota, or at whatever interval you set — Trail4R's author does all driveline fluids every 30,000. 10 mm hex bit · 24 mm socket · fluid pump · torque wrench · Toyota LT 75W-85 GL-5 · Toyota LF 75W transfer oil · washers: transfer case 90430-A0003, front drain 90430-24003, front fill 12157-10010

Gear oil weeping where the CV axle enters the front differential; a puddle under the front of the truck. 19/21/35 mm sockets · breaker bar · seal puller · ball-joint separator · CV axle removal tool · seals: left 90311-47027; right 90311-47026 (2014+) or 90311-47013 (2010–13)

Grease flung around the wheel well, a split boot, clicking on turns once dirt gets in. Lifted trucks with excessive droop tear boots on the lower control arm. OEM CV boot kit 04427-60131 · optional dust cover 41336-35020 and axle nut 90178-28002 · 19/35 mm sockets · impact or breaker bar · CV clamp pliers · retaining-ring pliers · torque wrench (50–250 ft-lb)

After a lift: out-of-spec caster/camber, upper ball joint at its angle limit, or you're installing coilovers anyway. 10/12/14/19 mm sockets · torque wrench to 100 ft-lb · grease gun · jack stands · e.g. Total Chaos 2010–2024 4Runner UCAs

Steering-wheel shake under braking (warped rotors — Trail4R blamed cold water crossings), noise, thin pads. 12/17/19 mm sockets · piston compressor or clamp · mallet · brake grease · torque wrench · e.g. Powerstop kit (fits 2013+ per Trail4R)

t: Rear hatch window won't close (re-initialise and clean)
x: The rear glass bounces back down as if it found an obstruction, or stays down. Common after a battery disconnect or an obstruction event. Compressed air · rubber cleaner · rags · flat screwdriver

Due every 5,000 miles on dirt or dusty roads, or when towing/heavily loaded, per Toyota's schedule as quoted by Trail4R. Dry joints may pop when greased. Grease gun (a locking coupler helps) · NLGI No. 2 lithium chassis grease · shop towels · wheel chocks

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: Trail4R's short answer is 32 inches. Stock is 265/70R17 (31.6 in). A 275/70R17 or 255/75R17 (about 32.1 in) shouldn't rub; a 285/70R17 (32.7 in) is 'questionable' and may need a body-mount chop; 255/80R17 (33 in) and anything bigger needs a lift and trimming. Tire brand and wheel offset change the outcome.

t: Which trims have the rear locker?
x: The Trail (2010–2016) and its renamed successor, the TRD Off-Road (2017–2024), which pair the electric rear locker with Crawl Control and Multi-Terrain Select. SR5 and Limited owners who want one retrofit an aftermarket unit — Trail4R documents an Eaton E-Locker install in an SR5.

If you'll stay stock or near-stock, yes: owners praise the reduced body roll and slightly better articulation. If you plan a big lift or long travel, it's a complication — Trail4R puts the practical lift limit at about 3 inches and lists bracket, sway-bar and panhard fixes for lifted KDSS trucks. Leaking KDSS cylinders are an expensive repair.

SR5, Trail and TRD Off-Road 4x4s use a part-time two-speed transfer case with no centre differential, so 4H locks the front and rear driveshafts together. The Limited used full-time 4WD. All trucks have A-TRAC.
5,000 lb, per Car and Driver. The 6th gen raised that to 6,000.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: EPA-rated 16 city / 19 highway (17 combined) in later years. Car and Driver's 2022 TRD Pro averaged 15 mpg overall and 17 mpg on its 75-mph highway test, good for about 390 miles of highway range.

t: Does the 4.0 V6 have a timing belt?
x: No — the 1GR-FE uses a timing chain with no scheduled replacement interval, meant to last the life of the engine. The serpentine belt is the wear item: Toyota calls for inspection at 63,000 miles and every 18,000 thereafter.

Per Toyota-Club's N280 data: engine oil with filter 6.2 L (Trail4R refills with about 6.6 qt of 0W-20); ATF WS 10.7 L total; front diff 1.55 L (part-time) / 1.40 L (full-time); rear diff 2.70 L without locker / 2.65 L with; transfer case 1.00 L (part-time) / 1.40 L (full-time); coolant 10.5 L. Diff oil is Toyota LT 75W-85 GL-5.

t: Which years should I buy or avoid?
x: There's no bad engine year, so buy on condition. 2014+ gets the facelift and upgraded brake lines; 2020+ adds TSS-P safety tech and CarPlay. SlashGear singles out 2013–2016 for higher complaint and recall counts. Whatever the year, confirm the Takata airbag (2010–2016) and fuel pump (2018–2019) recalls are closed.

Trail4R's shortlist runs from Old Man Emu (2.5–3 in) and Bilstein 6112/5160 to Eibach, Falcon, OME BP-51, Dobinsons MRR, ICON, Fox and King. Beyond about 2.5–3 in, plan on aftermarket upper control arms and, on KDSS trucks, sway-bar and panhard corrections.

t: Why does my truck lean to the driver's side?
x: Toyota puts heavy items — battery, driveshafts, transfer case, fuel tank — on the driver's side, leaving that side typically ¼ to ¾ in lower. Trail4R fixed it with a thicker top spacer on the driver's-side coilover than on the passenger side.

t: Suspension Lift — Old Man Emu kit (via Mudify), Bilstein lift kits (via Mudify), Dobinsons lift kits (via Mudify)
x: A 2–3 in lift with quality shocks makes room for 33s and fixes the stock nose-down rake.

t: Upper Control Arms — Total Chaos Fabrication, JBA Offroad
x: Restore alignment range and ball-joint angle once the front is lifted.

t: Kdss Geometry — Dr. KDSS rear drop kit (4RunnerMods), Dr. KDSS BOTCK track-bar kit (4RunnerMods), Sonoran Steel KDSS panhard bar
x: Lifted KDSS trucks need the sway bars and panhard bar brought back into line.

t: Rear Locker (Sr5 / Limited) — Eaton E-Locker (via SDHQ)
x: A-TRAC gets you far; a locker gets you up the ledge without drama.

t: Armor — C4 Fabrication lo-pro bumpers, ARB Summit bumper (via 4Runner Lifestyle), C4 Fabrication full skid plate (via 4Runner Lifestyle)
x: Sliders, skids and a winch bumper protect the rockers, oil pan and transfer case.

t: Mid / Long Travel — Total Chaos mid/long travel, Dirt King Fabrication
x: For desert running, wider arms and bigger shocks — and goodbye to KDSS.

t: Roof Rack — Cali Raised premium roof rack (via 4Runner Lifestyle)
x: Recovery boards, a tent or a spare fuel can need somewhere to live.

Don't over-tighten; use genuine housings.

Toyota Super Long Life Coolant (pink, pre-mixed) · 10.5 L (Toyota-Club) Pre-mixed — don't dilute.

Toyota ATF WS · 10.7 L total; a drain and fill swaps ≈5 qt No dipstick: the level is set through the 5 mm Allen check plug at 104–113 °F in maintenance mode (see the repair card). A filter-and-pan job is a good baseline on a truck with no records.

Toyota Differential Gear Oil LT 75W-85 GL-5 · front ≈1.6 qt (part-time) / 1.5 qt (full-time) · rear ≈2.9 qt (locker) / 2.8 qt (no locker) Fill plug first. Front uses 10 mm hex plugs (48/29 ft-lb); rear 24 mm (36 ft-lb).
ATF Dexron II/III (Toyota-Club) Hydraulic rack on the 5th gen.
DOT 3 Rear bleeds use the ABS pump with the ignition on and the pedal weighted — don't run it more than 100 seconds at a time. Bleeders 8 ft-lb.

Toyota 90916-A2015 Spin the idler and tensioner pulleys by hand while the belt is off. The 1GR-FE uses a timing chain with no service interval.
Threads into the driver-side rear of the engine · 19 mm deep socket · Threebond 1324 · 20 ft-lb If the ball inside doesn't rattle, it's stuck.
Group 34 fits (Trail4R used an Odyssey) Switch any accessory that doesn't need constant power to avoid parasitic drain.

N500 i-FORCE i-FORCE MAX Moves to the TNGA-F (GA-F) frame shared with the Tacoma; turbo 2.4 four or the i-FORCE MAX hybrid, eight-speed auto. Toyota finally replaced the V6, the five-speed and the 2009 dashboard — and somehow kept the roll-down rear window and the attitude. Quicker, smarter and far nicer to live with; whether a turbo four and a hybrid will rack up 300,000 miles like the old truck

t: Front brake squeal fix (TSB pad and shim kit)
x: Squeal from the front brakes, typically when reversing and often worse cold. TSB T-SB-0046-25 applies to 2025 4Runner and 4Runner Hybrid (and 2024–25 Land Cruiser). Disc brake piston spreader (Toyota SST 09719-77020 / 09719-77050) · caliper grease · torque wrench · pad kit 04465-34040 · shim kit 04945-0C060 · fitting kit 04947-0C030

Due every 15,000 miles under severe use (towing, roof loads, heavy loading) per the maintenance chart; otherwise inspect. Many owners do an early break-in change. 10 mm hex bit · 24 mm socket · 12 mm socket · fluid pump · 6-qt drain pan · Toyota LT 75W-85 GL-5 (00279-DGOLT-01) · washers 12157-10010 (front fill, both rear) and 90430-24017 (front drain)

Due at the transfer-case interval in the maintenance chart for dusty roads or towing; first change is a common break-in item. 24 mm socket (per Tacoma/LC250 data; confirm on your truck) · fluid pump · torque wrench · Toyota LF 00279-DGOLF · washers 90430-A0003 ×2

Every 10,000 miles or 12 months normally; every 5,000 miles or 6 months when mostly on dirt or dusty roads, per the maintenance chart. Drain pan · filter wrench · torque wrench · new drain-plug washer · Toyota-spec synthetic oil

Weak HVAC airflow; on i-FORCE MAX trucks used on dusty roads, clogged hybrid battery intake filters that can let the pack run hot. Trim tool · cabin filter 87139-60030 (or carbon 87139-30110) · hybrid battery filters G92DH-34010 / G92DJ-34010
Part of dusty-road and towing maintenance. Owners count five zerks on a 4WD truck. Grease gun · lithium-base chassis grease · creeper
Water sloshing inside the liftgate or dripping from the inner panel with the gate open, after rain or a wash. Trim tool or small screwdriver

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: TRD Off-Road, TRD Pro and Trailhunter trucks already run 33-inch tires (265/70R18) from the factory. SR5 owners on 4Runner6G.com report 285/70R17 (about 33 in) on stock height without rubbing, though they argue about whether the stock 17×7 wheel is too narrow for that tire; one owner saw the tread balloon and moved to 8.5-in-wide wheels.

It's the only choice on the TRD Pro, Trailhunter and Platinum. Elsewhere, Car and Driver says the extra cost isn't worth it: the gas truck is lighter, keeps the optional third row and is rated 21–22 mpg combined against the hybrid's 23. The hybrid's real gain is torque — 465 lb-ft against 317.

t: Which trims have a locker and the sway-bar disconnect?
x: The electronic rear locker comes on the TRD Off-Road, TRD Pro and Trailhunter; other trims get a limited-slip rear differential. The disconnecting front anti-roll bar is standard on the TRD Pro and Trailhunter and optional on the TRD Off-Road.
No. Car and Driver confirms KDSS is gone, replaced by the electronic front bar disconnect, and Wikipedia notes that from 2025 KDSS is exclusive to Lexus.
6,000 lb, hybrid or not — 1,000 lb more than the 5th gen.

t: What fuel economy and range should I expect?
x: EPA: up to 20 city / 26 highway / 22 combined for the gas truck (21 combined in 4WD), 23 combined for the hybrid. Car and Driver's 4WD Limited returned 21 mpg on its 75-mph highway test; its Trailhunter averaged 17 mpg. Owners complain about range, with one reporting about 280 miles between fill-ups.

t: Is the transmission overheating issue real?
x: Car and Driver saw the eight-speed's temperatures approach the red zone after repeated acceleration runs, and some owners report warnings on long, slow off-road climbs. Owners' advice: use 4Lo at low speeds or hold a lower gear in S mode, and report it to Toyota if it happens.

t: What are the oil change and fluid intervals?
x: Oil and filter every 10,000 miles or 12 months, or 5,000 miles / 6 months if mostly on dirt or dusty roads; differential oil at 15,000-mile intervals under severe use. Owners cite 5.9 qt of engine oil, about 1.4 qt front and 5.9 qt rear diff oil (6.9 qt on the Trailhunter), and 1.2–1.5 qt in the transfer case.

t: Can I get a third row?
x: Only on the SR5 and non-hybrid Limited, and Car and Driver describes the rearmost seats as little more than floor-mounted jump seats. The hybrid's battery lives under the cargo floor, so no hybrid gets a third row.

t: What lift options are there yet?
x: The aftermarket moved quickly: leveling and lift kits from ReadyLift and TORQ, Total Chaos kits with King shocks, Dirt King coilovers, plus upper control arms from Total Chaos, Peak and Westcott. Forum members are still waiting for news of an OEM TRD lift.

t: Did it keep the roll-down rear window?
x: Yes. Motor1 reported the engineers almost lost it, and only kept it by trimming weight from each part of the mechanism.

t: Suspension Lift — ReadyLift 2.5 in SST kit (via 4Runner Lifestyle), TORQ TRD Pro 2 in kit (via 4Runner Lifestyle), Dirt King 2.5 coilovers (via 4Runner Lifestyle)
x: Level the rake or add a couple of inches for bigger rubber; TRD Pro/Trailhunter owners can go further with coilovers.

t: Upper Control Arms — Total Chaos 6th gen UCAs, Peak Suspension tubular UCAs (via 4Runner Lifestyle)
x: Restore caster and ball-joint angle once the front is lifted.

t: Rear Geometry — Dr. KDSS BOTCK track-bar kit (via 4Runner Lifestyle), Durobumps rear bump stops (via 4Runner Lifestyle)
x: A lifted live axle shifts sideways on its track bar; bump stops keep big tires out of the wheel wells.

t: Armor — C4 Fabrication lo-pro winch bumper (via 4Runner Lifestyle), CBI rock sliders (via 4Runner Lifestyle), C4 Fabrication rock slider steps (via 4Runner Lifestyle)
x: Non-Trailhunter trims need sliders and a proper bumper before the rocks find the rockers.

t: Roof Rack — Prinsu Pro roof rack (via 4Runner Lifestyle), Sherpa Capitol roof rack (via 4Runner Lifestyle)
x: Only the Trailhunter gets the ARB rack from the factory.

t: Turbo Engine Care — SXTH Element TrailShield filter cover (via 4Runner Lifestyle), SXTH Element catch can kit (via 4Runner Lifestyle)
x: Dusty trails and a direct-injected turbo four: keep the intake clean and the crankcase vapour out.

The Geländewagen began as a military truck, commissioned in the early 1970s after the Shah of Iran — then one of Mercedes-Benz’s largest shareholders — pre-ordered some 20,000 of them. Mercedes engineered it; Steyr-Daimler-Puch built it in Graz, Austria, and production began in 1979. The utilitarian W460 and later W461 served armies, border police and farmers. In 1990 the civilian W463 moved upmar

W460 230 GE 280 GE 300 GD The original military-derived G, in short and long wheelbase, petrol and diesel. The original Geländewagen: built for a Shah, bought by armies, blessed by a Pope and slower up a motorway on-ramp than most tractors. It is the purest G there is, and it will happily outlive you if you keep the rust and the hydraulics in check.

t: Front axle rebuild (bearings, kingpins, swivel seals, CVs)
x: Oil or grease weeping from the steering ball (the big swivel housing behind the hub), play at the wheel, clicking on full lock, torn CV boots. t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: About a 32-inch 235/85R16 on the stock steel wheels. An Expedition Portal owner runs 235/85R16s on standard steel wheels on a short-wheelbase G. The original fitment was a skinny 205 R16, and many owners stay close to 215/85R16 because a naturally aspirated diesel struggles to turn a bigger tire up hills. For 33s and up, plan on lift springs.

t: Is the W460 full-time four-wheel drive?
x: No. It's part-time: you engage the front axle by lever through the transfer case, with high and low range. Permanent 4WD arrived with the 1989–90 W463. Don't drive a W460 in 4WD on dry pavement.

t: Do all W460s have locking differentials?
x: Not all of them. Mercedes made front and rear locks standard on every W460 from 1985, so earlier trucks may not have them. Look for the locker control on the dash and the slave cylinders on the axles. A W460 never had the W463's third (centre) lock.

The 300 GD was the most popular W460 and the 280 GE the most powerful. Auto Bild names the 230 GE and the 300 GD, with their long-lived manual gearboxes, as the ones to have. The OM617 five-cylinder in the 300 GD has a reputation for reaching huge mileages, but it's slow and was never turbocharged in a W460.

Not very. Factory figures for a 300 GD are 88 PS, 0–100 km/h in about 27 seconds and a 127 km/h (79 mph) top speed. An IH8MUD owner says his mildly modified OM617 ran out of power around 70 mph. A 280 GE is good for about 165 km/h.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: Mercedes' cycle figures for the 300 GD run from 11.7 to 18.8 L/100 km, roughly 12.5–20 mpg US. The 280 GE is thirstier, at 14.0–22.4 L/100 km (about 10.5–17 mpg). Big tires, a roof rack and a lift make both worse.

t: Was the W460 sold in the US?
x: Not by Mercedes. Grey-market specialists federalised some in the 1980s until the 1988 Imported Vehicle Safety Compliance Act made it much harder. Official US sales didn't begin until the 2002 model year, and before that Europa International imported later W463s.

t: W460, W461 or W463 — what's the difference?
x: The W460 (1979–1991) is the original, with part-time 4WD and two lockers. The W461 kept the W460's body and chassis but used W463 running gear, and was built for armies, authorities and NGOs. The W463 is the civilian luxury G from 1990, with permanent 4WD, three lockers, ABS and wood trim.

In the US they're scarce and expensive, according to IH8MUD owners. In Europe, Auto Bild says Mercedes dealers still stock most parts at high prices and used parts are plentiful. Specialists such as Expedition Imports stock W460 axle, locker, steering and cooling parts, and some components are shared with Mercedes cars and vans.

Classic & Sports Car's 2023 guide put a pre-1990 hardtop at £5,000 as a project, £14,000 average and £27,000+ for a show truck. Soft-tops run £12,000 / £30,000 / £75,000+. For a US example, a rusty, re-engined 1986 300 GD project sold for $13,000 on PCARMARKET in January 2022.

t: Can I use the diff locks on pavement?
x: No. A locked diff stops the wheels turning at different speeds, so on grippy surfaces the driveline binds and the tires scrub. Lock on dirt, sand, snow or rock at low speed, and unlock before you're back on tarmac.

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: The G 300 CDI Professional comes on 265/75R16s, about 31.6 inches. On narrow-body Gs, an Expedition Portal owner runs 235/85R16s (about 32 inches) on the standard steel wheels, which is a sensible no-lift ceiling. Beyond that you're into lift springs: GwagenParts' ROGUE spring listing talks about 33- and 35-inch tires, and warns that bigger tires can trigger ABS and ESP warnings.

t: What's the difference between a W461 and a W463?
x: The W461 uses the W460's narrow body and chassis with W463 running gear, plain trim, and barn doors and panel-van bodies you can't get on a W463. Military trucks also have 24-volt electrics. The W463 is the luxury civilian G with wood, leather and more electronics.

t: Is the 250 GD 'Wolf' a W460 or a W461?
x: Expedition Motor Company, which restores them, calls the 250 GD Wolf an ex-military W461, and Wikipedia lists the 1990–91 Wolf in the W461 table. The line between late military W460s and early W461s is blurry, so check the VIN and data card on the truck in front of you.

t: Could civilians buy a new W461?
x: Yes, in limited form. Mercedes sold the G 280 CDI EDITION.30 PUR in 2009, followed by the G 280 CDI Professional (2009) and the G 300 CDI Professional (2010–2019). In Australia the G 300 CDI Professional cab-chassis launched in 2016 at A$119,900, and the wagon followed in 2017 at A$109,900.

t: How much can it carry and tow?
x: 4X4 Australia's figures for the G 300 CDI Professional cab-chassis: 2,410 kg kerb weight, 4,490 kg GVM, about 2,080 kg payload and 2,210 kg towing capacity, with a 6,700 kg GCM.

Yes. The G 300 CDI Professional has permanent all-wheel drive with a 50:50 split, a two-speed transfer case and three locking diffs selectable on the move. Unusually, you can unlock the centre diff even in low range.

t: Does it really run on 24 volts?
x: Military W461s do. Wikipedia lists the 24-volt system as one of the W461's defining features, and parts suppliers stock 24 V components such as blower motors. The Australian civilian Professional wagon is described as carrying two 12-volt batteries. Check what your truck actually has before wiring in accessories.

t: Which engine should I look for?
x: For highway use, the 1998–2001 290 GD Turbodiesel or later: the G 270 CDI (156 PS, 400 Nm) and the OM642 V6 in the G 280/300 CDI (184 PS, 400 Nm). The naturally aspirated 290 GD (95 PS) and the 250 GD Wolf are charming and simple but very slow.

t: How big is the fuel tank?
x: 96–97 litres on the G 300 CDI Professional, depending on whether you read WhichCar or 4X4 Australia.

t: Why does the late W461 have a bonnet bulge?
x: It clears an air pump that's part of the emissions equipment, according to 4X4 Australia. The W460 doesn't have one.
No. Civilian production ended in 2019, and military production continued until 2022, when the W464 took over. Mercedes announced the W464 on 1 October 2021.

W463 The civilian G: full-time 4WD, three lockers, ever-more luxury — and still solid axles. Twenty-eight years and engines from four to twelve cylinders, all on the same ladder frame and two solid axles. It became a rapper's accessory and stayed a real off-roader the whole time. Buy one for the three lockers and keep a budget for the vacuum lines.

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: About 33 inches. A 275/70R18 on the factory 18s fits an unlifted G 500/G 550, according to Expedition Portal owners. JWO designed its 4-inch springs specifically to clear tires bigger than 33 inches without rubbing. Some owners squeeze in more, such as one G 500 on 315/75R16s with no lift, and offset ET63 wheels help, but 35s on stock springs will usually rub somewhere at full compression or lock.

t: Which W463 engine is the most reliable?
x: Handsome Motors ranks it G 500 → G 55 → G 550 → G 63 for mechanical reliability, and calls the 2002–2015 V8s the safest bets. In Europe, Autocar names the G 320 CDI diesel V6 the best all-rounder. Avoid neglected G 63s unless you've budgeted for big brakes and cooling-system work.
2.16:1 through the two-speed transfer case.

t: How do the three lockers work, and in what order?
x: You press the dash buttons and a controller engages them in sequence: centre first, then rear, then front. Each one locks after the truck has rolled a short distance. Vacuum operates the centre lock and the valves; hydraulics move the front and rear locks. Unlock everything before you're back on pavement.

t: Was the W463 sold in the US before 2002?
x: Yes, but not by Mercedes. Europa International of New Mexico federalised and sold them from 1993, and became the exclusive US importer of the G 500 with small-volume-manufacturer status. Those trucks have US VINs. Mercedes took over with the 2002 model year.

t: When did the manual gearbox disappear?
x: In 1994, when the 200, 230 and 300 GE were dropped. From 1996 the automatic was an electronically controlled five-speed. The seven-speed came in for 2007 on the US G 500.

t: Which years have ESP and traction control?
x: ESP, Brake Assist and the four-wheel electronic traction system (4ETS) arrived with the 2001–02 update that coincided with the official US launch. Earlier W463s have ABS but rely on the lockers alone for traction.

t: How often should I service the automatic?
x: Toolsource cites a 40–60k-mile interval for the five-speed 722.6, using MB 236.14 ATF. Handsome Motors suggests every 40–50k miles for the seven-speed. If the history is unknown, do it now.

t: Are the 2016–2018 G 550s with the twin-turbo V8 a good buy?
x: Handsome Motors says yes. The M176 is a lower-stressed relative of AMG's M177, and by those years the early electrical gremlins were gone. Watch for a failed crankcase-vent oil separator causing rear-main-seal and valve-cover leaks. The same dealer personally recommends 3–5k-mile oil changes.
It's an enthusiast label for the 2018-on second-generation G, which kept the W463 chassis code. Mercedes doesn't use the term itself.

t: How do I spot a fake AMG?
x: Check the VIN and the factory data card. Bumpers, flares, wheels and badges are easy to bolt on, and Autocar specifically warns about Gs converted to look like AMGs.

t: Can I use the diff locks on pavement?
x: No. Locked diffs stop the wheels turning at different speeds, so on grippy surfaces the driveline binds and the tires scrub. Use them on dirt, sand, snow or rock at low speed.

t: How is it different from the later G 500?

t: Is a Europa G a gray-market truck?
x: No. Europa certified the trucks to US emissions and safety standards, including crash testing, sold them with US VINs, and gained Small Volume Manufacturer status, making them 50-state legal. Gray-market Gs were private imports cleared one at a time.

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: About 33 inches. An Expedition Portal owner runs 275/70R18 on an unlifted 2000 G 500 and only rubbed on aftermarket ET63 wheels. Another runs 285/65R18 with a slight rub at full left lock. Another owner says up to about 32 inches should clear with no rubbing. Have the tire size re-coded with Mercedes diagnostics so the speedometer and ESP stay accurate.

t: Which Europa G should I buy?
x: Forum regulars usually prefer the G 500 for its much greater power at similar mileage. German Cars For Sale Blog prefers the 300 GE or G 500 to the inline-six G 320 because of its head-gasket issue. One owner found the V6 G 320 more economical than a G 500, though the gap narrows when towing.

t: Do Europa trucks have all three lockers?
x: Yes. Scott Brady's 1996 Europa truck had dash buttons for the centre, rear and front locks, plus ABS and airbags.

t: How is a Europa G 500 different from a 2002 Mercedes-Benz USA G 500?
x: It looks nearly the same outside, apart from black-painted bumpers. Inside it has a pre-facelift W210 E-Class steering wheel and cluster, no wheel-mounted radio controls, older climate control, and a 722.6 automatic without the tip-shift gate. It also avoids the COMAND electronics that German Cars For Sale Blog blames for early MBUSA trucks' electrical problems.

t: How much did they cost new?
x: Hagerty says some sold for up to $135,000. The 1999 Neiman Marcus Christmas-catalogue G 500 was $160,000, and six were sold.

Usually about the same as 2002-on trucks. Recent asks include a 202,750-mile 2000 G 500 at $32,000 (Jalopnik) and a well-documented 1998 G 320 at $47,500 (German Cars For Sale Blog), which the blog called high but understandable. Clean Europa G 320s come up only every few years and tend to sell quickly.
We couldn't find a reliable total. The rarest variant is better documented: fewer than ten short-wheelbase Cabriolets were certified as US models, according to Ferraris Online.

t: How often should the front axle be serviced?

t: Can I use the diff locks on pavement?

W463 Portal axles Portal axles, enormous ground clearance and absolutely no subtlety. A G-Class on stilts: portal axles, two springs per corner and 22-inch wheels. Utterly unsubtle — but the 17 inches of ground clearance are entirely real.

t: What’s the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: It doesn’t need one — the portal axles are the lift. Stock tires are 325/55R22, about 36 inches tall. When Mercedes showed the truck, it said 37×12.5×18 mud-terrains would be available for production trucks, and the Geneva show car wore 37-inch mud-terrains on beadlocks. Check caliper clearance before going to 18-inch wheels, and re-code the tire size.

t: Was the 4×4² sold in the US?
x: Yes, for the 2017 model year, as the G 550 4×4². Mercedes-Benz USA listed it at $225,000 plus a $925 destination charge, with deliveries from early 2017.

t: How much ground clearance and wading depth?
x: 17.24 inches at maximum load and 39.4 inches of fording depth in US spec — up 7.9 and 15.8 inches respectively over a 2016 G 550. European figures are 450 mm and 1,000 mm.

t: What are its approach and departure angles?
x: 51.6° approach and 43.8° departure. Mercedes quoted breakover as 47.4° in its launch release and 44.6° at maximum load in the spec sheet.

t: Is it just a G 63 6×6 with an axle missing?
x: Partly. It uses a shortened version of the 6×6’s chassis and portal running gear, but with the five-door long-wheelbase body, the G 500/G 550’s 4.0-litre twin-turbo V8 and a seven-speed automatic.

t: What fuel economy does it get?
x: Mercedes-Benz USA’s spec sheet lists 11 mpg city, 11 highway and 11 combined. The fuel tank holds 25.4 gallons.

t: Will it fit in my garage?
x: Maybe not. It’s 88.0 inches tall, 86.2 inches wide including mirrors and 177.1 inches long, with a 46.9-foot turning circle.
6,694 lb curb weight — almost a thousand pounds more than a regular G 550.
Mercedes-Benz USA’s 2017 spec sheet listed towing as “TBA,” so check the owner’s manual and hitch rating for your specific truck rather than assuming the regular G 550’s figure.

t: Can I use the diff locks on pavement?
x: No. Locked diffs bind the driveline on grippy surfaces. Lock up on loose ground at low speed and unlock before tarmac.

t: How is it different from the newer G 63 4×4²?
x: The 2022-on G 63 4×4² is built on the second-generation G with independent front suspension, makes 585 hp and costs $350,050. It has less clearance (13.8 in) and wading depth (35.8 in) than the original, and weighs 379 lb less.

t: Does it still have three locking differentials?
x: Yes — centre, rear and front, 100% locks, on every gas model. The electric G 580 drops mechanical lockers in favor of per-wheel torque vectoring.

t: Is it still body-on-frame with a solid axle?
x: It’s still on a ladder frame — even the EV. The rear axle is rigid; the front is now independent double wishbones, the first time a G has had independent front suspension.
2.93:1, versus about 2.1:1 on the previous G. It engages at up to 25 mph with the transmission in neutral, and you can shift back to high range at up to 43 mph.

t: How much ground clearance and wading depth?
x: 9.5 inches between the axles (10.6 inches to the front axle), 27.6 inches of wading depth, and 31° / 30° / 26° approach, departure and breakover angles. The G 580 EV has 9.8 inches and wades 33.5 inches.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: The V8 G 550 is EPA-rated 14 mpg combined for 2019–2020; the mild-hybrid inline-six G 550 is rated 18 mpg combined for 2025–2026.

The 2019–2024 G 550’s 4.0-litre twin-turbo V8 makes 416 hp and 450 lb-ft; the 2025-on 3.0-litre mild-hybrid six makes 443 hp and 413 lb-ft and is rated about 4 mpg better combined. Same lockers, same clearance.

t: What can the electric G 580 do off-road?
x: Climb 100% grades on suitable surfaces, hold 35° side slopes, wade 33.5 inches, crawl in three settings, and turn on the spot with G-Turn. It has a 2:1 low range in each axle’s transmission.
It’s an enthusiast label for the 2018-on truck. Mercedes-Benz doesn’t use it officially.

t: Are there recalls I should know about?

t: Can I use the diff locks on pavement?
x: No. Locked diffs bind the driveline on high-grip surfaces. Use them on dirt, sand, snow or rock at low speed and unlock before tarmac.

When Land Rover ended classic Defender production at Solihull in January 2016 after 67 years, chemicals billionaire Sir Jim Ratcliffe tried to keep it alive. Jaguar Land Rover said no. So Ratcliffe did what billionaires do: he founded a car company, Ineos Automotive, and named its first product after his favourite pub, The Grenadier in Belgravia, where the idea was first kicked around. The result

B58 petrol B57 diesel (non-US) 2,922 mm WB The five-door, five-seat original: ladder frame, Carraro beam axles, BMW six, three lockable diffs available. US gets the petrol B58 only. The old Defender's spirit with a BMW heart and Italian tractor axles. Huge capability, real quirks, and steering that only got properly sorted for 2026.

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: From the factory the Grenadier rides on LT265/70R17 or LT255/70R18 (about 32 in.). INEOS Forum owners report 285/70R17 fits with no problem. 285/75R17 (about 34 in.) is the popular sweet spot: owners report no rub on stock suspension, but you'll probably need a couple of washers under the spare carrier to clear the small rear door. Owners have also run 295/70R17, 255/85R17 and 35x11.5R17 (the 35s

3,500 kg braked, about 7,700 lb (GearJunkie lists 7,716 lb). That's well above a Wrangler's 2,495 kg in Australian spec. Payload is about 1,680 lb in US figures, so a heavy trailer plus a fully loaded overland build will run into the GVWR before the hitch rating.

t: What fuel economy does it get?
x: Not much. The EPA rates the 2024 petrol Grenadier at 15 mpg city, highway and combined, and the Trialmaster at 14 mpg on premium fuel. The tank holds 90 litres (about 23.8 gal), which gives a range of roughly 350 miles in mixed use at the EPA figure, less with a roof tent and big tires.

t: How much weight can go on the roof?
x: 150 kg (330 lb) dynamic, meaning while driving, and 420 kg (925 lb) static, meaning parked. That's enough for a rooftop tent with people in it. Front Runner's Slimline II kit attaches to the grab-handle brackets with no drilling and weighs about 57 kg itself, so count it against the dynamic limit.

t: Can I get the diesel in the US?
x: No. In the US and Canada the Grenadier and Quartermaster come only with the BMW B58 3.0 petrol six, 282 hp and 332 lb-ft. The B57 diesel (245 hp, 406 lb-ft) is sold in Europe, Australia and other markets.

t: Does it have lockers, and how does the 4WD work?
x: It has permanent four-wheel drive through a Tremec two-speed transfer case (2.5:1 low), with a centre diff lock on a lever. Front and rear lockers come with the Rough Pack, which also adds BFG KO2 tires. It's standard on the Trialmaster and was a $2,850 option on base and Fieldmaster trucks at US launch. The locker switches are in the overhead panel.

t: What oil does the B58 take and how often should I change it?
x: An owner quoting the manual on the INEOS Forum lists 6.5 L of 0W-20 meeting ACEA C2 / BMW LL-17FE. Check your own manual, since the oil forums note the US manual is vague. One owner reports the manufacturer schedule as every 12,000 miles. Many owners do an early break-in change (500–1,000 miles on dealer advice) and then change it every 5,000–7,500 miles, especially if they tow.

t: Is the steering really that bad?
x: Before 2026, it's slow: a Bosch hydraulic recirculating-ball box with almost four turns lock to lock, which The Drive found wandered on the highway and was heavy when parked. Some owners like it off-road, and Owl sells a $2,150 pump kit and a Fox stabilizer. For MY2026 Ineos fitted a variable-ratio worm gear with more assist and a tighter on-center feel. GearJunkie called it 'a big leap forward'.

t: Which years should I buy or avoid?
x: There's no bad engine to avoid, since every US truck has the B58. The early US trucks (MY2024) carry all three recalls, so get proof they're closed. MY2026 brings the revised steering, HVAC and driver-assist tweaks plus more than 40 smaller changes. If you plan to drive a lot of highway miles, 2026 is the one to buy.

It's too new for a long-term verdict. The BMW six and ZF eight-speed are widely used and well proven elsewhere. Owner reports focus on electronics: modules, false warnings, software reflashes, sticky door buttons and water ingress, plus three US recalls. Most owners on the forums still sound happy, but a good dealer matters more than usual.

t: How capable is it off-road out of the box?
x: Very. It has 264 mm of ground clearance, 800 mm wading depth, and approach, breakover and departure angles of 35.5°, 28.2° and 36.1°, with solid axles and up to three locking diffs. GearJunkie noted there's no disconnecting sway bar, but the soft coils still articulate well.

Gives room for 285/75s and up, and restores ride height under bumpers, winches and roof tents. Eibach, the factory spring supplier, makes a Pro-Lift set (about +2.5 in. front, +1.2 in. rear). Watch driveshaft angles.

t: How much payload does it have?
x: It depends on market and engine. Ineos quoted 1,675 lb at US launch. In Australia it quotes 907 kg for the petrol and 832 kg for the diesel, against a 3,550 kg GVM. That's below most one-tonne utes and the 79 Series LandCruiser. Expedition Portal's optioned Trialmaster (winch, rack, dual batteries) had about 1,400 lb left.

t: Will a Euro pallet really fit?

It stands upright in the bed. Mounted underneath, it would cut into a departure angle that's already down to 22.6°. Ineos also offers a roof mount and a 15-litre lockable box that fits in the middle of the spare. Owners have moved it under the deck or under the rear axle.

x: No. US trucks have only the BMW B58 3.0 petrol six (282 hp, 332 lb-ft). The B57 diesel (183 kW, 550 Nm) is sold in Europe, Australia, New Zealand and other markets.

t: Why does it cost so much more than the wagon in the US?
x: Mostly the 25% chicken tax on imported light trucks. At launch the Quartermaster cost $15,400 more than the Station Wagon. When new tariffs arrived in April 2025, total duty rose to 50%. Ineos said it would absorb most of that, but still raised the price 11%, to $94,500 including shipping.

t: How does it drive compared with the wagon?
x: It's much the same, with a longer turning circle: about 14.5 m against 13.5 m before 2026. Unladen it can feel jittery over small bumps, and it settles with weight in the bed. Expedition Portal found it quieter and more comfortable than the wagon. Top Gear noted the light rear end can lose grip on slippery climbs, which is where the lockers and all-terrain tires help.

t: What fuel economy does it get?
x: Australian test-cycle figures are 12.6 L/100 km for the petrol and 10.5 L/100 km for the diesel. Edmunds lists 14 mpg combined for the US truck. Towing a caravan, Caravan World saw the high 20s in L/100 km from both engines. The tank holds 90 litres. Caravan World says about 10% of Australian Grenadier buyers fit a Brown Davis long-range tank, which adds 78 litres.

The engines haven't changed, so the main question is steering. MY2026 trucks have the variable-ratio box, about a 5% tighter turning circle, better HVAC and a quicker way to silence the speed-limit chime. Earlier trucks can be fitted with Owl's steering pump upgrade, which Owl says fits both the Grenadier and Quartermaster. Whichever year you buy, run the VIN for recalls.

t: What camper and canopy options exist?
x: Dirtbox Overland sells a canopy camper made for the Quartermaster bed for $11,499, and Norweld makes full-length, compact and half canopies plus trays. Leitner Designs makes a full-length roof rack (375 lb on-road, 200 lb off-road). INEOS Forum owners have fitted Dirtbox caps. Ineos's own accessory list includes a canvas tonneau, a roll-top cover and a hardtop.

t: Canopy & Camper — Dirtbox Overland — Quartermaster canopy camper, Norweld — Quartermaster canopies
x: The bed is a pallet-width box with an upright spare in it. Canopies and canopy campers turn it into secure storage and a bed off the ground. Watch payload.

t: Suspension & Load Support — Owl — Eibach Pro-Lift springs (Grenadier and Quartermaster), Dirtbox Overland — rear air-bag kit
x: Restores ride height under a canopy and gear, and makes room for 34–35 in. tires. The springs and air bags fit both Grenadier bodies.

t: Roof Rack — Leitner Designs — Quartermaster ACS full-length rack
x: Puts the tent, solar panels or the spare up top and leaves the bed free. The Quartermaster rack bolts to the roll cage, not the gutters.

t: Steering — Owl — steering pump upgrade (Grenadier and Quartermaster)
x: Pre-2026 trucks have the slow, non-self-centring box. Owl sells a $2,150 pump upgrade that it says works on both the Grenadier and the Quartermaster.
Outside the US, the cab-chassis plus an aluminium tray gives a flat, wider deck with drawers and water tanks. That's how the Kaiju was built.
