International Harvester had been building trucks since 1907, but in the late 1950s it set out to build a rival for the Jeep CJ. Chief designer Ted Ornas later recalled his brief from the engineering manager: 'design something to replace the horse.' The result, the Scout 80, went on sale in late 1960 as a 1961 model and was built in Fort Wayne, Indiana. The original Scout 80 and 800 grew from a fol

Scout 80 800 800A 800B The original Jeep fighter: four-cylinder Scout 80, then the more civilized 800 series with sixes and V8s. A tractor company was told to build something to replace the horse, and ten years later it was selling V8 wagons with bucket seats. Same 100-inch wheelbase, same honest steel box, and more rust than any seller will admit to.

Soft or holed floors under the mats, rockers bubbling at the bottom of the doors, and daylight around the fuel-tank compartment. Silodrome warns that rust usually starts inside and works out. MIG welder · cutoff wheel and spot-weld drill · clamps and self-tapping screws for fitting · seam sealer and weld-through primer.

t: Swap the vacuum wipers for an electric kit (800 series)
x: The original vacuum wipers on an 800 are dead, sluggish or simply not worth rebuilding. Basic hand tools · drill · wiring crimpers · test light.

t: Front knuckle seals and kingpin bearings (closed-knuckle Dana)
x: Grease weeping from the knuckle balls, torn wipers, and play in the knuckle when you rock the wheel top to bottom. One IHPA forum owner described his 1968 800 this way: "the wipers for the knuckles are shot and the king pin bearings are worn out." Floor jack and stands · hub/bearing nut socket · seal driver · torque wrench · inch-pound scale for preload · wheel-bearing grease.

t: Transfer case pops out of gear: Dana 20 rebuild
x: The transfer case jumps out of 2-High or won't fully engage 4-High. On a 1967 800, an IHPA forum member found the shift-cover opening was too small for the levers to travel fully, so check that before you strip the case. Transmission jack or a second floor jack · puller · snap-ring pliers · seal drivers · gasket scraper.

Four-wheel drums that fade, pull or simply don't stop a V8 Scout on modern roads. Die grinder · flare-nut wrenches · bearing packer · brake bleeder · tube flaring tool for 80s and single-circuit trucks.

t: Springs, shackles and bushings (fix the sag and the ride)
x: A tired stance, clunks from worn spring eyes and shackles, and the choppy ride of forward-shackle front springs. Jacks and stands · penetrating oil and heat for seized bolts · torque wrench · drill (and welder for a reverse-shackle kit).
Hard starting, a misfire that comes and goes, and points that keep closing up. Silodrome lists electronic ignition among the sensible upgrades. Timing light · screwdrivers · test light.

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: We couldn't find a forum consensus for a bone-stock 80 or 800. The best data point comes from IH Parts America, which says "a 31" tire should fit fine" with its CPT spring system. That system adds 1 to 3 inches, about 2 on most trucks, and IHPA's own 800B runs 31x10.50 Duratracs on Scout II rally wheels. IHPA also notes that the front tires can hit the rear of the front wheel well, which its rever

t: What's the difference between the 80, 800, 800A and 800B?
x: The 80 (1961–65) has the fold-down windshield, top-mounted vacuum wipers and the 152 four. The 800 (1965–68) got a fixed windshield, bucket seats, better heating and gauges, plus the 196 four, 232 six and 266 V8. The 800A (late 1968–70) added the 304 V8, a three-piece grille and black headlight bezels. The 800B (August 1970 to March 1971) is the same truck with chrome bezels.

t: Which engine should I look for?
x: The 152 four makes 93 hp, and Autotrader Classics warns that a four-cylinder probably won't hit 75 mph. The 196 four makes 111 hp, the same as the 152 turbo, with better economy. For trail use and highway speed most people want the 266 or 304 V8, but they sit in a heavier nose. Check the block stamping to confirm what's actually fitted.

t: Is the four-cylinder really half a V8?
x: Yes. The 152 is one bank of IH's 304 V8, and the 196 is half of the 392 V8. That's why the engines share so many parts, and why the fours lean over in the engine bay.

t: What oil goes in the transfer case?
x: IH specialists on the IH Parts America forum recommend SAE 90 GL-1 mineral oil, or straight 50-weight motor oil as a substitute, filled to the bottom of the filler hole with the truck level. One moderator estimated the capacity at about 2.5 to 3 quarts. Don't use 80W-90 GL-5.

t: What gear oil for a Power-Lok or Trac-Lok rear axle?
x: Use 80W-90 with a limited-slip additive, according to IHPA forum regulars. One owner found Mobil 1 gear oil made his Power-Lok chatter, while Red Line and Royal Purple worked.
No. The Scout was sold in two- and four-wheel drive from the start, and Wikipedia says four-wheel drive became standard by 1968. To check a truck, see whether the hub protrudes through the hub cap.

t: How do I date my Scout and confirm the model?
x: Use the serial number. Binder Planet hosts a list of starting and ending serial numbers and VINs for the 80, 800, 800A and 800B, plus the special models. Jim Allen, author of the International Scout Encyclopedia, compiled it from IHC records and microfiche. The data plate is on the driver's side of the cowl.

t: What is an early Scout worth?
x: In mid-2024 Autotrader Classics advised budgeting at least $40,000 for a good example. It said a semi-decent one starts around $25,000 and anything under $15,000 is a major project. Restored trucks have sold for far more, including $33,000 for a Scout 80 at Barrett-Jackson in 2014 and a $114,900 asking price for a frame-off 800A.

Yes, and more than for many trucks this age. IH Parts America and Super Scout Specialists list floors, rockers, patch panels, brakes, axle seals, transfer-case kits and wiring. Silodrome notes that engine and transmission parts are widely available. The gap is large panels: Autotrader Classics says no one reproduces fenders.

t: Can an early Scout be made into a usable daily or trail truck?
x: Yes, if you upgrade the right things together. Common jobs are a front disc conversion, a power-brake booster, a power-steering conversion (CPT makes one for 800A and 800B with the IH V8), new springs and shackles, and electronic ignition. Silodrome's advice is that any power upgrade should come with better brakes, a stronger transmission and better suspension.

t: Suspension & Ride — IH Parts America — CPT suspension system, IH Parts America — CPT reverse shackle kit, Super Scout Specialists — CPT lift kit, Scout 80/800B
x: Fresh springs and shackles fix the sag. A reverse-shackle front end tames the forward-shackle chop and makes room for 31s.

t: Brakes — IH Parts America — CPT front disc brake kit, Super Scout Specialists — front disc conversion kit, Super Scout Specialists — power brake booster kit
x: Front discs and a booster are the single biggest improvement to how an early Scout feels in traffic.

t: Steering — IH Parts America — CPT power steering conversion (800A/800B with IH V8), IH Parts America — Borgeson lower steering column kit (800A/800B), IH Parts America — CPT Gold Series tie rod and drag link
x: Tight linkage and, on V8 800A and 800B trucks, a power-steering conversion make the truck far less tiring off-road and on.

t: Ignition & Cooling — Super Scout Specialists — Pertronix Ignitor (4-cyl Holley), Super Scout Specialists — HFI 152 distributor, Super Scout Specialists — aluminum radiator (V8)
x: Electronic ignition and an aluminum radiator remove two of the most common reasons an old Scout gets towed home.

t: Hubs & Traction — IH Parts America — Mile Marker locking hubs (10-spline), IH Parts America — Warn locking hub service kit, Super Scout Specialists — Dana 44 Trac-Loc clutch pack
x: Serviceable locking hubs and a healthy limited-slip are what keep a short-wheelbase Scout moving on loose climbs.

t: Tops & Weatherseals — Super Scout Specialists — Softopper snap top kit (1961–71), Super Scout Specialists — weatherstrip seal kit (80/800), Anything Scout — Scout 800 parts
x: The original top-off life is the point of an early Scout. Good seals and a soft top make it bearable when the weather turns.
[CONFIRM IN MANUAL] for grade and capacity Super Scout Specialists lists a canister-type oil filter for the IH four-cylinder and V8 in these Scouts. Check what your engine has before ordering.
Points or Pertronix · gap and timing [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Points-type distributors on the fours are Holley or Delco. Identify yours before buying an electronic conversion.
Inline filter · pump and sender condition Old tanks shed rust and varnish. If the gauge is wrong, the sender is cheap. Check the tank selector valve too, if the truck has one.
Coolant type and capacity [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Original radiators are often tired. Aluminum replacements are made separately for 4-cylinder and V8 trucks.

Oil type and capacity [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Silodrome says the Scout 80 used a Warner T-90A three-speed and that four-speeds came later. Identify the gearbox before choosing oil. Check the mount while you're under there.

SAE 90 GL-1 mineral oil, or straight 50-weight motor oil · about 2.5–3 qt (IHPA moderator's estimate) Fill to the bottom of the filler hole with the truck level. An IHPA moderator says: "You should not use 80-90wt GL-5 gear oil in the t-case."

80W-90 gear oil; add limited-slip additive for Power-Lok/Trac-Lok · capacity [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] One IHPA forum owner found Mobil 1 gear oil made his Power-Lok clutches chatter, while Red Line and Royal Purple did not.
Inspect seals, wipers and kingpin play These are closed knuckles. Torn wipers let water and grit into the kingpin bearings.
Clean, inspect and repack with wheel-bearing grease Do the front bearings with the knuckle service, and fit new inner seals.

Fluid type [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Rubber hoses this old should be replaced, not inspected. Note whether the truck has a single- or dual-circuit master cylinder, because dual-circuit arrived on 1967 and later 800s.

Chassis grease · inspect drag link, tie rods, steering bell joint and U-joints Check every joint in the linkage before blaming the steering box. If it is the box, IH Parts America sells rebuilt Ross boxes for the 80 and 800.
Inspect the battery, cables, voltage regulator and starter solenoid IH Parts America lists an external voltage regulator for 1962–71 Scouts. Clean every ground while you're checking it.

Scout II Traveler Terra SSII The definitive Scout: IH V8s, Dana 44s, the 118-inch Traveler and Terra, a Nissan diesel and the Baja-winning SSII. Built by a tractor company, designed to beat the Jeep, and rustier than a shipwreck. The Scout II is also a properly tough ladder-frame 4x4 with a 345 V8, Dana 44s and a parts and club scene that makes keeping one alive easier than it should be.

t: Floor, rocker and rear crossmember rust repair
x: Bubbling under the doors, soft or holed floors, a sagging door opening, water on the carpets, and rust at the rear spring mounts and rear crossmember. MIG welder · cut-off wheel · spot-weld drill · clamps and door-opening bracing · seam sealer and weld-through primer

t: Reinforce a cracking steering-box frame mount
x: Wandering steering, a box that moves when someone turns the wheel with the engine running, or visible cracks in the frame rail around the three steering-box bolts. Big tires and front lockers make it worse. Socket set · drill and bits · welder and grinder (if cracked) · torque wrench

t: Rear main seal on an IH V8
x: Oil dripping from the bellhousing area and a wet oil pan rear lip. The engine-to-transmission joint is the giveaway, since valve-cover and pan-gasket leaks run down from higher up. Transmission jack · flywheel holder · seal driver · factory service manual

t: Points or tired electronic ignition → Pertronix
x: Hard starting, misfires, burnt points, or a failing stock electronic module that's hard to find. Timing light · distributor wrench · test light

Wandering, clunks over bumps, uneven tire wear, and play at the top and bottom of the tire with the front end jacked up. Ball-joint press (Dana 30/44 adapter) · spindle-nut socket · pickle fork · torque wrench

t: Front disc brakes, wheel bearings and seals
x: Pulling, a soft pedal, grinding, or play in the wheel. Even when new, the brakes were the weak point: Motor Sport's 1978 test said they tended to pull and twitch. Wheel-bearing (spindle nut) socket · bearing packer · seal driver · brake bleeder

t: Tired leaf springs and shackle bushings
x: A truck that sits low or leans, clunks from the shackles, tires rubbing on 31s, and a harsh ride. Floor jack and stands · breaker bar · penetrating oil · bushing press or vise

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: There's no clean stock answer, because 31s are already marginal. One owner of a 1977 Scout II said his 31s rubbed. IH Parts America's owner recommends a reverse-shackle kit and a 2.5-inch spring lift to run 31s without rubbing, and at least a 1-inch body lift plus a steering upgrade for 33s. Anything Scout rates the Rough Country 2.5-inch kit for up to a 32-inch tire. Plan on stock-sized tires (ar

t: Which engine should I look for?
x: The 345 V8 is the one most people want. Moses Ludel of 4WD Mechanix calls it 'one of the strongest and most durable gasoline V-8s ever built,' and Motor Sport's 1978 test of a 345 automatic gave 163 bhp and 292 lb-ft. The 304 is the same family. The 196 four is slow but simple, and the AMC sixes and Nissan diesels are rarer.

t: Does mine have a Dana 30 or Dana 44 front axle?
x: Until 1974 the Dana 30 was standard at the front, with a Dana 44 as a special order in 1974. After 1974 every Scout II had Dana 44s at both ends. If the front cover is smaller and rounder than the rear one, it's a Dana 30. The line ticket confirms the axle and ratio.

t: How do I tell what year it is?
x: Look at the grille. 1971–72 trucks have three horizontal bars; 1973 has 14 vertical bars; 1974–75 adds a vertical-bar overlay, with square chrome-and-black headlight rings on 1975. 1976 has a one-year 15-bar grille in three sections, 1977–79 has two big horizontal bars, and 1980 has a one-piece plastic grille with square headlights.

t: What's a line ticket and where do I find it?
x: It's the factory build sheet for your VIN, showing the engine, transmission, axles, gear ratio, paint and options. On 1971–76 Scout IIs it's under the hood on the cowl; on 1977–80 trucks it's inside the glove box door. If yours is missing, you can order a replacement.

About 7 quarts with a filter, according to an IH Parts America tech moderator. The IH V8 has a flat-tappet cam, and Binder Planet members recommend a high-zinc oil such as a 15W-40 diesel oil (or 20W-50 in a worn engine) rather than a modern low-zinc synthetic.

t: How good is the fuel economy?
x: Not good with a V8. Motor Sport got 10 mpg on a fast motorway run in a 345 automatic and expected about 14 in gentler use. Super Scout Specialists claims 20 mpg in the city and up to 30 on the highway for the Nissan diesels.

t: Is the diesel worth hunting for?
x: If you want something rare, yes. Super Scout Specialists counts 10,182 diesel Scouts: 4,222 naturally aspirated SD33s from 1976 to 1979, then 571 SD33T turbos in 1979 and 5,389 in 1980. Filters, water pumps and seals are still listed, but it's a slow, specialist engine, so check that the seller has records.

t: Traveltop, Traveler, Terra or SSII: what's the difference?
x: The Scout II is the 100-inch-wheelbase truck with a steel Traveltop, half-cab Roadster top or soft top. The 1976–80 Traveler and Terra are 18 inches longer, with a fiberglass full top and hatch (Traveler) or a half-cab pickup (Terra). The 1977–79 SSII is the stripped soft-top off-roader with a plastic grille and roll bar.

t: Does it have lockers, and how does the 4WD work?
x: There were no factory lockers. Trac-Lok limited-slip differentials were optional. The transfer case is manually shifted, with 2WD high, 4WD high and 4WD low, and the front hubs are free-wheeling. For 33-inch tires, Jim Weed's Off-Road.com build list recommends a front locker, a Detroit or ARB at the rear, and 4.10 gears.

Hagerty gives a median condition #2 value of $42,200 for 1972–80 Scout IIs. SSIIs are the most valuable at $64,750, while some configurations sit below $30,000. Values have levelled off or dipped slightly since 2022.

Hagerty puts Scout II production at about 260,000. Super Scout Specialists' yearly figures run from 31,866 (1975) to 44,434 (1979), with only 13,106 in 1980. About 4,000 SSIIs were built from 1977 to 1979.

t: Suspension Lift — IH Parts America — CPT reverse shackle kit, Anything Scout — Rough Country 2.5-in lift kit, Crawler Proven Technology (CPT)
x: Fresh springs and a mild lift undo decades of sag and clear 31–32-inch tires. Reverse shackles improve the ride and the clearance up front.

t: Steering — Anything Scout — Straight Steer brace, IH Parts America — Borgeson lower steering joint, IH Parts America — PSC hydro-assist-ready steering box
x: Bigger tires overload the steering-box mount and the rag joint. A brace, a Borgeson joint and a rebuilt or hydro-assist box make the truck track straight.

t: Brakes — Anything Scout — complete front disc rebuild kit, IH Parts America — 11-in booster with master cylinder
x: Even new, the brakes were the weak link. A rebuilt front end, braided hoses and a bigger booster are the usual fixes.

t: Lockers, Gears & Hubs — ARB (Air Locker), IH Parts America — Warn premium locking hubs, 1972–80 Scout II, Anything Scout — Dana 44 master install kit
x: There were no factory lockers, and taller tires need lower gears. Dana 44 parts are shared with half the 4x4 world.

t: Ignition & Fuel — Anything Scout — Pertronix by year, IH Parts America — CPT fuel filter bracket (Holley Sniper)
x: Electronic ignition is the cheapest reliability upgrade for an IH V8, and throttle-body EFI brackets are made for the Scout.

t: Body & Rust — IH Parts America — Scout II floors and supports, Anything Scout — rockers and floor pans, Super Scout Specialists — steel body parts
x: Every Scout needs metal eventually. Floors, rockers, quarters and rear crossmembers are all reproduced.

7 qt with filter on Scout II 4x4s (IH Parts America tech moderator) · high-zinc (ZDDP) oil, e.g. 15W-40 or 20W-50 for a worn engine It reads one quart over on the dipstick. On Binder Planet, owners warn that modern low-zinc oils aren't right for the IH flat-tappet cam.
IH 196/266/304/345/392 element; separate elements for SD33 and SD33T diesels The 1980 turbo-diesel uses its own filter.
Champion RJ12YC or NGK 3332 (IH Parts America fitment) · gap [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Caps differ by distributor: Holley, Delco or Prestolite. Check yours before ordering.

About 20 qt cooling system (AMSOIL lists 20.1 qt for the 5.0 L V8) · coolant type [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] The IH V8 water pump feeds through a separate tube sealed with O-rings. Replace them whenever the pump comes off; a complete IH V8 gasket set includes four.

ATF · AMSOIL lists 5 qt initial fill · fluid type [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Moses Ludel of 4WD Mechanix credits the A727's lack of overdrive with helping it survive. Do a pan drop and filter change, not a pressure flush.
AMSOIL's Scout II listing gives engine-oil grades (10W-40 class) for the manual gearboxes · [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Factory boxes vary by year and engine. The line ticket tells you which one you have.
AMSOIL lists 3.4 pints for the two-speed case · lubricant grade [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] The 1980 Dana 300 was a one-year fit. Gasket, seal and overhaul kits are still made for the Dana 20.
GL-5 85W-140 or 90 · AMSOIL lists 4.2 pt front, 3 pt rear · add friction modifier for Trac-Lok The line ticket or the axle tag shows the ratio (2.72 to 4.54) and whether there's a Trac-Lok.

t: Front wheel bearings, seals & locking hubs
x: Repack with wheel-bearing grease · new inner seals Pull the locking hubs and check them while you're in there. Rebuilt or replacement Warn hubs are available.

t: Steering: power steering fluid, rag joint & box bolts
x: Dexron-II-type ATF (AMSOIL's AF2 equivalent) Check the rag joint for play and the steering-box frame mount for cracks. New grade 8 box bolts are cheap.
DOT 3 Replace old rubber brake hoses. If the pedal is poor, check the master cylinder and booster too.
Inline 5/16-in filter on V8s; spin-on filter on SD33 diesels Replace cracked rubber fuel hose. In-tank sender filters are also available.
Chassis grease Greaseable ball joints (Moog) add zerks up front.
Build sheet for your VIN; licensed IH service manual reprints The line ticket settles every 'which part do I need' question. Factory service manuals are split 1971–75, 1976–77 and 1978–80.

Traveler Terra Volkswagen Group's revival of the name, with a Traveler SUV and Terra pickup revealed in October 2024. A boxy, body-on-frame 4x4 with a solid rear axle and lockers at both ends is exactly the kind of truck this site exists for. The catch is that it doesn't exist yet: as of October 2026, Scout is welding test bodies in South Carolina and says customer deliveries start in 2028.

t: When can I actually buy one?
x: Scout says it expects customers to begin taking delivery in 2028 (statement reported April 2026), though its reservation pages still say initial production is targeted for 2027. AutoForecast Solutions reported in April 2026 that Traveler production would start in September 2028 and Terra production in March 2030, and Scout declined to comment on those dates.

Scout says entry-model pricing is "expected to start under $60,000" for both the Traveler and the Terra (scoutmotors.com, checked October 2026). At the October 2024 launch, coverage quoted as low as $50,000 for the Traveler and $51,500 for the Terra with incentives available at the time. Scout says final pricing will be confirmed closer to production.

t: EREV or BEV: what's the difference?
x: The battery-electric version is projected at up to 350 miles of range. The Harvester extended-range version adds a gasoline generator and is projected at 500 miles or more. By March 2026, 87% of reservation holders had chosen the EREV, and Scout now plans to launch it first. Jalopnik reported in April 2026 that EREV towing may be roughly half that of the EV.

On paper, yes. Scout has announced body-on-frame construction, a solid rear axle, four-wheel drive, and front and rear mechanical locking differentials for both models. Launch coverage also mentioned a front sway-bar disconnect, about a foot of ground clearance and 3 feet of water fording, but treat those as reported, not confirmed.

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: Unknown, because production specifications haven't been published. The concepts were shown on 35-inch tires (Traveler) and 37-inch tires on 18-inch wheels (Terra, November 2025 LA Auto Show).

At Scout's $2 billion Production Center in Blythewood, South Carolina, announced March 3, 2023. It's planned for up to 200,000 vehicles a year and more than 4,000 jobs. The first test Traveler body was welded there in July 2026.

Reservations cost $100, are fully refundable and are non-binding. They opened on October 24, 2024. Electrive reported about 160,000 reservations by March 2026, with about three-quarters for the Traveler.

t: Will I buy it from a dealer?
x: No. Scout plans to sell directly, and says retail stores will open in 16 metro areas and grow to about 100 locations in the US and Canada by 2032. Dealer groups, including the National Automobile Dealers Association (February 3, 2025), have sued over the direct-sales plan.

At launch in October 2024, coverage reported more than 10,000 lb for the Terra, more than 7,000 lb for the Traveler, and nearly 2,000 lb of payload for both. Scout says capacities vary by model and trim, and the EREV may tow less.

t: Is it related to the original Scout?
x: In name and styling only. Volkswagen Group acquired the Scout trademarks in 2021 through Navistar, and the new trucks borrow the original Scout's shape. Scout Motors now owns the Scout, Traveler, Terra and Travelall trademarks, and IH Parts America notes that it uses them under license for parts for the original trucks.

The civilian Jeep began with the CJ-2A of 1945, and the CJ (Civilian Jeep) line reached the CJ-5 for the 1955 model year, after Kaiser had bought Willys. It was based on the Korean War-era M38A1, and 603,303 were built before it ended in 1983. American Motors bought Kaiser Jeep in 1970 and gave the CJ its own straight-six and V8 engines from 1972. In 1976 AMC stretched the wheelbase to make the CJ

CJ-5 Renegade Golden Eagle Derived from the M38A1 military Jeep. Rounded door cutouts, Kaiser then AMC power, and 603,303 built across 29 years. The CJ-5 outlived three corporate owners, four engine families and a television hit piece, and it still feels like the original idea of a Jeep with the corners filed off. Short, loud and happiest on a trail, it is the purest classic Jeep you can still use

t: Steering box mount and frame cracks
x: Wandering steering, a box that shifts on the frame when the wheel is turned, or cracks around the box mounting holes. RockCrawler.com reports a CJ-5 that tore its steering box off the frame on a trail. Pitman arm puller · sockets and torque wrench · thread-locker · file · welder for frame cracks · Rust Buster RB1008 (1976–86 CJ-5/7/8)

Clunks on take-off, a rear hub working loose on its shaft, or worn and spun splines. Quadratec's listing explains the cause: the factory hardened hubs cut splines into softer axle shafts, leaving weak spots in the driveline. Hub puller · slide hammer · seal driver · torque wrench · Crown RT23007 kit (1976–83 CJ-5; not for Quadra-Trac)

A sloppy or heavy clutch, trouble finding first, or linkage that falls apart. On Jeep-CJ.com, members say the plastic bushings wear out, and that the pivots can break once the motor mounts go. Wrenches · grease · new bushings or bellcrank · motor mounts if worn

Stumbling, sputtering or stalling at idle and poor fuel economy, but running fine at higher rpm. Offroaders.com says the cause is almost always clogged idle tubes, which let fuel drip from the venturis. 3/16 in socket · small screwdrivers · carb cleaner · fine wire · 0.032 in drill bit · Crown 83300057 kit for 1973–78 YF carbs

t: Ignition refresh or HEI swap (AMC sixes)
x: Hard starting, rough idle, hesitation and poor economy. Hagerty calls ignition the weak point of AMC-engined CJs, and Jeep-CJ.com's write-up blames the factory Duraspark. Timing light · volt meter · soldering iron · plug gapper · HEI distributor and AMC V8 drive gear · 8 mm plug wires
Oil dripping from the joint between the engine and bellhousing. Brass drift · torque wrench · Permatex No. 2 or equivalent · two-piece rear main seal · oil pan gasket set

t: Floor pan and tub rust repair
x: Soft or holed floors, rot along the rockers, rear corners and under the roll bar, and rusty body mounts. Hagerty says floors usually go around the chassis mounts. Cut-off wheel · MIG welder · clamps · seam sealer · weld-through primer

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: In a Jeep-CJ.com thread on stock CJs, members (one running a '79 CJ-5) put 31-inch tires as the safe maximum: one says '31's without rubbing,' and another says 32s rub the rear wheel wells. A little trimming can make 32s fit, but there isn't much to trim ahead of the rear wheels, and most doubt 33s will fit. Old springs sag, so 31s may be the practical limit. Wide tires may need wheels with less b

t: Which engine should I look for?
x: Hagerty recommends the 1972-on 232 or 258 straight-six for smooth power, relaxed cruising and lower running costs than the V8. Jeep-CJ.com praises the 258 for torque and reliability, and says to avoid the GM Iron Duke four used from 1980 to 1983. The early Hurricane four is authentic but limited by its three-speed. The Dauntless V6 is the period hot-rod choice.

t: What's the difference between early and late CJ-5s?
x: For 1972, AMC lengthened the wheelbase from 81 to 83.5 inches and the hood and fenders by 5 inches to fit its sixes and V8. AMC trucks also got the open-knuckle Dana 30 front axle. The tub and windshield changed again for 1976, so tops for 1955–75 trucks don't fit 1976–83 trucks.

t: Is the CJ-5 really a rollover risk?
x: It's short and tall, so drive it with respect. The famous December 1980 60 Minutes segment overstated the case: the IIHS testers got only eight rollovers in 435 runs, and only after hanging hidden weights in the body's corners. A roll bar and seat belts are worthwhile upgrades, and Hagerty advises care on damp roads.

t: What's wrong with the AMC 20 rear axle?
x: From 1976 the CJ-5 used an AMC 20 with two-piece axle shafts. The hardened hubs cut into the softer shaft splines over time. One-piece axle kits, such as Crown's RT23007 for 1976–83 CJ-5s, fix the hub to the shaft. They don't fit Quadra-Trac axles.

It's Buick's 225-cubic-inch V6, which Kaiser licensed in 1965; GM sold Kaiser-Jeep the design and tooling in 1967. It made 155 hp, about double the Hurricane four, and by 1968 about 75% of CJ-5s had it. It's an odd-fire engine, so Jeep fitted a much heavier flywheel to smooth it out. The V6 was dropped after 1971.

t: Did the CJ-5 get disc brakes?
x: Power front disc brakes became an option in 1977. Earlier trucks have drums all round. Power steering became optional with the V6 in 1965, and Hagerty recommends it with the bigger engines.

ExtremeTerrain's CJ chart lists 5W-30 or 10W-30 oil (6 qt for the 4.2, 5 qt for the 304, 4 qt for the 2.5), 80W-90 gear oil in the Dana 30 (1.25 qt), AMC 20 (2.4 qt) and Dana 300 (2 qt), with limited-slip additive for Trac-Lok axles. Brakes take DOT 3. For pre-AMC trucks, a BITOG thread starter summarizes the original 1955 recommendation as GL-4 in the transmission and transfer case [CONFIRM IN MA

t: What's a Renegade worth compared with a base CJ-5?
x: Hagerty's UK guide put clean, usable US CJ-5s from about $12,000, with Renegade and Laredo models at about $20,000. Rare special editions command more. Original special-edition trim and upholstery are hard to find, so check that a Renegade is complete before paying a Renegade price.

Yes. Hagerty says most mechanical, service and body parts are available from US specialists. Quadratec alone lists Omix and Crown replacement parts back to the 1955 CJ-5, including complete steel tubs, floor pans and F-head gasket sets.

Jeep-CJ.com calls the T-18 four-speed (often with a granny-low first) the best transmission ever put in a CJ, and recommends the T-176 among the 1980s gearboxes. Hagerty rates the T-14 three-speed as durable. On 1980–83 trucks, the Iron Duke came with the SR-4 and the 258 with the T-176.

t: Shackles & Springs — Fishbone Offroad greaseable shackles, 1955–75 CJ-5, Rough Country 1-3/8 in front lift shackles, 1976–86 CJ, Energy Suspension rear shackle bushings, 1976–86 CJ
x: Fresh bushings and greaseable shackles fix most of the squeak and slop in a 40-year-old leaf-sprung Jeep. Mild lift shackles add a little clearance.

t: Steering — Rust Buster RB1008 heavy-duty steering box mount
x: Stamped factory steering-box brackets crack with age and big tires. A plate mount is cheap insurance.

t: Axles & Front End — Crown RT23007 AMC 20 one-piece axle kit, Yukon ball joint kit, 1971–93 CJ/Wagoneer, Mile Marker stainless manual hubs, 1981–86 CJ (5-bolt)
x: A one-piece AMC 20 conversion and fresh ball joints in the Dana 30 are the classic AMC-era driveline upgrades.

t: Fuel & Ignition — Holley Sniper EFI BBD, Weber 38 DGES carburetor kit, Performance Distributors DUI distributor
x: Carburetor and ignition are where AMC sixes lose their manners. Common fixes are a Weber, throttle-body EFI or a better distributor.

t: Drivetrain Swaps — Advance Adapters, Novak Conversions
x: Gearbox, transfer-case and engine swaps are part of CJ culture. Members on Jeep-CJ.com use adapter kits to fit T-18s and other boxes.

t: Body & Restoration — OMIX steel body tub kit, 1976–83 CJ-5, Key Parts half floor pan, 1976–83 CJ-5, Rust Buster frame sections, Quadratec — 1945–1986 Jeep CJ parts
x: Reproduction tubs, floors and frame sections mean almost any rusty CJ-5 can be saved.
5W-30 or 10W-30 · 4.2 L six: 6 qt · 5.0 L 304: 5 qt · 2.5 L four: 4 qt · F134 / V6 [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] These are flat-tappet engines. New drain-plug washer every time.
Paper element in the factory air cleaner Fit a new one before tuning the carburetor.
Plugs, cap, rotor, wires; points and condenser on pre-electronic trucks · gaps and timing [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Hagerty calls ignition the CJ's weak point. The AMC six fires 1-5-3-6-2-4.
50/50 coolant · 4.2 L: 10.5 qt · 304 V8: 14.5 qt · Iron Duke: 7.8 qt (ExtremeTerrain) ExtremeTerrain lists a three-year IAT formula. Flush until the water runs clear and fit a new thermostat.
V-belts and molded hoses by engine Old hoses fail from the inside. Squeeze them, and replace any that feel crunchy or spongy.

80W-90 · T-18: 3.25 qt · T-150: 1.4 qt · SR-4: 1.5 qt · T-176: [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] · T-90 / T-14: GL-4 (1955 manual) [CONFIRM CAPACITY] ExtremeTerrain's T-176 figure (3.5 qt / 1.7 L) contradicts itself, so check the manual. On T-14/Dana 18 trucks, oil can migrate from the gearbox into the transfer case, so check both levels.
80W-90 · Dana 300: 2 qt · Dana 20: 1.6 qt · Dana 18: GL-4 [CONFIRM CAPACITY] All CJ-5 transfer cases are gear-driven. Leaks at the output seals are common and cheap to fix.
80W-90 · Dana 30: 1.25 qt · pre-1972 front axle [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] ExtremeTerrain suggests 75W-140 for towing or extreme use.
80W-90 · AMC 20: 2.4 qt · Dana 44: 2 qt · Trac-Lok: add 4 oz limited-slip additive Renegades and many V8 trucks have Trac-Lok. Look for a tag on the cover and add friction modifier if it's there.

Repack and adjust · preload [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Inspect the manual locking hubs while they're apart. Later trucks use five-bolt hubs, earlier ones six-bolt; Offroaders.com dates the change to 1981, Wikipedia to 1980, so count the bolts.
DOT 3 Old drum-brake trucks also need the shoes adjusted. Check the wheel cylinders for weeping.
Power Steering +4, or ATF+4 if unavailable Leaks at the box are common. Seal kits are cheap.
Driveshaft U-joints and slip yokes · shackles · steering joints Replace any dry or notchy U-joint now. Greaseable shackles are an easy upgrade.
Inline filter by engine Old tanks shed rust and varnish. If the filter comes out dirty, inspect the tank and sender.

CJ-7 Renegade Golden Eagle Laredo The CJ-5's 10-inch-longer, square-door evolution: room for an automatic, optional hardtop and steel doors, and AMC's 258 six. Nearly 380,000 were built. The CJ-7 is the classic Jeep that still makes sense: a longer wheelbase, real doors, AMC's unkillable 258 six and a gear-driven transfer case. It's also a 40-year-old steel tub on a frame that cracks by the steeri

t: Convert the AMC 20 to one-piece axle shafts
x: A clunk under load, a rear wheel that suddenly stops driving, or a hub that wobbles on its shaft. The key between the shaft and the pressed-on hub shears once the big hub nut loosens. Or you've simply bought a CJ with original two-piece shafts and bigger tires. Hub puller · slide hammer · 1/2 in breaker bar · dial indicator for end play · welder (optional) · 80W-90 gear oil.

t: Repair a cracked frame at the steering box
x: Steering that wanders or clunks, a steering box that moves when someone turns the wheel with the engine running, or a visible crack in the driver's frame rail near the box. Lifted trucks and trucks on big tires crack more often. Drill and bits · angle grinder · welder (or a shop) · 1/8 in steel plate · clamps · torch for normalizing (optional).

t: Clean the Carter BBD idle tubes
x: Stumbling and sputtering at idle, stalling at stop signs, poor fuel economy, or an idle that someone has turned up to hide the problem. Offroaders.com says the most common cause is clogged idle tubes letting fuel drip from the venturis, so it runs rich. Screwdrivers · snap-ring pliers · carb cleaner · fine wire · masking tape for labeling hoses.

t: Replace rotten floor pans and body mounts
x: Daylight through the floor, wet carpet, a tub that shifts on the frame, or body mounts you can push a screwdriver through. The buyer's guide points to the floor, rockers, rear corners and the area under the roll bar. Cut-off wheel · spot-weld drill · MIG welder · panel clamps · seam sealer · weld-through primer · floor jack and wood block.

t: Rebuild rusted rear shackle mounts and replace shackles and bushings
x: A rear end that sits crooked or crashes over bumps, squeaking leaf springs, or a shackle hanger with rust holes. The buyer's guide calls the shackle mounts a common rot spot, because mud blocks the boxed frame's drain holes. Jack stands · cut-off wheel · welder · grease gun · bushing press or vise.

t: Service the front wheel bearings and locking hubs
x: Play at the top and bottom of the tire, growling that changes when you turn, grease flung inside the rim, or hubs that won't engage. The stock five-bolt Warn hubs on 1981–86 CJs are weak, and Quadra-Trac trucks have drive plates rather than hubs. Hub/spindle-nut socket · torque wrench · bearing packer (optional) · race driver or long bolt · brake cleaner · high-quality wheel-bearing grease.

Gear oil on the skid plate, wet yokes or a drip from the rear output. The Dana 300 holds only 2 quarts, so a slow leak can starve it. Yoke holder or pipe wrench · large socket for the output nut · pry bar · seal driver or 1 1/2 in socket · 80W-90 gear oil.

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: A 31x10.50R15 on the right wheel, on a healthy stock CJ-7. Performance Plus Tire's guide says it needs healthy springs and shallow backspacing (about 3.5 in on a 15x8 for narrow-track trucks), and JeepCJ.com owners agree 31s are the practical limit. One member reported 32x11.50s on a stock CJ with very little rubbing. 33x12.50R15s need a lift; most CJs running 33s have about 4 inches of spring lif

t: Should I keep the AMC 20 or swap it?
x: The AMC 20 has a bigger ring gear (8⅞ in) than a Dana 44, but thinner 29-spline shafts, smaller tubes and, on CJs, keyed two-piece hub-and-shaft axles that shear. On a mild truck, one-piece shafts and stitch-welded tubes fix most of it. If you're running big tires and a locker, the usual swap is a Dana 44, and some late-1986 CJ-7s came with a wide-track Dana 44 from the factory.

t: Which transmission should I look for?
x: The T-18A (1977–79) with its 6.32:1 granny first is the toughest factory CJ gearbox. From 1980, the Tremec T-176 four-speed (3.52:1 first) is the strong option. The SR-4 (1980–81) and the T-4 and T-5 (1982–86) are light-duty Borg-Warner boxes that Novak calls 'essentially a small car transmission in a truck'.

The Dana 300 (1980–86) has a 2.62:1 low range against the Dana 20's 2.03:1, and helical low-range gears that make it quieter. Novak says there's probably no real strength advantage, and the Dana 20 is shorter, which helps driveshaft angles. For more crawl, TeraFlex's TeraLow gearset gives a Dana 300 a 4:1 low range; one owner's crawl ratio went from 32.3:1 to 49.8:1.

t: What is Quadra-Trac, and should I keep it?
x: Quadra-Trac was the optional full-time 4WD in 1976–79 CJ-7s: a chain-driven Borg-Warner 13-39 case paired only with a TH400 automatic. It has a vacuum-locked center differential (the 'Emergency Drive' switch) and an optional bolt-on low range (2.57:1). The chain is known for a short life. Mile Marker sold an overdrive gear-and-chain set that also converts it to part-time, and Offroaders.com names

t: How do I find my axle ratio?
x: Look for the code stamped on the AMC 20 housing boss to the left of the cover, near the tube. Narrow-track codes differ from wide-track ones: on a wide-track axle, A is 3.54 open, AA is 3.54 Trac-Lok, H is 3.73 open, and C is 4.10 open. Offroaders.com advises confirming with a tape measure or the front axle's Dana tag, because codes conflict between versions. Offroaders.com gives the common Dana 3

t: What's the difference between narrow track and wide track?
x: 1976–81 CJ-7s use narrow-track axles, 50.5 in wheel to wheel on the AMC 20. From 1982 the wide-track axles measure 54.5 in, which helps stability. Both use 5 x 5.5 in wheels. The 1982–86 Dana 30 also switched to pin-bolted calipers and crimped brake hoses.

t: Which engine is the one to have?
x: The 258 straight six (1976–78 trucks may have the smaller 232 six, which was standard until 1979). JeepCJ.com's buyer's guide calls it 'a strong, torquey, reliable motor' and says to avoid the GM Iron Duke four (1980–83). The 304 V8 (to 1981) is quicker but was choked by smog controls by the end: 125 hp in 1980–81 against the 258's 110.

ExtremeTerrain's CJ guide lists 80W-90 gear oil for the Dana 30 (1.25 qt), AMC 20 (2.4 qt; add 4 oz of limited-slip additive for Trac-Lok), Dana 300 (2 qt) and Dana 20 (1.6 qt). Quadra-Trac needs its own transfer case fluid (2.25 qt). The T-176, SR-4, T-150 and T-18 take 80W-90; ExtremeTerrain lists ATF+4 for the T-4 and T-5 and for the automatics (the TH400 is a GM unit, so check your manual befo

t: Will Wrangler wheels and parts fit?
x: Not the wheels. CJ axles use 5 x 5.5 in, and later Jeep Dana 30s use 5 x 4.5 in. Lots of other parts carry over, though: the 258 lived on in the YJ until 1990, and outer Dana 30 parts (knuckle outward) swap between CJ versions, so a drum-brake CJ can be converted to discs.
Only for export. From 1980 to 1982 AMC built CJ-7s in Ohio with Isuzu's 2.4-liter C240 diesel four, a T-176, a Dana 300 and 4.10 axles. None were sold new in the US.

t: Suspension & Spring Swaps — Fishbone Offroad — spring hangers for YJ springs on a CJ-7, Warrior Products — CJ-5/CJ-7 shackle kits, Rancho
x: Old CJ leaf springs sag and ride like a cart. New springs, shackles and bushings cure it. A popular upgrade is to fit hangers that let you run Wrangler YJ leaf springs.

t: Bumpers & Armor — LoD Offroad — CJ-5/CJ-7 front bumpers, LoD Offroad — Expedition rear bumper, WARN — winches
x: The factory bumpers are thin. A steel front bumper gives you a winch mount and recovery points, and a rear tube bumper with D-rings protects the tub corners, which tend to rust anyway.

t: Axles & Lockers — USA Standard Gear — AMC 20 Spartan Locker, Crown Automotive — AMC 20 one-piece axle kits, Yukon Gear & Axle
x: Put one-piece shafts in the AMC 20 before you add a locker, or the locker will find the weak keyed hubs quickly.

t: Transfer Case & Gearing — Novak Conversions — Dana 300 guide & parts, Advance Adapters
x: The Dana 300 takes a 4:1 low-range gearset, its shifter interlock can be removed for twin-stick operation, and Novak and Advance Adapters can help you swap out a weak T-4 or T-5.

t: Fuel System — Holley Sniper EFI BBD kit for CJ 258, Weber 38-DGES kit for CJ/YJ 4.2L
x: The computer-controlled BBD is the 258's weakest link. A Weber 38 kit or Holley's bolt-on Sniper EFI replaces it.

t: Tops & Body — Bestop Supertop for CJ-7/YJ, Key Parts — CJ-7 rear corner panel, Omix — steel body tub, CJ-7
x: A new soft top keeps you drier. Officially licensed replacement panels mean even a rotten tub can be saved.

About 6 qt including the filter, per a 1984 CJ-7 owner's manual quoted on JeepCJ.com · ExtremeTerrain lists 5W-30 or 10W-30 for CJ engines Owners report 5 to 5.5 qt reaching FULL depending on the pan and filter, so fill to 5, run it, then top up on the dipstick. The 304 V8 takes 5 qt and the 2.5 four takes 4 qt (ExtremeTerrain). The MFK16 and MFK18 kits below are for 304 and 2.5L trucks, not the 2
Paper element in the factory TAC housing Check the TAC flapper and its vacuum hose while the lid is off: the BBD and its emissions plumbing run poorly with a stuck flapper or split hoses.
In-line filter, 4.2L Rust from an old tank clogs the filter and the BBD's idle circuits, which is often the real cause of a 'carb problem'.
Plug part numbers change by year: Crown 4318137 for 1978–80 4.2L, 4318138 for 1981–90 Fresh ignition parts are the cheap first step before blaming the carb.

50/50 conventional (IAT) green coolant · 258 (4.2): 10.5 qt · 304 V8: 14.5 qt · 151 Iron Duke: 7.8 qt · AMC 150: 11 qt (ExtremeTerrain) Old CJs run warm with partly blocked radiators. Flush the block, replace both radiator hoses and the thermostat, and pressure-test the cap.
Belt type depends on year and accessories [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Inspect the air-pump and power-steering belts too; air-pump brackets are hard to find, so don't lose them.

T-176: 80W-90, about 1.7 L · T-18: 80W-90, 3.25 qt · SR-4: 80W-90, 1.5 qt · T-150: 80W-90, 1.4 qt · T-4/T-5: ATF+4, 2 qt (ExtremeTerrain) ExtremeTerrain lists the T-176 as '3.5 quarts / 1.7 liters'; the liter figure matches 3.5 pints, so fill to the plug rather than by volume. Some owners run synchromesh fluid in T-4s. Check the casting number on the driver's side before you buy fluid.

ExtremeTerrain lists ATF+4 · TF999/TF904: 3 qt service fill · TH400 (Quadra-Trac trucks): 6 qt service fill · TH400 is a GM unit: confirm fluid type [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] A service fill replaces only part of the fluid, so do a second drain-and-fill if the old fluid is dark or burnt.

Dana 300: 80W-90, 2 qt · Dana 20: 80W-90, 1.6 qt · Quadra-Trac: Quadra-Trac formula fluid, 2.25 qt (ExtremeTerrain) Quadra-Trac's chain stretches when the oil is low or old, so don't skip this one. Check the Dana 300's output seals while you're under there.
80W-90 gear oil · 1.25 qt (ExtremeTerrain) Check the axle U-joints for play while you're at the knuckles.

80W-90 gear oil · 2.4 qt · add 4 oz of limited-slip additive for Trac-Lok (ExtremeTerrain). Late-1986 Dana 44: 2 qt Read the gear-ratio and Trac-Lok code stamped left of the cover while it's clean, and check that the hub nuts on two-piece shafts are tight.

Repack with high-quality wheel-bearing grease · inner nut to 50 ft-lb to seat, back off, then set 0.001–0.005 in end play (manual figures quoted in an Off-Road.com thread) · outer nut torque [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Hubs are the weak five-bolt Warn type on 1981–86 trucks. Quadra-Trac trucks have drive plates instead, and hubs shouldn't be fitted unless the case has been converted to part-time.

DOT 3 for the brake master cylinder and, where fitted, the clutch master cylinder (ExtremeTerrain) Rubber hoses on a CJ are probably original. 1982–86 trucks use crimped hose-to-steel-line assemblies, so check them for cracks.
Power steering fluid +4, or ATF+4 if unavailable (ExtremeTerrain) Watch the steering box as someone turns the wheel. If the box moves, inspect the frame for cracks before you blame the box.

Chassis grease at every zerk Driveshaft U-joints and slip yokes, steering joints, and greaseable shackles if fitted. CJ leaf-spring pivots that have been neglected squeak first and then wear out their bushings.

CJ-8 Scrambler A CJ-7 stretched to a 103.5-inch wheelbase, with a removable half cab and a small pickup bed. Ronald Reagan kept one at his ranch. The Scrambler is a CJ-7 that kept going after the roll bar and grew a little pickup bed. Jeep sold barely 28,000 of them, one went to a president, and now everyone wants one.

Clunks on take-off, a rear hub loosening on its shaft, or spun splines. Quadratec explains that the factory hardened hubs cut into softer axle-shaft splines, leaving weak spots in the driveline. Hub puller · slide hammer · seal driver · torque wrench · Crown 1982–86 CJ-7/CJ-8 one-piece kits (sold per side)

t: Steering box mount and frame cracks
x: Wandering steering, a box that shifts on the frame, or cracks around the box mounting holes. RockCrawler.com blames cheap stamped brackets, age, mileage and big tires. Pitman arm puller · torque wrench · thread-locker · welder for frame repairs

t: T-5 jumping out of gear: rebuild or swap
x: On a 1985 CJ-7 thread, a T-5 behind the 258 popped out of first and third, grinding on downshifts. Transmission jack · snap-ring pliers · bearing puller · adapter kit if swapping

Stumbling or stalling at idle and poor economy, but fine at higher rpm. Offroaders.com says the cause is almost always clogged idle tubes. It also says post-1981 feedback carbs with a stepper motor are 'a bit more troublesome.' 3/16 in socket · small screwdrivers · carb cleaner · fine wire · 0.032 in drill bit
Hard starting, rough idle, hesitation and poor fuel economy, which Jeep-CJ.com's write-up blames on the factory Duraspark. Timing light · volt meter · soldering iron · plug gapper

A sloppy clutch, trouble selecting first, or linkage that pops apart. Jeep-CJ.com members say the plastic bushings wear out, and that worn motor mounts can break the pivots. Wrenches · grease · bushings or bellcrank · motor mounts if worn
Oil dripping from the joint between the engine and bellhousing. Brass drift · torque wrench · Permatex No. 2 or equivalent

t: Floor, bed and tailgate rust repair
x: Soft floors, rot in the rear bed corners, wheel wells and rockers, and a tailgate rusting around its seal and hardware. Cut-off wheel · MIG welder · clamps · seam sealer

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: Jeep-CJ.com members put 31-inch tires as the safe maximum on a stock CJ. They say 32s rub the rear wheel wells without trimming, and doubt 33s will fit. The thread covers CJs generally rather than the Scrambler specifically, but the CJ-8 shares the CJ-7's front end and springs. Saggy old springs and wheel backspacing can make even 31s tight.

Wikipedia lists 8,355 in 1981, 7,759 in 1982, 5,405 in 1983, 4,130 in 1984, 2,015 in 1985 and 128 in 1986, about 27,800 in total. Some argue the 1986 trucks were leftovers. SlashGear compares that with more than 379,000 CJ-7s.

The 258 straight-six, rated at 115 hp. SlashGear calls it the most desirable option, and Jeep-CJ.com praises it for torque and reliability. The Iron Duke four in early trucks is the one Jeep-CJ.com says to avoid. The later AMC four, at 105 hp, is better. No Scrambler came with a V8.

Jeep-CJ.com recommends the T-176 four-speed among 1980s CJ gearboxes, and members call the 1985–86 T-5 five-speed weak. The automatics were Chrysler TorqueFlites: the 904 behind the four and the 999 behind the six.

Sort of. The bed is part of the body tub behind a removable half cab, not a separate box. 4WDrive quotes a 636 kg (about 1,400 lb) payload and a bed two feet longer than the CJ-7's rear tub. Full soft and hard tops were optional, so you can also run it as a long open CJ.

t: Did Ronald Reagan really own one?
x: Yes. A blue Scrambler was bought for Rancho del Cielo, and White House photographers caught Reagan with it there in April 1983. RealTruck identifies it as a 1983 CJ-8 Renegade with about 18,000 miles. It's displayed at the Reagan Ranch Center in Santa Barbara with a 'GIPPER' plate.

t: What's wrong with the AMC 20 rear axle?
x: Its two-piece shafts let the hardened hub cut into the softer shaft splines over time. One-piece kits for 1982–86 CJ-7s and CJ-8s, such as Crown's, fix the hub to the shaft. Some 1986 Scramblers have a Dana 44 instead, which doesn't have this issue.

ExtremeTerrain's CJ chart lists 5W-30 or 10W-30 oil (6 qt for the 4.2, 4 qt for the 2.5), 80W-90 in the Dana 300 (2 qt), Dana 30 (1.25 qt), AMC 20 (2.4 qt) and Dana 44 (2 qt), ATF+4 in the T-4/T-5 (2 qt) and TorqueFlites (3 qt service fill), and DOT 3 brake fluid. Trac-Lok axles need limited-slip additive.

t: What are the World Cab and Overlander?
x: Right-hand-drive Scramblers with a full-length steel top and rear barn doors in place of the tailgate. The Alaskan postal service bought 230, with automatic transmissions. Venezuela and Australia got a similar CJ8 Overlander with full-length rear windows.

A lot more than it cost new. 4WDrive lists a $7,288 base price at launch. SlashGear says a well-preserved Scrambler now costs at least $30,000, and eBay Motors featured a 2,100-mile truck asking $39,900. Rust and originality drive the price.
Wikipedia says the Cherokee-based Comanche pickup effectively replaced the Scrambler in 1986. The open-top CJ itself gave way to the Wrangler YJ in 1987.

t: Springs & Shackles — OMIX OE leaf springs, 1976–86 CJ-7/CJ-8, Fishbone Offroad greaseable shackles, 1976–86 CJ-7, Energy Suspension shackle bushings, 1976–86 CJ5/7/8
x: Forty-year-old leaves sag, and a long-wheelbase truck shows it at the back. Fresh OE springs, greaseable shackles and new bushings restore the ride height.

t: Steering — Fishbone Offroad FB26318 steering box mount, Rust Buster RB1008 heavy-duty steering box mount
x: Boxed CJ frames crack at the steering box. A plate mount spreads the load.

t: Axles & Hubs — Crown one-piece axle kit, 1982–86 CJ-7/CJ-8, Yukon ball joint kit, 1971–93 CJ, Mile Marker stainless manual hubs, 1981–86 CJ
x: A one-piece AMC 20 conversion is the classic Scrambler upgrade. Add fresh ball joints and good manual hubs up front.

t: Fuel & Ignition — Holley Sniper EFI BBD, Weber 38 DGES carburetor kit, Performance Distributors DUI distributor
x: The feedback Carter BBD and Duraspark are the 258's weak spots. Throttle-body EFI, a Weber or a better distributor sorts them out.

t: Transmission Swaps — Advance Adapters, Novak Conversions
x: Owners replace the T-5 with stronger gearboxes using adapter kits.

t: Tops & Body — Bestop Supertop for 1981–85 CJ-8, OMIX steel body tub kit, CJ-8 Scrambler, Quadratec — 1945–1986 Jeep CJ parts
x: Scrambler tops, tubs and tailgate parts are model-specific. Reproductions keep the truck original.
5W-30 or 10W-30 · 4.2 L six: 6 qt · 2.5 L four: 4 qt Look for rear-main and valve-cover leaks while you're under there.
Paper element in the factory air cleaner Fit a fresh one before you judge the carburetor.
Plugs, cap, rotor, wires · gap and timing [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] The 258 fires 1-5-3-6-2-4. Duraspark pickups and modules are common culprits for poor running.
50/50 coolant · 4.2 L: 10.5 qt · Iron Duke: 7.8 qt · AMC 2.5: 11 qt Flush until clean, fit a new thermostat and check the overflow bottle for cracks.
V-belts or serpentine (1984–86 with factory A/C) · molded hoses Squeeze every hose and replace any that feel crunchy or spongy.
SR-4: 80W-90, 1.5 qt · T-4 / T-5: ATF+4, 2 qt · T-176: 80W-90 [CONFIRM CAPACITY] ExtremeTerrain's T-176 figure (3.5 qt / 1.7 L) contradicts itself, so check the manual. Don't put gear oil in a T-5.
TF904 / TF999: ATF+4 · 3 qt service fill (8.5 qt overhaul) A pan drop changes only part of the fluid. Do it twice if the old fluid is dark.
Dana 300 · 80W-90 · 2 qt Output seals weep with age, and kits are cheap.
Dana 30 · 80W-90 · 1.25 qt ExtremeTerrain suggests 75W-140 for towing or extreme use.
AMC 20: 80W-90, 2.4 qt · Dana 44 (some 1986): 2 qt · Trac-Lok: add 4 oz limited-slip additive While the cover is off, check the hubs for play. It's the AMC 20's weak point.
Repack and adjust · preload [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] 1980–86 CJs use five-bolt manual locking hubs. Check them for slipping while they're apart.
DOT 3 Check the rear wheel cylinders and front calipers for weeping.
Power Steering +4, or ATF+4 if unavailable Box seal kits are cheap. Inspect the box mount while you're there.
U-joints and slip yokes (the long rear shaft especially) · shackles · steering joints · inline fuel filter Replace dry or notchy U-joints now.

SJ Grand Wagoneer The full-size SJ wagon that began as the 1963 Wagoneer, renamed Grand Wagoneer for its final luxury-V8 years. A 1962 design in a vinyl-wood cardigan, still drinking carbureted 360 V8 fuel when Chrysler finally switched off the Toledo line in 1991. It is slow, thirsty and gloriously out of date, and it invented the idea that a truck could be the nicest car in the driveway. Buy the

t: Rebuild the Motorcraft 2150 or convert to throttle-body injection
x: Hesitation, stumbling or stalling cold or hot, hard hot starts, fuel smell, poor idle. Hagerty's specialist blames the carburetor for about 40% of owner headaches. Carb rebuild kit with specs · gasket scraper · carb cleaner · vacuum gauge · timing light · for TBI: fuel-line tools, wiring tools, laptop or handheld tuner per kit

Oil dripping from where the engine meets the transmission, with no obvious leak above it. Hagerty lists rear main leaks as a common 360 fault. Floor jack and stands · engine support · torque wrench · seal pick · RTV per seal instructions · factory service manual for torque specs [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]

t: Fix a dead power window (flex rack and motor)
x: You can hear the motor run, but the glass doesn't move or moves in jerks. Hagerty says window flex tracks snap often on these trucks. Door-panel clip tool · glass holder · screwdrivers and sockets · white lithium grease

The rear glass won't go down, so the interior tailgate handle can't be reached. YourMechanic says the tailgate window is 'notorious for failing'. Trim tools · test light or multimeter · sockets · silicone or lithium lube

t: Patch floors, rockers and lower quarters
x: Wet or crunchy carpet, holes under the driver's floor mat, bubbling under the woodgrain, rotten rockers that can let exhaust into the cabin. MIG welder · cut-off wheel · spot-weld drill · clamps · weld-through primer · seam sealer

t: Drop the fuel tank and replace the skid plate and straps
x: Rust where the tank meets the body, a sagging or perforated skid plate, fuel smell, a sending unit that reads wrong. Both Hagerty and YourMechanic name this area. Transmission jack or floor jack with board · penetrating oil · fuel-line clamps · sockets

t: Selec-Trac won't engage: vacuum system and transfer-case service
x: The dash 2WD/4WD control does nothing, the truck stays in one mode, or 4WD drops out. Hagerty says to check that 4WD engages on the fly; seals leak with age. Hand vacuum pump · vacuum hose · sockets · drain pan · fluid pump

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: We couldn't find a forum consensus we trust for the SJ, so we won't guess. The factory size is P235/75R15 on 15x7 six-lug alloys (1989 spec). Anything larger should be test-fitted at full lock and with the suspension compressed. Team Grand Wagoneer sells a 3-inch lift kit with springs and shocks for owners who want more. Running bigger tires on yours? Tell us through Show Us Your Rig.

t: How much power does the 360 V8 make?
x: It depends on the source. Hagerty quotes 140 hp and 280 lb-ft, Offroaders.com says 144 hp, and Wikipedia's AMC V8 entry lists 160 hp for the two-barrel 360 from 1978 to 1991. Either way, the torque is what moves it. The 360 is a tall-deck AMC engine. Chrysler kept building it until 1991, changing only the casting from '360' to '5.9L'.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: Not much. Wikipedia cites a combined 11 mpg, and Hagerty says single digits in town and about a dozen on the highway with the V8. Fuel prices after the 1990 oil shock helped kill the truck. TBI conversions are said to help, but don't expect miracles from a carbureted-era V8 in a 4,000-plus-pound wagon.
Jeep's 1989 spec lists 5,000 lb maximum trailer weight (750 lb tongue) with the Class III Package B, and 3,500 lb (350 lb tongue) with the Class I and II Package A.

Most are Selec-Trac: an NP228 or NP229 (the 229 adds a viscous coupling) with a dash control that shifts between 2WD and 4WD on the move using vacuum. Offroaders.com says some 1984–88 Grand Wagoneers used the part-time NP208 instead. Going between 4-High and 4-Low takes neutral and a crawl of under 5 mph.

1989–91, if you can. Those years got better rust-proofing (electrocoat primer), base-clear paint, an improved A/C compressor, an overhead console, keyless entry and a rear wiper. The 1991 Final Edition carries a premium. Hagerty's specialist adds that low mileage, under about 100,000, is the safest buy.

Every Grand Wagoneer left the factory with a carburetor, a two-barrel Motorcraft on the 360. Throttle-body injection kits are the most common upgrade. Hagerty puts the conversion at about $2,000 in parts and up to $1,000 in labor, and Wagonmaster builds its trucks around a Howell TBI system.

Values rose for years. In one report, Hagerty listed a 1991 at $36,900 in #2 condition and $62,200 in #1, and said a nice #3 driver shouldn't cost much more than $20,000. Restomods from Wagonmaster or Classic Gentleman were $40,000–80,000 in 2019. These figures are dated, so check current Hagerty valuations and recent BaT results.

t: Is this the same as the Wagoneer Limited (XJ)?
x: No. From 1984 to 1990 Jeep also sold a compact, unibody Wagoneer based on the Cherokee XJ, with woodgrain decals. The Grand Wagoneer is the full-size, body-on-frame SJ.

Mostly. Specialists such as Team Grand Wagoneer and BJ's Off Road stock everything from floor pans to woodgrain vinyl. But Hagerty's specialist estimates about 20% of the parts a restoration needs come from salvage yards, and front fenders are no longer available.

Yes. It's vinyl, not wood. The 1987–91 trucks use 'marine teak' and earlier trucks the cherry-oak style, and replacement kits are sold for both. Fix any rust under the old vinyl first, because bubbles usually mean the metal is rotting.

t: Fuel Injection — Team Grand Wagoneer — TBI conversion kit, Wagonmaster
x: The single most popular upgrade: easier starts, smoother running and an end to carburetor tinkering.

t: Suspension & Lift — Team Grand Wagoneer — 3" lift kit with leaf springs & shocks, Team Grand Wagoneer — Skyjacker shock & stabilizer set
x: Fresh leaf springs and shocks fix the wallow. A modest lift makes room for slightly bigger tires on gravel and snow.

t: Cooling — Team Grand Wagoneer — HD 3-row radiator, Team Grand Wagoneer — high-flow water pump
x: A carbureted V8, a 30-plus-year-old radiator and a tow hitch make a recipe for boiling over. Heavy-duty radiators and high-flow pumps are cheap insurance.

t: Brakes — Team Grand Wagoneer — stainless brake line kit, BJ's Off Road — brake parts
x: Stainless lines and modern pads help a heavy wagon stop on old drum-rear brakes.
If you'd rather buy one finished, specialist builders restore and update trucks for about the price of a new SUV.

t: Full-Size Jeep Parts Specialists — Team Grand Wagoneer, BJ's Off Road (Full-Size Jeep Parts)
x: SJ-specific sheet metal, trim, weatherstrip and drivetrain parts that general parts stores no longer carry.
AMC 360 V8 · capacity and grade [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] The filter changes by year: one for 1984–86, another for 1987–90, and a third for 1991. Order by model year.
Stock air-cleaner element · inline fuel filter A dirty filter makes the 2150 carb run rich. Replace the air-cleaner-to-carb gasket at the same time.
8 plugs · gap per underhood label [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Hagerty flags Motorcraft ignition problems. A fresh tune-up is the cheapest drivability fix before you blame the carburetor.
Early 1978–1987 / late 1988–1991 Electronic ignition modules are split by year; a spare in the glovebox is cheap insurance on a 30-plus-year-old system.
Coolant type and capacity [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Replace the thermostat, gasket, radiator hoses and cap together, and check the thermal fan clutch while the system is open.
ATF · drain pan, new filter and gasket [CONFIRM CAPACITY IN MANUAL] This is a pan drop, not a flush. Team Grand Wagoneer recommends fully synthetic ATF.
ATF-type fluid (per Team Grand Wagoneer) · capacity [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] While you're under there, check the yoke seals and the Selec-Trac vacuum lines.

75W-90 gear oil · limited-slip-rated oil for Trac-Lok axles · capacities [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] The front is a Dana 44; the rear is an AMC or Dana 44 depending on year. Read the tag and use LSD-compatible oil if the truck has Trac-Lok (standard with Selec-Trac from 1986).
Grease every zerk; inspect for play Check the front axle U-joints at full lock and the driveshaft joints and slip yoke for clunks.
Check for vertical and horizontal play Worn joints show up as wander and uneven tire wear. Replace upper and lower together.
Power-steering fluid · flush the old fluid Team Grand Wagoneer notes most owners never flush it. While you're there, check the steering box rag joint.
Brake fluid per the master-cylinder cap [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Old steel lines on a salt-state truck deserve a hard look. A complete pre-bent stainless kit is available.
Alternator/AC pair and power-steering belt (V8-360) The 360 uses V-belts. Replace both alternator/AC belts as a matched pair.
Stock-height leaf springs front and rear Sagging springs and dead shocks make the truck wallow. Stock-height sets and full nitrogen shock sets are available.

XJ The compact unibody Cherokee, with the 4.0-liter straight six from 1987. It was the template for the modern SUV. A small box designed by AMC with help from Renault, given one of the best straight-sixes ever bolted into a 4x4 and two solid axles, then sold to suburbia for 18 years. Now it's the budget wheeler everyone recommends. Check the rockers, the floors, the head casting on 2000–01 trucks,

Unexplained coolant loss, brown or dirty coolant, milky residue under the oil cap, and often a recent overheat. Wikipedia says the crack sits between cylinders 3 and 4 and often shows as a tan line with the valve cover off. Torque wrench · head bolt sequence and spec from FSM [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] · gasket scraper · pushrod organizer · coolant pressure tester

t: Replace the rear main seal (4.0 two-piece)
x: Oil dripping from the joint between engine and transmission. Rule out the valve cover gasket, oil-pressure sender, oil-filter-adapter O-rings and (on distributor engines) the distributor gasket first. Jack and stands · torque wrench · seal pick · RTV per seal instructions · new pan gasket
Oil on the driver's side of the block and dripping onto the exhaust or crossmember, which is often mistaken for a rear main leak. Sockets and extensions · filter wrench · drain pan · clean rags

t: Fix the overheating: radiator, fan clutch, pump and mounts
x: The gauge climbs on hills or in traffic, the electric fan doesn't come on, or the radiator's plastic tanks seep. OffroadXtreme found factory radiators cracking from frame twist on the trail. Coolant drain pan · fan-clutch wrench · sockets · infrared thermometer · funnel kit for bleeding

t: Replace the crankshaft position sensor (hot stalls)
x: The engine dies when hot and restarts after cooling. No spark, and fuel pressure checks out but fuel doesn't reach the injectors. Sometimes the gauges go dead or 'no bus' shows on the odometer. NAXJA members call thermal failure 'pretty common'. Multimeter · long extensions and swivel · flashlight

t: Cure death wobble: track bar, steering linkage and box mount
x: Violent front-end shake after a bump at speed, wandering, clunks. OffroadXtreme says the track bar is the usual cause. Helper · pry bar · tie-rod puller · torque wrench · alignment afterward

t: Replace rusted floor pans and rockers
x: Wet carpet, holes under the mats, rockers that crumble under a screwdriver, rusted lower rear quarters. MIG welder · cut-off wheel · spot-weld drill · clamps · weld-through primer · seam sealer · cavity wax

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: NAXJA's consensus is 235/75R15 (about 29 in) on the stock 15x7 wheels with 5.25 in backspacing, which fits fine. A 30x9.50R15 is the practical limit. One owner's '88 rubbed only the front control arms at full lock, which a steering-stop adjustment fixes at the cost of turning circle, and some later trucks have rubbed the rear fenders. A 255/70R16 (about 30 in) rubbed the rear on a loaded 2000. Les

t: Which years and engines should I buy?
x: Buy a 4.0. OffroadXtreme recommends the 1991-and-later HO, says 1987–90 Renix trucks suit owners who like diagnosing sensors, and says to avoid 1984–86 (no 4.0). NAXJA members single out non-ABS 1998–99 trucks with the 4.0, AW4, NP231 and 29-spline 8.25 as about the most solid combination. The 2000–01 trucks are good if the head has been checked or replaced.

The 2000–01 4.0 got a head with casting number 0331 that can crack between cylinders 3 and 4, letting coolant into the oil. Look through the oil filler between the cylinder 3 and 4 exhaust rockers: a 'TUPY' mark means a revised head. Most failures follow an overheat, so keep the cooling system healthy, and never replace a cracked one with another 0331.

t: Which rear axle do I have, and is it any good?
x: There are three possibilities. The Dana 35 was used on early trucks and on ABS-equipped trucks throughout; it's fine stock but weak with bigger tires. The Chrysler 8.25 is common on non-ABS 1991–2001 trucks and went from 27 to 29 splines in late 1996. The Dana 44 came on some 1987–91 tow-package trucks. The axle tag or the cover shape will tell you.

From 1987 both have 2.72:1 low range. The NP231 Command-Trac is part-time (2H, 4H, N, 4L) and NAXJA calls it better for heavy off-road use. The NP242 Selec-Trac adds a full-time 4WD mode for slippery pavement.

t: What fluids and capacities does it take?
x: Per the 2001 owner's manual as quoted on NAXJA: 4.0 oil 6 qt with filter, coolant 10.5 qt, AW4 4 qt drain-and-fill (Dexron III/Mercon), NP231 2.2 pt, Dana 30 2.5 pt 75W-90, Dana 35 3.5 pt, 8.25 4.4 pt, plus friction modifier for Trac-Lok. ExtremeTerrain lists ATF+4 for the AW4 and 12 qt of coolant. Check your manual. See 'After you buy it' for the full list.

The usual suspects are a clogged or cracked radiator (the factory plastic tanks can split under frame twist), a weak fan clutch, a dead electric fan or relay, an old water pump, and worn motor mounts that let the fan get too close to the radiator. On Renix trucks, check whether someone has converted the cooling system.

t: What causes death wobble, and how do I fix it?
x: Usually the track bar: worn bushings, a loose bracket or a bent bar. Worn tie-rod ends, the drag link or ball joints can also cause it. Find the loose part with a helper turning the wheel, replace it, and check the unibody around the track-bar and steering-box mounts for cracks. A new steering stabilizer only hides the problem.

NAXJA members report XJs commonly running 250,000–300,000 miles or more on factory drivetrains if they're maintained. The original poster in NAXJA's beginner thread called anything under 100,000 miles hard to find and probably overpriced.

t: Why is my Renix XJ so hard to diagnose?
x: The 1987–90 Renix computer doesn't store fault codes, so you diagnose sensors with a multimeter. It's well documented, but it's more work than the 1991-and-later Chrysler system, which became OBD-II with the JTEC computer in 1996.

t: How much lift do I need?
x: It depends on the tires and the trail. The factory Up Country package added an inch. Kits run from TeraFlex's 1.5-inch Budget Boost, through 3-inch leaf-and-coil systems from Zone and Rough Country, to 4.5–6.5-inch long-arm kits. Bigger lifts usually need an adjustable track bar and driveline work.

t: Suspension Lift — TeraFlex 1.5" Budget Boost (Quadratec), Zone Offroad 3" XJ system (Quadratec), Rough Country 3" Series II XJ kit (Quadratec), Old Man Emu (ARB)
x: The XJ responds well to a modest lift. Coils and add-a-leafs or new packs clear 30–31 in tires, and long-arm kits are for serious rock work.

t: Track Bar & Steering — JKS Manufacturing OGS126 adjustable track bar (Quadratec), Rough Country forged adjustable track bar (Quadratec), Crown RT21004 HD steering kit (Quadratec)
x: Lift moves the axle sideways and loads the steering. An adjustable track bar and heavier linkage keep it straight and wobble-free.

t: Rocker Armor — Rock Hard 4x4 RH1014 rocker sliders (Quadratec), Warrior Products under-door sideplates (Quadratec), Rock Hard 4x4
x: Unibody rockers are part of the structure. Protect them before the first rock hits.

t: Cooling — Cold Case aluminum radiator (Quadratec), CSF copper/brass radiator (Quadratec)
x: The XJ's weak spot, especially in hot climates or with a 2000–01 head you'd like to keep.

t: Axles & Lockers — Yukon Gear & Axle, ARB (Air Lockers)
x: Regearing for bigger tires and adding lockers. The 8.25 and Dana 30 are worth building, while many owners replace a Dana 35.

t: Bumpers & Recovery — Rock Hard 4x4, Rough Country
x: Stock plastic bumpers don't hold a winch or survive a stump. Steel bumpers add recovery points and approach angle.
4.0: 6.0 qt (5.7 L) with filter · 5W-30 (ExtremeTerrain) · 2.5: 4.0 qt Check the oil-filter-adapter O-rings while you're under there. They're a common leak that gets blamed on the rear main.
Panel element, 1987–2001 Crown's master filter kits (MFK8 / MFK9) bundle the oil, air and fuel filters.

Copper plugs, 0.035 in gap (4.0) · cap, rotor and wires through 1999 · coil rail on 2000–01 On 2000–01 coil-on-plug trucks, NAXJA warns the expensive coil rail sometimes gets blamed for misfires it didn't cause. Rule out heat soak and plugs first.

4.0: 10.5 qt (9.9 L) per the 2001 manual quote; ExtremeTerrain lists 12 qt · IAT through 2000, HOAT for 2001 (ExtremeTerrain) Flush completely when changing coolant types. On 2000–01 trucks, a healthy cooling system is your best protection against a cracked 0331 head.

Dexron III/Mercon per the 2001 owner's manual quote (ExtremeTerrain lists ATF+4) · 4 qt drain-and-fill, 8 qt with filter Do a pan drop and filter change, not a pressure flush. Check the throttle-valve cable adjustment if shifts are harsh or late.
AX-15: 3.32 qt 75W-90 GL-3/GL-4 (not GL-5) · AX-5: 3.3 qt same · NV3550: 2.1 qt Mopar 04874464AA or equivalent NAXJA notes some owner's manuals wrongly list GL-5 for the Aisin boxes.
NP231: 2.2 pt (1.0 L) · NP242: 2.85 pt (1.3 L) · Dexron III/Mercon or ATF+3/ATF+4 If it pops out of 4WD or is hard to shift back to 2WD, the case may be worn.
2.5 pt (1.2 L) SAE 75W-90 Low-pinion on 2000–01 trucks, high-pinion before that. Check the inner axle seals if the knuckles are wet with gear oil.
Dana 35: 3.5 pt (1.66 L) · 8.25: 4.4 pt (2.0 L) · SAE 75W-90 (75W-140 synthetic suggested for towing) · add 4 oz friction modifier with Trac-Lok Read the tag. ABS trucks have the Dana 35.
297x/760 series (1996 and later; check earlier ABS/non-ABS sizes) Turn each front wheel to full lock and check the axle-shaft U-joints for play or rust bleeding from the caps.
Belt by year and accessory layout OffroadXtreme says to check pulley alignment: bent pulleys suggest an overtightened belt and tired bearings.
Confirm it switches on at idle Idle for 5–10 minutes and confirm the fan runs. The assemblies differ for 1987–96 and 1997–2001.
Brake fluid per the master-cylinder cap [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Larger tires may need more brake-pedal effort. Rear drums on most XJs need adjusting and fresh hardware.
Power-steering fluid [CONFIRM TYPE IN MANUAL] Check the box for seepage, and check the unibody around the box mount for cracks.

YJ The first Wrangler, with square headlights and leaf springs. Track bars and anti-roll bars made it more civil than the CJ. The Wrangler that dared to have square headlights, and spent thirty years being forgiven for it. Under the controversial face it's a wider, calmer CJ-7 on leaf springs, and from 1991 it has the 4.0 straight-six. Buy that one, check the frame, and enjoy the cheapest ticket t

t: Fix the vacuum front-axle disconnect (or convert to cable)
x: 4WD light stays off, the front axle won't drive in 4H, or it engages and drops out with a clunk under load at speed. Hand vacuum pump with gauge · vacuum hose and connectors · check valve · gasket for the disconnect cover.

t: Replace the clutch and internal slave cylinder (early YJs)
x: Sinking or spongy clutch pedal, fluid loss from the clutch reservoir, a slipping clutch after fluid has soaked the disc, and fluid at the bottom of the bellhousing. Transmission jack · flare-nut wrenches · clutch alignment tool · torque wrench · brake washer (treat old linings as if they contain asbestos) · DOT 3/4 fluid.

t: Rebuild the 4.2's Carter BBD feedback carburetor (1987–90)
x: Stalling, flooding, hunting idle, loss of power or running hot. Many of these are vacuum leaks or ignition faults rather than the carburetor itself. T-gauge · hand vacuum pump · timing light · carb cleaner · alcohol · thread locker · Mopar or Echlin/NAPA premium rebuild kit (Ludel's preference).

t: Replace leaf springs, shackles and bushings
x: Sagging or uneven ride height, clunks over bumps, cracked or squeezed-out bushings, broken leaves and rusted shackles. Jack stands · floor jack · press or vise for bushings · wire brush · grease · torque wrench · new U-bolts.

t: Replace the rear main seal (4.0 / 4.2 six)
x: Oil dripping from where the engine meets the bellhousing, and an oily transmission and crossmember. Rule out the valve cover and oil pan gaskets first, because oil runs downhill. Pick · thin punch · torque wrench · RTV · oil pan gasket · new oil and filter.

t: Cut out and replace rusted floor pans
x: Soft, flaking or holed metal under the driver's carpet, water in the footwell, and rust around the seat and roll-bar mounts. Cut-off wheel · grinder · MIG welder · clamps · seam sealer · primer and paint.

t: Chase down front-end shimmy and worn steering
x: A violent side-to-side shake after a bump at around 45 mph, wandering, or a clunk when you turn the wheel with the engine off. Pry bar · floor jack and stands · torque wrench · helper.

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: A stock YJ usually takes 30-inch tires on stock rims without trouble. Four Wheel Trends says 31x10.50s can be squeezed on, but they may need wheels with different backspacing and can still rub, so don't wheel that setup hard without a lift.

Most buyers want a 1991–1995 truck with the fuel-injected 4.0 six. Hagerty calls it often the most desirable engine and says it commands a larger premium over the four. For 1987–90, Hagerty says the four- and six-cylinder versions differ by only a few hundred dollars in #3 condition.

t: Why does the YJ have square headlights?
x: Neither Wikipedia nor Hagerty gives an official reason. Wikipedia says only that the rectangular lamps set it apart from the round-eyed CJs. The TJ brought round headlights back for 1997. Owners who can't live with them fit round-headlight conversion kits.

t: My 4WD light won't come on. Is the transfer case broken?
x: Probably not. The YJ front axle is engaged by a vacuum motor, and Quadratec says dry-rotted, cracked or disconnected vacuum lines are the usual culprit. Test the system with a hand vacuum pump before buying parts, or convert to a cable-operated disconnect.

t: Should I avoid the Peugeot gearbox?
x: Six-cylinder YJs from 1987–89 could have the Peugeot BA-10/5 five-speed, which ExtremeTerrain describes as historically unreliable. Wikipedia lists the Aisin AX-15 behind the 4.2 from 1989, and the AX-15 stayed with the 4.0 through 1995. Four-cylinder trucks use the AX-5.
The NP207 was used on 1987 YJs only, and ExtremeTerrain calls it a poor unit. The NP231, used from 1988 onward, is the stronger and far better-supported case. A 1988–95 YJ will have the NP231.

t: Which years have the internal clutch slave cylinder?
x: Sources disagree. 4WD Mechanix says 1987–92 YJs used a slave cylinder built into the release bearing and that 1993 brought the external slave and pivot arm used in the TJ. Wikipedia dates the move outside the bellhousing to 1994, and Advance Adapters lists its internal-bearing hose kit for 1987–93. Treat 1993 as either, and look for an external slave on the bellhousing. The internal type means pul

t: What fluids do the axles and transfer case take?
x: Quadratec's factory-based chart lists GL-5 80W-90 or 75W-140 synthetic for the Dana 30, Dana 35 and Dana 44, with 4 oz of limited-slip additive for a Trac-Lok. ExtremeTerrain recommends 75W-140 in the rear for warm-weather towing.
