The NP231 takes automatic transmission fluid (ExtremeTerrain lists ATF+3 or ATF+4); Quadratec's chart gives 2.2 pints for the NP231 and 4.4 pints for the NP207. Haynes'

t: Can the 4.2's carburetor be made reliable?
x: Yes. Moses Ludel's 4WD Mechanix guide says the Carter BBD can be reliable when rebuilt to factory specs, and that a clogged fuel filter, a weak mechanical pump or a vacuum leak can mimic carburetor faults. He calls Mopar's multi-point injection conversion the bigger upgrade.

t: Is a YJ a good investment?
x: Hagerty puts a median #3-condition YJ at about $8,100, against $9,900 for an earlier CJ-7. Its Hagerty Vehicle Rating is 86 and climbing while the CJ's has fallen, although Hagerty says the rating is not a predictor of future collectability. Renegades bring the most, followed by Saharas and Islanders.

t: What's the difference between the Sahara, Islander and Renegade?
x: The Sahara (from 1988) included most options, with body-color flares, green trail-cloth seats and fog lamps. The Islander (1988–93) had sunset graphics and body-color flares and steps. The Renegade Decor Group (October 1990–94) added the 4.0, 8-inch alloy wheels and a widebody look.

t: Springs & Suspension — Old Man Emu (ARB), Quadratec — YJ lift kits & suspension, Warrior Products
x: Fresh leaf packs and urethane bushings transform a tired YJ, and a mild lift clears 31s. Spring-over-axle conversions are the classic path to bigger tires.

t: Axle Disconnect & Steering — JKS Posi-Lok PSL900 (ExtremeTerrain), Quadratec — YJ steering & brakes
x: A cable-operated front-axle disconnect removes the vacuum system that strands so many YJs in 2WD.

t: Gears & Lockers — Yukon Gear & Axle, ARB USA (Air Lockers), Quadratec — YJ driveline
x: Bigger tires need lower gears, and a locker turns the YJ's short wheelbase into a proper crawler.

t: Transmission & Engine Swaps — Advance Adapters, Novak Conversions
x: Replacing a Peugeot BA-10 or dropping a 4.0 into a four-cylinder truck is well-trodden ground, with adapters and mounts off the shelf.

t: Bumpers & Winches — Warn, Quadratec — YJ bumpers, Rugged Ridge
x: The factory bumpers are thin. A steel bumper with a winch mount is the first piece of armor most YJs get.

t: Armor & Skids — Quadratec — YJ armor & protection
x: Rocker guards and skid plates protect the tub and the low-slung transfer case.

t: Tops & Doors — Quadratec — YJ soft tops
x: Half doors, a fresh soft top or a hardtop: the YJ is still a convertible at heart.

SAE 10W-30 (Quadratec); ExtremeTerrain lists 10W-30 or 5W-30 · ≈4 qt (2.5) / 6 qt (4.0, 4.2) with filter (Quadratec) Drain-plug torque: ExtremeTerrain's TJ-era table gives 25 ft-lb for the 2.5 and 4.0 [CONFIRM IN MANUAL for your YJ]. ExtremeTerrain lists separate filters for 87–93 and 91–06 engines, so check which one yours takes.
Engine air filter and PCV filter/valve On the 4.2, Ludel lists the PCV valve and air cleaner among the first checks before blaming the carburetor.

Plug torque [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]: ExtremeTerrain's 1997–2006 table gives 27 ft-lb for the 2.5 and 4.0; no YJ-specific figure verified Both the 4.2 and 4.0 in the YJ use a distributor. Haynes lists inspecting the plug wires, cap and rotor on 2003-and-earlier models, so do them with the plugs.

Carter BBD feedback carburetor · mechanical fuel pump Ludel says a clogged filter, a weak mechanical pump or a vacuum leak can mimic carburetor faults. Replace brittle vacuum hose before rebuilding anything.

50/50 antifreeze and water (ExtremeTerrain) · ≈9 qt (2.5), 10.5 qt (4.0 and 4.2) (Quadratec chart) · antifreeze type [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Inspect the radiator, hoses and fan clutch while you're there. ExtremeTerrain lists a fan clutch that fits all YJs.

75W-90 GL-3 or GL-4 for the AX-5 and AX-15 (ExtremeTerrain) · ≈3.3 qt AX-5/AX-15, 5.2 pints BA-10/5 (Quadratec chart) [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Retailer charts disagree slightly on AX-15 capacity (3.25–3.32 qt), so fill to the bottom of the fill hole. Haynes lists a 30,000-mile change.

Mopar ATF of the type on the dipstick or in the manual [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] · total capacity 8.3 qt TF999, 17.1 pints 32RH, 7 qt 30RH (Quadratec chart); a pan drop takes much less Change the pan filter at the same time. ExtremeTerrain's TJ table gives 35 in-lb for the 30RH/32RH filter screws [CONFIRM IN MANUAL for YJ].

ATF (ExtremeTerrain lists ATF+3 or ATF+4 for the NP231) · NP231 2.2 pints, NP207 4.4 pints (Quadratec chart) · fill until it runs out of the fill hole ExtremeTerrain's TJ table gives 15–25 ft-lb for NP231 drain and fill plugs [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]. Inspect the output seals: Quadratec lists them among common leaks.

GL-5 80W-90 or 75W-140 synthetic · +4 oz limited-slip additive for Trac-Lok (Quadratec chart) · Dana 30 2.5 pt, Dana 35 3.5 pt, Dana 44 4.0 pt (Quadratec chart) [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Cover bolts take 30 ft-lb in ExtremeTerrain's TJ-era table for the same Dana axles [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]. Check the Dana 30 disconnect housing and pinion seals for leaks.
Shift motor, check valve, reserve tank and hoses Quadratec lists dry-rotted or cracked vacuum lines as the usual cause of a YJ that won't engage 4WD.
DOT 3 (ExtremeTerrain); Ludel uses DOT 4 in the clutch for heat resistance The clutch shares brake fluid type. On 1987–92 trucks a falling clutch reservoir points to the internal slave.
Lubricate chassis components (Haynes) Grease the steering joints and driveshaft U-joints, and check the shackles and spring bushings for cracks.
Firewall ground straps and battery terminals Quadratec suggests cleaning the grounds first when you see flickering lights, jumping gauges or intermittent starting.

TJ Coil springs and round headlights return on the short wheelbase. Many people think it's the best-riding classic Wrangler. Round headlights back, leaf springs gone, the 4.0 straight-six carried over, and from 2003 a Rubicon with lockers from the factory. For many people the TJ is the sweet spot of the whole Wrangler line. Just check the frame before you fall in love.

t: Cure death wobble: track bar, ball joints and tie rods
x: Uncontrollable side-to-side shaking of the front end, usually triggered by a bump at around 45 mph and stopped only by slowing right down. Helper · pry bar · floor jack and stands · torque wrench · factory service manual torque specs.

t: Replace the oil pump drive assembly (OPDA)
x: A chirping 'laughing monkey' noise from the top of the engine, most often on 2005–06 4.0s. Left alone, the drive can seize and stop the oil pump. Socket set · factory service manual (TDC and sync procedure) · paint marker · scan tool if available.

Oil weeping from the joint between the engine and bellhousing, and an oily crossmember and transmission. Rule out the valve cover, oil-filter adapter and pan gasket first. Pick · thin punch · O2-sensor wrench · torque wrench · RTV · jack and stands.
Coolant smell, green crust at the top tank seam, and eventually a split tank spraying coolant over the engine. Drain pan · hand tools · thread sealant · distilled water · correct coolant.

A ticking exhaust leak that's loudest from cold and may fade as the engine warms. Drivingline says it's more common on 1997–2000 trucks and is something you hear more than see. Extensions · wobble sockets · flex-head ratcheting wrenches · O2-sensor socket · anti-seize · Loctite.

t: Repair rusted rear lower control-arm mounts
x: Flaking, swollen or holed frame around the rear lower control-arm brackets, clunks from the rear, or a bracket that moves. Quadratec warns it can lead to structural failure. Floor jack and stands · grinder · cutting wheel · welder · primer, paint or POR-15 · torque wrench.

t: Fix a transfer case that won't shift (linkage bushings)
x: The shifter moves but the transfer case won't go into 4-Low, or the lever flops around. The rod has usually popped out of a worn plastic bushing. Pliers · small pry bar · grease.

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: Four Wheel Trends says the largest tire for a TJ on stock wheels and suspension is generally a 31x10.50, and that it usually allows full articulation. The Rubicon came from the factory on 31-inch LT245/75R16 Goodyear MT/Rs.

Get the 4.0 if you can. Drivingline strongly recommends the six, which makes 190 hp and 235 lb-ft from 2000 against 120 hp for the 2.5 and 147 hp for the 2.4. The fours are reliable but run out of power once you add bigger tires, and swapping in a 4.0 later costs about as much as a V8 swap.

It's the sound of a failing oil pump drive assembly (OPDA), flagged by Quadratec on 2005–06 4.0 TJs. The factory steel upper bushing is starved of oil, and if it seizes it can wreck the cam bearing and stop the oil pump. Replace it if there's no record it has been done.

t: What causes death wobble, and will a new stabilizer fix it?
x: Worn or loose steering and suspension parts cause it, most often the track bar and its bolts, and Off Road Xtreme singles out a loose lower track-bar bolt. Quadratec says a bigger steering stabilizer only masks the problem. Find and replace the part that moves, then align.

t: Is the Dana 35 rear axle really that bad?
x: Drivingline calls it 'junk' and says its C-clip design is unreliable in stock form, while the low-pinion Dana 30 front is fine up to about 35-inch tires. A factory Dana 44 rear was optional on the Sport and Sahara and standard on the Rubicon. Otherwise, budget 'a couple grand' for a bolt-in upgrade.

Dana 44 axles front and rear with 4.10 gears, air-actuated front and rear lockers, the NV241OR Rock-Trac transfer case with a 4.0:1 low range, 31-inch MT/R tires, 16-inch wheels and diamond-plate sill guards. RockCrawler reported a 65.92:1 crawl ratio. It was sold for 2003–06.

Drivingline says the AX-15 has notable synchro issues and the NV3550 that replaced it is stronger. Wikipedia lists the AX-15 for 1997–99, the NV3550 for 2000–04 and the six-speed NSG370 for 2005–06, though some sources say the six-speed arrived earlier. Fours used the AX-5 and, for 2003–04, the NV1500.

t: How much can a TJ tow?
x: Wikipedia lists 2,000 lb for the standard TJ and 3,500 lb for the long-wheelbase Unlimited.

Haynes says 2000-and-earlier Wranglers use conventional ethylene-glycol antifreeze, and 2001-and-later use Mopar's 5-year/100,000-mile HOAT coolant, both mixed 50/50. Capacity is about 9 qt for the fours and 10.5 qt for the 4.0.

t: What gear oil goes in the axles?
x: Haynes lists 75W-90 GL-5, or 75W-140 synthetic for towing, plus 4 oz of friction modifier for Trac-Lok. Quadratec and ExtremeTerrain's charts say the Rubicon's Dana 44s use 75W-140 synthetic.

t: Why does my TJ leak oil?
x: The usual spots on the 4.0 are the rear main seal, oil pan gasket, valve cover gasket and oil-filter adapter gasket. Off Road Xtreme notes the valve cover has many bolts and takes longer than expected. Drivingline says the two-piece rear main can be replaced without pulling the transmission.

The Unlimited, sold for 2004–06, stretches the TJ by 15 inches, 10 of them in the wheelbase (103.4 in versus 93.4 in). Drivingline says that adds cargo room and stability on steep trails, but the LJ costs more because it was built for only three model years.

t: Suspension Lift — Quadratec — TJ lift kits & suspension, MetalCloak, Rock Hard 4x4
x: The coil-sprung TJ responds well to a 2–4 inch lift, which clears 33s and gives it more flex. Plan on matching track bars and control arms as you go higher.

t: Rock Rails & Armor — Poison Spyder Customs, GenRight Off Road, Savvy Off Road, Quadratec — TJ armor & protection
x: The TJ's low tub corners and rockers are the first things to hit rocks. Rails, corner guards and a belly-up skid make the biggest difference.

t: Bumpers & Winches — Warn, Quadratec — TJ bumpers
x: A steel front bumper with a winch is cheap insurance on a short-wheelbase rig that wheels alone.

t: Gears, Lockers & Axles — Yukon Gear & Axle, ARB USA (Air Lockers), Quadratec — TJ driveline
x: Non-Rubicon TJs on bigger tires need lower gears and lockers, and the Dana 35 rear is usually the first thing to replace.

t: Engine & Transmission Swaps — Novak Conversions, Advance Adapters
x: Four-cylinder TJs get 4.0 or V8 swaps, and manual swaps and transfer-case upgrades are well documented.

t: Cooling — 4-row aluminum radiator, 97–06 TJ (ExtremeTerrain), Quadratec — TJ engine & fuel system
x: Off Road Xtreme recommends an all-aluminum radiator to replace the leak-prone plastic-tank original, especially as the 4.0 runs warm.

t: Tops & Recovery — Quadratec — TJ soft tops, Quadratec — TJ winches, recovery & safety gear
x: Drivingline prefers a soft top for weight and easy removal, and every trail TJ needs recovery points.

4.0: 6 qt with filter · 2.4: 4 qt · 10W-30 or 5W-30 (ExtremeTerrain) Drain-plug torque is 25 ft-lb (Haynes). Look for leaks at the oil-filter adapter gasket while you're under there, because it's a known 4.0 leak.
Oil pump drive / camshaft synchronizer Quadratec recommends replacing it proactively on 2005–06 trucks with no records. Listen for the 'laughing monkey' chirp at idle.
Engine air filter and PCV Quadratec lists aging throttle-position, crank and O2 sensors as causes of stalling and rough idle, so a fresh filter rules out the easy stuff first.
4.0 and 2.5: 27 ft-lb · 2.4: 132 in-lb (Haynes) Check the plug wires and coil while you're there.

1997–2000: ethylene glycol 50/50 · 2001–06: Mopar 5-yr/100k HOAT 50/50 · ≈9 qt (four), 10.5 qt (4.0) (Haynes) Inspect the plastic radiator end tanks for seam leaks. Quadratec says they often start around 100,000 miles.

AX-5/AX-15: SAE 75W-90 (Haynes: GL-3 for 1998 and later), ≈3.3 qt · NV3550: Mopar manual transmission fluid, about 2 bottles · NV1500: Mopar NV1500 lube, 4.8 pints · NSG370: 3.17 pints (Quadratec chart) [CONFIRM TYPE IN MANUAL] The NV3550 fill and drain plugs take a 17 mm Allen bit, and the oil-pan skid may need to come off (4x4xplor). Fine filings on the magnet are normal, but chunks are not.

2000 and earlier: Mopar ATF+3 · 2001 and later: ATF+4 · ≈4 qt pan drop (Haynes) Change the filter with the fluid. Filter screws take 35 in-lb (30RH/32RH) or 45 in-lb (42RLE) (Haynes). Drivingline calls the 42RLE heat-sensitive, so consider a cooler if you tow or crawl.

Mopar ATF+4 (Haynes) · NV241OR 4.2 pints (ExtremeTerrain chart) · fill until it runs out of the fill hole On a TJ the skid plate has to be lowered for a proper drain (4x4xplor). Plugs take 20 ft-lb (Haynes). Check the output seals and the shift-linkage bushings while you're there.

75W-90 GL-5; 75W-140 synthetic for towing · Rubicon Dana 44s: 75W-140 synthetic · +4 oz friction modifier for Trac-Lok (Haynes, Quadratec) Cover bolts take 30 ft-lb (Haynes). Drivingline says to check the Dana 30's pinion seal and U-joints.
Track bar and bolts, ball joints, tie-rod ends, drag link, stabilizer Torque the track-bar bolts to spec first. Off Road Xtreme says a loose lower bolt is the most common cause of death wobble.
DOT 3 (ExtremeTerrain) The TJ's external clutch slave shares brake fluid. Flush both.
Lubricate chassis components (Haynes) Grease the steering joints and driveshaft U-joints, and look over the control-arm bushings.

Rails, rear lower control-arm brackets, transfer-case crossmember, body mounts, footwells Quadratec warns rust at the rear lower arm brackets can cause structural failure. Clean and coat the frame inside and out before it gets there.

LJ TJ Unlimited The long-wheelbase TJ: more cargo room, a calmer ride and a short production run. The LJ is a TJ that went to the gym and grew ten inches of wheelbase, which turned out to be exactly the right number. Jeep sold it for barely two and a half model years and buyers mostly shrugged. Now everyone wants one, and the sellers know it.

t: Replace the oil pump drive assembly (2005–06 4.0)
x: A squeak or 'laughing monkey' chirp from the back of the engine, sometimes with a check-engine light. Left alone, Quadratec warns, OPDA failure can damage the engine. Socket set · factory service manual for TDC and indexing · scan tool to verify cam/crank sync · new camshaft position sensor (5149034AA for 2005–06 4.0) if the old one is suspect.

t: Repair rotted rear control-arm frame mounts
x: Flaking, swollen or holed frame around the rear lower control-arm brackets, the transfer-case crossmember or the central body mounts. Quadratec's correspondent found all three on a 1998 TJ with 190,000 miles. Welder · cutoff wheel and grinder · jack stands · floor jack · torque wrench · thread locker · rust-proof coating. Rust Buster sections are side- and year-specific (2003–06 differ from 1997–0

t: Hunt down death wobble and set toe in the driveway
x: Violent front-end shake after a bump, usually at 45–65 mph, that stops only when you slow right down. 13 mm and 15 mm sockets · tape measure · pipe wrench or locking pliers · a helper · torque wrench.

t: Replace the radiator before the plastic tank lets go
x: Coolant smell, green crust or seepage at the upper tank seam, often around 100,000 miles, and creeping temperatures on the trail. OffroadXtreme notes that the 4.0 runs hot and recommends an all-aluminum radiator. Drain pan · pliers for the hose clamps · line wrench for the cooler lines · funnel · coolant to the spec on the cap and in the owner's manual.

t: Replace a throttle position or crank sensor
x: Stalling, rough idle or random check-engine lights. Quadratec's example was a TJ throwing P0122 that stalled while driving; automatics rely on the TPS to run properly. Aging crankshaft-position, throttle-position and oxygen sensors are all common failures. 13 mm (or 1/2 in) socket for the battery · 5/16 in driver · 10 mm socket · T25 Torx · code reader.

t: Fix a transfer case that won't go into 4-Low
x: The lever moves but the transfer case won't fully engage 4-Low, or pops out of it. Quadratec says the factory 'Z-bar' linkage pops out of worn plastic bushings. Flat screwdriver or trim tool · pliers · wheel chocks.

t: Replace a front axle U-joint and unit bearing
x: A squeak that fades as speed rises, a vibration or bind on slow turns as if you were in 4WD, and visible play in the axle-shaft U-joint. Quadratec's correspondent found the hub was worn too once it was apart. 36 mm socket · big breaker bar · 13 mm sockets · press (strongly preferred) · snap-ring pliers · anti-seize · torque wrench.

t: Stop the rear main seal leak
x: Oil dripping from the joint between engine and transmission and a wet bottom of the bellhousing. Rule out the valve cover and oil-filter adapter gasket first, because oil runs downhill. Jack stands and floor jack (to lower the front axle if needed) · torque wrench · RTV per the factory manual · drain pan · factory service manual.

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: Jeep answered this itself: the Rubicon Unlimited left Toledo on LT245/75R16 tires, about 31 x 9.5 inches, on the stock-height suspension. A 31-inch tire of similar width on the right backspacing is the realistic unlifted ceiling. Going wider or taller usually means rubbing at full flex, and RealTruck's general Wrangler advice is that anything beyond stock-height comfort 'may cause rubbing during t

t: What's the difference between an LJ and a TJ?
x: The LJ has 10 more inches of wheelbase (103.4 in against 93.4 in), is about 15 inches longer overall, and has 2 more inches of rear legroom and 13 more inches of cargo length. It tows 3,500 lb instead of 2,000. Every LJ also got a Dana 44 rear axle (limited-slip on standard models, locking on the Rubicon), which many short TJs lacked.

About 47,000 across 2004–2006, roughly 20 percent of Wrangler sales in that period, per Jalopnik's tally from forum and sales data. The 2005 Sahara Edition Unlimited Rubicon was a numbered run of 1,000.

t: Why are LJs so expensive now?
x: There's never been a replacement. It's the only factory Wrangler with two doors, a long wheelbase, coil springs and the 4.0 straight six, and the Rubicon version adds lockers at both ends. Hagerty says late TJs, 'especially the Unlimited Rubicon,' have been the priciest TJs on the market.

t: Which years and drivetrains should I look for?
x: 2005–06 brought the NSG370 six-speed manual. Those years also need the OPDA checked. The 2005–06 Rubicon Unlimited is the one with front and rear Dana 44s, air lockers and the 4:1 Rock-Trac. A 2004 or non-Rubicon LJ still has the Dana 44 rear and is a better starting point for a build than a Dana 35 TJ.
Jeep rated the LJ at 3,500 lb, against 2,000 lb for the short-wheelbase TJ.

Quadratec's factory-based chart gives the 4.0 6 qt of 10W-30 with a filter and 10.5 qt of coolant. The 42RLE takes ATF+4, 4 qt at a service fill. The NSG370 takes 3.17 pints. The NV231 takes 2.2 pints and the NV241 Rock-Trac 4.2 pints of ATF+4. The Dana 30 takes 2.5 pints and a Dana 44 4.0 pints of GL-5 80W-90 or 75W-140 synthetic. Rubicons specify 75W-140 synthetic, and a Trac-Lok rear needs 4 oz

The oil pump drive assembly on 2005–06 4.0 engines can wear. The warning sign owners describe is a 'laughing monkey' noise, and if it's ignored the engine can be damaged. Replacements with a relocated seal are cheap; the indexing to keep the cam sensor in sync is the fiddly part.

t: What fuel economy and range should I expect?
x: Jeep's 2005–06 TJ spec sheet lists 16/20 mpg (city/highway) for the 4.0 with either transmission, on the short-wheelbase truck. The LJ carries the same 19-gallon tank, according to owners on RME4x4. Bigger tires, a lift and a roof load cost several mpg.

t: What about the low belly and the rear overhang?
x: Jalopnik flags both. The departure angle is 27.7 degrees, and the transfer-case skid hangs low, so a high-clearance or 'tummy tuck' skid is a common first mod. Rough Country's 1126 is listed for 2003–06 TJ and Unlimited.

t: Do I need a slip-yoke eliminator if I lift it?
x: Quadratec says lift-kit makers strongly recommend an SYE and a CV driveshaft above 2 inches of lift, and treat it as required at 4 inches or more, to cure vibration and stop the slip yoke pulling out of the transfer case.

t: Belly Skid / Tummy Tuck — Rough Country 1126 high-clearance skid, 2003–06 TJ & Unlimited (Quadratec), GenRight Off Road
x: The LJ's low transfer-case skid is the first thing to drag. A high-clearance skid tucks it up into the frame.

t: Suspension Lift — MetalCloak, Quadratec — TJ/LJ lift kits
x: 2–4 inches clears 33s. Above 2 inches, budget for an adjustable track bar, alignment correction and an SYE with a CV driveshaft.

t: Lockers — ARB Air Locker, Quadratec — TJ lockers
x: Non-Rubicon LJs have only a rear limited slip. Selectable lockers turn an LJ Sport into most of a Rubicon.

t: Armor: Bumpers, Corners, Sliders — Rock Hard 4x4, GenRight Off Road, Quadratec — TJ front bumpers
x: The long rear overhang and the plastic corners are what get hurt. Steel rear corners and rocker sliders are standard trail kit.
Rust Buster sells bolt-up-and-weld replacement sections for the TJ's known rot zones.

t: Axle Truss & Protection — Quadratec — TJ axle truss and protection
x: Bigger tires bend the Dana 30 front tubes first. Trusses and diff guards are cheap insurance.
SAE 10W-30 · 6 qt with filter (4.0 L) Look at the oil-filter adapter gasket and the rear main seal while you're under there: both are common 4.0 leak points.
Updated OPDA with relocated seal Listen for the 'laughing monkey' squeal; the replacement must be indexed to keep the cam sensor in sync.
Factory airbox element [CONFIRM part fitment for your intake]
6 plugs (Crown 56041402AB listed for 1999–06 TJ & Unlimited) Check the plug wires and coil while you're there.
10.5 qt (4.0 L); coolant type per the cap/manual [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Inspect the radiator's plastic end tanks for seepage at the upper seams, a known 100k-mile failure.
Crown 4060882 listed for 2000–06 TJ & Unlimited 6-cyl Spin the tensioner and idler pulleys while the belt is off.
ATF+4 · 4 qt service fill A service fill only replaces part of the fluid. Do two drain-and-fills rather than a high-pressure flush.
3.17 pints; Mopar Manual Transmission Lubricant (as specified for the NSG370) [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] The NSG370 uses a hydraulic clutch with a dual-mass flywheel. Check the clutch fluid (DOT 3) too.
NV231: 2.2 pints · NV241 Rock-Trac: 4.2 pints · ATF+4 Check the output seals and the shifter-linkage bushings at the same time.

Dana 30: 2.5 pints · Dana 44: 4.0 pints · GL-5 80W-90 or 75W-140 synthetic; Rubicon 75W-140; Trac-Lok rear needs 4 oz of limited-slip additive Standard LJs have a limited-slip Dana 44 rear, so don't forget the friction modifier.
Greasable 1310 driveshaft joints · axle-shaft U-joints Check for play by hand. A front axle U-joint that binds on slow turns is due.
DOT 3 Manual LJs share the brake fluid type in the clutch hydraulics.
Track bar, tie rods, drag link, ball joints, bushings Re-torque the front-end hardware. Set toe to about 1/16 in in, then get a proper alignment.
Rear lower control-arm mounts, transfer-case crossmember, center body mounts Clean, treat and oil the frame inside and out. Catching surface rust now saves a welder later.

JK A bigger, wider and more refined two-door Wrangler. In the US it had V6 power: a 3.8 at first, then the 3.6-liter Pentastar from 2012. The JK took the Wrangler from a summer toy to a computer-controlled, power-windowed mainstream hit, and the two-door is the version that kept the old-school wheelbase. Buy a 2012-on Pentastar unless you enjoy merging slowly. Then check the ball joints, because J

t: Replace the Pentastar oil filter housing (2012–18)
x: Oil (and sometimes coolant) pooling in the valley between the cylinder banks, a burning smell, slow oil loss. You often won't see drips on the ground until the leak is bad. 27 mm and 19 mm deep sockets · E8 external Torx · 24 mm cap socket · inch-pound torque wrench · 8, 10 and 13 mm sockets · magnet and pick · shop vac.

t: Cure death wobble: track bar, tie rods and steering
x: Violent side-to-side shaking of the front end after a bump at 45–65 mph that won't stop until you slow right down. Helper · pry bar · torque wrench · sockets · tape measure.

Vertical play at the top and bottom of the tire, wandering, uneven tire wear, and wobble after bumps. Quadratec says factory JK ball joints 'often wear surprisingly quickly', especially on heavy, lifted trucks. Ball-joint press and JK adapter set · pickle fork or tie-rod puller · large sockets · torque wrench · new cotter pins.

Play when you rock the tire with the truck in the air, a growl that changes with steering, and, as part of the death-wobble checklist, looseness in the front end. Large axle-nut socket · breaker bar · torque wrench · anti-seize · hammer.

t: Fix a ticking exhaust manifold (broken bolts)
x: A tick-tick-tick on cold start that quiets as the engine warms, from a leak at the rear of a manifold. Quadratec says the rear manifold bolts on both the 3.8 and 3.6 are 'notorious for snapping'. Penetrating oil · sockets and extensions · left-hand drill bits and extractors (or a welder) · thread chaser · torque wrench.

Airbag warning light, horn or steering-wheel buttons that don't work, and cruise or audio controls dropping out. Quadratec lists it with the TIPM as the usual JK electrical culprits. On 2007–10 trucks, check recall 16V-290 first: Chrysler recalled the clockspring because dust contamination could stop the driver's airbag from deploying. Torx and metric sockets · steering-wheel puller if it's stuck

t: Change the spark plugs (and don't over-torque the Pentastar)
x: Misfires, rough idle and lost economy, or simply a truck past the interval. ExtremeTerrain quotes Chrysler's interval as 102,000 miles [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]. ExtremeTerrain suggests pulling one plug for inspection at 60,000 on modified, trail-used trucks. 5/8 in spark plug socket · extensions · 3/8 in torque wrench · gap gauge · dielectric grease.

t: Gusset or truss a bent front axle
x: Camber you can't align out, odd tire wear or changed steering on a JK running 35s or bigger. Quadratec warns that heavy tires and hard use can bend the axle C's where the ball joints sit. Welder · grinder · clamps · axle stands · rust-proof coating.

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: 33 inches is the usual answer, with caveats. ExtremeTerrain says many JK owners fit 33s on a stock suspension, but fender rubbing will probably show up off-road at full flex, and width matters as much as height. On JK-Forum, owners of stock two-door Rubicons report 285/75R17s clearing on pavement, with rubbing on the control arms at full lock that adjusting the steering stops can cure. Not every w

The 3.6 Pentastar (2012–18) makes 285 hp against the 3.8's 202, and comes with a five-speed automatic instead of a four-speed. Quadratec says the 2012 switch ended the JK's 'rolling brick' era. The 3.8 is simpler and cheaper to buy. On a Pentastar, budget for the oil filter housing.

t: What's the Pentastar cylinder head problem?
x: Some early 2012–13 Wrangler Pentastars had faulty left cylinder heads. Chrysler's bulletin describes excessive cylinder leakage showing up as misfire codes (P0300, P0302, P0304 or P0306); owners also reported a tick from the left bank. Chrysler replaced heads under warranty, fitted redesigned heads to new engines from 2012 (AutoGuide), and in 2014 extended coverage on affected heads to 10 years or

t: What causes death wobble and how do I fix it?
x: Looseness or wear in the front end, most often the track bar, tie-rod ends, ball joints, control-arm bushings or wheel bearings, usually set off by a tire imbalance or a bump at 45–65 mph. A stabilizer only masks it. Find and replace the worn part, torque the hardware and align the truck.

t: Is the Rubicon worth it over a Sport?
x: If you'll wheel it, yes. You get Dana 44s at both ends instead of a Dana 30 front, front and rear electric lockers, a 4:1 Rock-Trac instead of 2.72:1, 4.10 gears and the electronic sway-bar disconnect. Retrofitting all of that to a Sport is a big, expensive job. A Moab or Willys Wheeler looks the part but keeps the 2.72:1 transfer case.

t: How much can a 2-door JK tow?
x: 2,000 lb, against 3,500 lb for the four-door Unlimited, per Quadratec's 2012 spec summary. Maximum payload is about 1,000 lb.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: The EPA rated a 2012 Pentastar two-door at 17 mpg city and 21 highway. The tank holds 18.6 gallons. Lifts, 33–35 inch tires and steel bumpers cost several mpg.

Per ExtremeTerrain's JK chart: 3.8 and 3.6 engines take 6 qt of 5W-20. Coolant is HOAT for the 3.8 and 2012 3.6 (about 13 qt), and OAT for 2013-on 3.6s (10.5 qt). The 42RLE takes ATF+4 (4 qt service fill), the W5A580/NAG1 ATF+4 (5.3 qt service fill), and the NSG370 1.6 qt of Mopar Manual Transmission Lubricant. The NV241 takes 2.1 qt of ATF+4. The Dana 30 front takes 2.1 pints, the Dana 44 front 2

t: How often should I change the oil?
x: Quadratec cites Jeep's 8,000 miles or six months for the Pentastar, and never more than 10,000. Severe use (towing, dust, off-road) shortens it. Mopar specifies oil meeting MS-6395. Note that the oil filter changed in 2014, so buy the right one.

t: Why does it tick at cold start?
x: Usually broken rear exhaust manifold bolts letting the manifold leak until it heats up and seals. It's very common on both the 3.8 and the 3.6.

t: What are the TIPM and clockspring problems?
x: The TIPM is the JK's central power-distribution module. With a failing clockspring, it's the usual source of airbag lights, dead steering-wheel controls, fuel-pump problems and wipers with a mind of their own. Water in the cabin makes it worse.

t: Suspension Lift — AEV (American Expedition Vehicles), MetalCloak, Quadratec — JK lift kits
x: 2.5–3.5 inches with proper geometry (track bar, control arms or brackets) clears 35s without inviting death wobble.

t: Ball Joints & Steering — Dana Spicer performance ball joints (Quadratec), Synergy Manufacturing HD ball joints (Quadratec)
x: Heavy-duty ball joints, tie rods and a correctly sized track bar are the cure for a front end that wears out under big tires.

t: Axle Armor — Quadratec — JK axle truss & protection
x: The Dana 30 front is the weak link once you go to 35s. Gussets and a truss stop the C's bending.

t: Bumpers & Winch — AEV, WARN, Quadratec — JK front bumpers
x: Steel bumpers with a winch mount are the JK's signature mod; the Call of Duty and Moab editions came with AEV-style ones from the factory.

t: Rock Sliders — Rock Hard 4x4, Quadratec — JK rocker guards
x: The factory rock rails on Rubicons are fine. Other trims have nothing to protect the sills.
Non-Rubicon JKs rarely got a factory locker. Air lockers add front and rear.

t: Aluminum Oil Filter Housing — Mishimoto MMOFH-JK-12 (ExtremeTerrain), Dorman 926-959 (ExtremeTerrain)
x: The permanent fix for the Pentastar's plastic housing.

5W-20 meeting MS-6395 · 6 qt (3.8 and 3.6) The Pentastar's cartridge filter lives in the top-mounted housing (24 mm cap; don't yank the filter or you can break the pressure-relief valve). The filter changed for 2014.
Plastic housing/cooler in the engine valley Oil or coolant pooled under the plenum means it's time for the aluminum upgrade.
Factory airbox element and cabin filter Dusty trail use clogs the air filter fast.
3.8: Champion RE14PLP5, 0.050 in, 12 lb-ft per ExtremeTerrain [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] · 3.6: Champion RER8ZWYCB4, 0.043 in, 13 lb-ft The 3.8 uses plug wires; the 3.6 is coil-on-plug.
3.8 and 2012 3.6: HOAT, ≈13 qt · 2013-on 3.6: OAT 10-yr/150k, 10.5 qt Don't mix HOAT and OAT; check which one is in the tank before topping up.
ATF+4 · 42RLE: 4 qt service fill · W5A580 (NAG1): 5.3 qt service fill A service fill only changes part of the fluid; do it twice rather than flushing.
Mopar Manual Transmission Lubricant · 1.6 qt The clutch hydraulics use DOT 3 brake fluid; check the clutch master level.
ATF+4 · 2.1 qt Same fluid for Command-Trac and Rock-Trac.
80W-90 (75W-140 for towing) · Dana 30: 2.1 pt · Dana 44 front: 2.7 pt · Dana 44 rear: 4.75 pt · Trac-Lok: add 4 oz limited-slip additive You can check JK diff levels without pulling the cover.
1350-series joints Lifted JKs chew through rear driveshaft joints. Check for play by hand.
Track bar, tie rods, drag link, ball joints, unit bearings Re-torque the hardware and align. This is your death-wobble insurance.
Power Steering Fluid +4 (ATF+4 acceptable) Big tires work the steering box and pump hard.
DOT 3 The same reservoir type also feeds the clutch on manual trucks.

JK Unlimited JKU The first four-door Wrangler, and the one that took Jeep from niche toy to family car. The Jeep that let Wrangler people have children, friends and luggage at the same time. The four-door JK turned a toy into a family car and an overland platform, and by 2017 three in four new Wranglers for sale were four-doors. Get the Pentastar, check the front end, and pack lighter than you thi

t: Chase down death wobble (track bar first)
x: Violent side-to-side shaking of the steering wheel and front axle, usually at 45–65 mph after a bump or bridge seam, which stops only when you slow right down. Helper · torque wrench · large sockets · pry bar · floor jack and stands · paint pen to mark bolts.

t: Replace the Pentastar oil filter housing / cooler (2012–2018)
x: Oil pooling in the valley under the intake, running over the back of the engine and dripping from the bellhousing. Sometimes coolant leaks too. E8 external-Torx socket · 27 mm and 19 mm deep sockets · inch-pound torque wrench · hose clamp pliers · trim tool · shop vac · Dorman 926-876 aluminum housing (as used by Curbside Classic).

A ticking or puffing noise at cold start that quietens as the engine warms, a smell of exhaust in the engine bay, and soot marks at the manifold-to-head joint. Penetrating oil · long extensions and swivels · stud extractor · torque wrench · new manifold studs and nuts.

t: Press in new front ball joints
x: Clunks over bumps, wandering, uneven tire wear, or play when you rock a lifted wheel top to bottom. Worn joints can contribute to death wobble. Ball-joint press and JK adapter set · axle-nut socket · breaker bar · torque wrench · pickle fork or hammer for the tapers.

t: Replace a front hub and bearing
x: A growl that changes with speed or while turning, play when you rock the wheel at 12 and 6 o'clock, or an ABS light from a damaged sensor. Large axle-nut socket · breaker bar · torque wrench · wire brush · anti-seize for the hub-to-knuckle face.

t: Truss a front axle before it bends (or after)
x: Toe that won't stay in alignment, inside-edge tire wear, or a visibly bent tube after a hard hit. It's common on lifted trucks running 35s and up on the factory axle. MIG or stick welder · grinder · straightedge or axle-alignment check · paint.

t: Re-spring the rear for an overland load
x: A rear end that sags below the front, bottoms out on washboard, or sits on the bump stops with a full load of water, fuel and gear. Floor jack and frame stands · sockets · torque wrench · spring compressor not usually needed on JK rear coils.

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: 33s. JK-Forum owners agree that most 285/70R17s (about 33 inches) fit on stock wheels, at stock height, with the stock bump stops. Expect light rubbing at full lock and at full flex, where they touch the flares, liners and sometimes the front sway bar. A steering-stop washer and the right backspacing help. ExtremeTerrain says 35s need at least a 2–3-inch lift, the right wheel offset and possibly n

The 3.6 Pentastar (2012–2018) by a mile: 285 hp against 202, plus a five-speed automatic instead of the four-speed. The 3.8 is known for burning oil, intake-gasket leaks and cracked exhaust manifolds. Driving Line suggests a 2013 or later truck for daily use. A cheap 3.8 can still make a good trail rig if you accept its limits.

t: How much can a JK Unlimited tow?
x: 3,500 lb, with a 350-lb tongue weight for the 2017 Rubicon. That's against 2,000 lb for the two-door. For heavy towing the factory manual calls for synthetic 75W-140 in the rear axle.

Less than you think. Quadratec lists 1,067–1,301 lb for 2012 four-doors depending on trim. For 2017, KBB lists 880–1,000 lb and Cars.com gives the Rubicon 1,178 lb against a 5,700-lb GVWR. Your door-jamb sticker is the number that counts, and a fully built overland JKU often exceeds it.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: The EPA rated the 2017 Unlimited 3.6 at 16 mpg city and 20 highway with the automatic (16/21 manual), and KBB lists a 22.5-gallon tank. Bigger tires, a lift and a rack all bring that down.

3.6 Pentastar: six quarts of 5W-20 meeting Chrysler MS-6395, or 5W-30 in hot climates. The filter is a cartridge under a cap on top of the engine, and Quadratec notes the filter changed for 2014, so buy for your year. The 3.8 also takes about six quarts with the filter, in 5W-20 or 5W-30; check the oil filler cap.

Every Rubicon has electric Tru-Lok lockers front and rear. Per Wikipedia, a rear locker was optional on X and Sahara for 2007, then only on select X models for 2008–2009; later the only non-Rubicon options were the 2015 Wrangler X and the 2016 75th Anniversary Edition. A Trac-Lok limited slip was the usual non-Rubicon option.

t: Will the Dana 30 front axle handle 35s?
x: Driving Line rates the non-Rubicon Dana 30 at about 35-inch tires. The tubes and C-ends can bend with big tires or hard use, and that's true of the Rubicon's Dana 44 too. Trusses help prevent it; replacement housings from Dynatrac or Currie are the cure.

t: What do I do if it gets death wobble?
x: Grip the wheel, don't brake hard, and slow down smoothly until it stops. Then fix the cause: start with the track bar, then the tie-rod ends, drag link, ball joints, control-arm bushings and wheel bearings, and check tire balance. A new steering stabilizer only masks it, and an alignment comes last.

In June 2014 Chrysler extended the warranty on the left cylinder head of some 2011–2013 3.6 V6s (2012–2013 on the Wrangler) to 10 years or 150,000 miles after cylinder-leakage misfires. Dealers replaced the head where testing showed excessive leakage, and AutoGuide reported that redesigned heads went into production in 2012. The extension has now run out, so a 2012–2013 truck with a misfire on tha

t: Is the four-door worse off-road than the two-door?
x: On tight, technical trails the 116-inch wheelbase gives up breakover angle and turning circle compared with the 95.4-inch two-door. Everywhere else it rides better and carries more. Driving Line says the two are mechanically nearly identical and recommends driving both before you choose.

t: Suspension Lift — AEV — DualSport suspension, Teraflex, MetalCloak, ExtremeTerrain — JK lift kits
x: 2.5–3.5 inches with matched coils and shocks clears 35s and can be specced for a loaded overland truck. Correct the track-bar and control-arm geometry, or death wobble will remind you.

t: Steering & Track Bars — Synergy Manufacturing, JKS Manufacturing, Teraflex Monster HD front adjustable track bar (Quadratec)
x: Heavier tie rods, drag links and adjustable track bars keep big tires pointed where you want them and keep the front end tight.

t: Axles & Gears — Dynatrac, Yukon ring and pinion kit, JK Dana 30 front (Quadratec), ExtremeTerrain — JK ring and pinion gears
x: Regear after going to 35s, especially on 3.8 trucks. Then truss the front, or replace it with something stronger.

t: Rock Sliders & Armor — DV8 Offroad SRSOTB-06 rock slider steps, JK Unlimited (Quadratec), GenRight, Poison Spyder, ExtremeTerrain — JK rocker armor
x: The long wheelbase makes the rockers the first thing to hit on a ledge.

t: Roof Racks & Storage — Rhino-Rack Pioneer platform with Maximus-3 brackets, JK Unlimited (Quadratec), Go Rhino overhead overland rack, JK Unlimited (Quadratec), ExtremeTerrain — JK racks and storage
x: The four-door roof is long enough for a proper platform, so you can keep weight off the tailgate. Mind the payload.

t: Snorkel — Injen EVO15070 side-mount snorkel, JK (Quadratec), ExtremeTerrain — JK snorkels
x: The stock intake draws from the fender. A snorkel lifts it above the dust and spray.

t: Bumpers & Recovery — ARB USA, Rock Krawler, ExtremeTerrain — JK bumpers and towing
x: A winch-ready steel front bumper is the usual first armor buy. Count its weight against the payload.

3.6: 6 qt SAE 5W-20 meeting MS-6395 (5W-30 permitted) · 3.8: 6.0 qt with filter, 5W-20 or 5W-30 per the filler cap The Pentastar uses a cartridge filter under a 24 mm cap on top of the engine. Quadratec notes the filter changed for 2014, so buy for your year, and says to pull the old element gently because the pressure-relief valve is in the cap. Don't overtighten the cap; Curbside Classic gives 1
Panel filter in the airbox If a snorkel or aftermarket intake is fitted, check the clamps and seals as well as the element.
Quadratec lists JK cabin filters from the 2011 model year on Quadratec lists separate cabin filters for 2011–2013 and later JKs.
3.6 Pentastar: 0.043 in (1.10 mm) gap Pentastar plugs are under the intake plenum on the rear bank, so it's a good time to look for oil filter housing seepage. 3.8 plugs: [CONFIRM IN MANUAL].

3.8 and 2012 3.6: HOAT 5-year/100,000-mile, about 13 qt · 2013–18 3.6: Mopar 10-year/150,000-mile OAT (MS.90032), 10.5 qt (ExtremeTerrain) Don't mix HOAT and OAT; check what's in the tank before topping up. On a 3.6, a coolant leak in the valley can come from the oil cooler, not the water pump.

W5A580 (2012–18): Mopar ATF+4, 5.3 qt service fill / 8.1 qt overhaul · 42RLE (2007–11): ATF+4, about 4.0 qt drain-and-fill / 8.8 qt total Driving Line says heat kills both automatics, especially with oversized tires, towing or hard off-road use, and recommends an auxiliary cooler and proper gearing. A drain-and-fill with a new filter is the usual DIY.

Mopar manual transmission lubricant meeting MS-9224 · 1.6 qt Driving Line says the NSG370 can grind, pop out of gear and get noisy, and recommends regular fresh fluid. A 2007 lube chart gives 22 ft-lb for the fill and drain plugs.
Mopar ATF+4 · 2.1 qt Remove the fill plug before the drain plug. Both are chain-driven cases with aluminum housings (Driving Line), so don't overtighten the plugs.
GL-5 80W-90 · Dana 30 (186 FBI): 2.1 pt · Dana 44 (216 FBI, Rubicon): 2.7 pt If the oil looks milky, water has got in through the axle vent or seals.

GL-5 80W-90 · 226 RBI: 4.75 pt · synthetic 75W-140 for trailer towing · add 4 oz Mopar limited-slip additive to Trac-Lok axles A tag on the cover marks a limited-slip axle. Rubicon lockers don't need friction modifier.
Mopar Power Steering Fluid +4 or Mopar ATF+4 Big tires work the steering box hard. Look for leaks at the box and the pressure lines.
Mopar DOT 3 (DOT 4 acceptable if DOT 3 isn't available) Manual trucks share the fluid type in the clutch master cylinder.
Front axle-shaft U-joints, plus driveshaft joints where greaseable Rubicon Dana 44 front U-joints take a beating with lockers and big tires, so carry a spare.
Engine-specific A sticking PCV valve adds to oil consumption, which matters on a 3.8.

JL The current two-door Wrangler, more modern inside and out, refreshed for 2024. The JL two-door is the most capable short Wrangler Jeep has built, and the most civilized: it's lighter, quicker and quieter than the JK, with an 8-speed that makes the Pentastar feel like it finally found its gearbox. Early trucks had real teething trouble, so buy one with its recalls done and its steering sorted.

t: Fix steering wobble: damper, track bar, then the rest
x: Front-end shimmy or full death wobble after a bump at 45–65 mph, with the steering wheel shaking side to side. Helper · torque wrench · sockets · jack and stands.

t: Replace a loose aluminum steering box (TSB 08-074-20)
x: Light, vague, loose steering and wandering on the highway, sometimes with play you can see at the pitman arm. One owner described it as 'super light, vague and loose' at nearly 100,000 miles. Pitman-arm puller · line wrenches · large sockets · torque wrench · drain pan · power steering fluid.

t: Clutch: check the recall, then replace if it slips
x: Slipping under load, a burning smell, or a clutch-overheat warning after crawling. Recall 20V-124 covered manual Wranglers built from August 23, 2017 to February 13, 2020 because the pressure plate could overheat, fracture and, in the worst case, start a fire. Transmission jack · alignment tool · torque wrench · brake bleeder · a friend.

t: Replace a leaking Pentastar oil cooler / filter housing
x: Oil, and sometimes coolant, pooling in the valley under the intake and running down the back of the engine. Pickup Truck + SUV Talk lists cracked Pentastar oil-filter housings and cooler adapters as a known JL issue. External-Torx and metric sockets · inch-pound torque wrench · hose pliers · shop towels to plug the intake ports.

A dropping coolant level, a sweet smell, or crusty residue around the turbo coolant lines or the coolant bottle hoses on a 2.0 turbo. Pickup Truck + SUV Talk lists a TSB for turbo coolant return line leaks. Cooling-system pressure tester · hose-clamp pliers · drain pan · Mopar OAT coolant.

t: Replace a front hub and bearing
x: A speed-related growl, play when you rock the wheel top to bottom, or an ABS fault. Worn bearings are also on every death-wobble checklist. Axle-nut socket · breaker bar · torque wrench · wire brush · anti-seize.

t: Press in new front ball joints
x: Clunks, wander, uneven tire wear, or movement when you rock a lifted wheel top to bottom. It's more common on lifted trucks with heavy tires. Ball-joint press with JL adapters · breaker bar · torque wrench · pickle fork.

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: On a Rubicon, 35s. Driving Line ran 35x12.50R17s on a stock-height JL Rubicon with JKS bump-stop spacers and the stock flares. They cleared on level ground but hit the inner fenders when flexed, and the spacers cost about 2 inches of up-travel. On a Sport or Sahara, the realistic answer is a 33 with a wheel change; 35s on those trims usually need bump stops, less backspacing and often a 2–2.5-inch

The 2.0T makes more torque (295 against 260 lb-ft), and the EPA rated the 2018 two-door 2.0T at 23/25 mpg against 18/23 for the 3.6 automatic (17/25 manual). It's automatic-only, has extra cooling loops and needs spark plugs every 30,000 miles. The Pentastar is the one with a manual option and a long, well-understood service history.

t: How much can a two-door JL tow?
x: Quadratec lists 2,000 lb for every two-door trim, against 3,500 lb for the four-door.
Quadratec's 2020–2021 specs list 1,000 lb for the two-door. Check the door-jamb sticker on the truck in front of you.

Sport and Sahara: Dana M186 front and M200 rear, with an M220 rear if the limited slip was ordered. Rubicon: wider M210 front and M220 rear with electric lockers. Way of Life notes the Sahara always has the 186 front.

t: Is death wobble still a thing on the JL?
x: Yes. Any solid front axle can do it. FCA offered early JL owners a stronger steering damper in 2019, and later fixes addressed the track-bar welds and the steering box. A worn or loose track bar, ball joints or tie-rod ends are still the usual cause, and Quadratec warns that a new damper alone only hides it.

t: What oil does the JL Pentastar take?
x: Five quarts of 0W-20 meeting MS-6395, with the Mopar MO-349 cartridge filter. That's a quart less and a thinner grade than the JK, so don't copy JK numbers. The 2.0T takes 5 quarts of full-synthetic 5W-30 rated API SN PLUS.

A 12.3-inch Uconnect 5 screen on every model, first- and second-row side-curtain airbags, a new grille, an antenna built into the windshield frame, an available 8,000-lb Warn winch, power seats, a Dana 44 HD full-float rear axle on the Rubicon, a better-equipped Willys, and a new Rubicon X with 35s.

No JL year is a write-off, but 2018–2019 trucks had the most recalls and fixes: track-bar welds, the damper program, the steering box TSB and clutch recalls on manuals. Buy one with every fix documented, or step up to a later truck.

It's better equipped than any earlier Wrangler: side airbags and stronger B-pillars from launch, and side-curtain airbags from 2024. But Euro NCAP gave it 1 star in 2018, and the IIHS rated the four-door Marginal after it tipped over in the small-overlap test.

t: Suspension Lift — AEV — DualSport RT, Teraflex, MetalCloak, ExtremeTerrain — JL lift kits
x: A 2–2.5-inch lift restores the up-travel you'd lose to bump-stop spacers and clears 35s on any trim. Correct the geometry with brackets or adjustable arms.

t: Steering — Synergy Manufacturing, Synergy 8875-01 adjustable front track bar (Quadratec), ExtremeTerrain — JL steering linkage
x: Heavier tie rods, drag links and an adjustable track bar keep big tires in line, which matters more on the twitchy short wheelbase.

t: Lockers & Gears — ARB Air Locker for JL (Quadratec), G2 ring and pinion, JL Dana 44 rear (Quadratec), ExtremeTerrain — JL lockers
x: Sport and Sahara owners add lockers and regear for 35s; Rubicons usually only need gears.

t: Armor — GenRight, Rock Krawler, ExtremeTerrain — JL armor and protection
x: On a short wheelbase you hit fewer rockers but more bumpers. Steel bumpers and skid plates come first.

JL Unlimited 4xe 392 The four-door JL, including the 4xe plug-in hybrid and the V8 Rubicon 392. The four-door JL is the Wrangler with a choice of engines: a diesel, a plug-in hybrid and a 470-hp Hemi V8, all with solid axles and doors that come off. Pick the powertrain that suits how you travel, and check the recalls first. Several of them tell you to park outside.

t: Fix steering wobble: damper, track bar, then the rest
x: Front-end shimmy or full death wobble after a bump at 45–65 mph, with the steering wheel shaking side to side. Helper · torque wrench · sockets · jack and stands.

t: Replace a loose aluminum steering box (TSB 08-074-20)
x: Light, vague, loose steering and wandering on the highway, sometimes with play you can see at the pitman arm. One owner described it as 'super light, vague and loose' at nearly 100,000 miles. Pitman-arm puller · line wrenches · large sockets · torque wrench · drain pan · power steering fluid.

t: Replace a leaking Pentastar oil cooler / filter housing
x: Oil, and sometimes coolant, pooling in the valley under the intake and running down the back of the engine. Pickup Truck + SUV Talk lists cracked Pentastar oil-filter housings and cooler adapters as a known JL issue. External-Torx and metric sockets · inch-pound torque wrench · hose pliers · shop towels to plug the intake ports.

t: Power-steering pump: recall check, then replacement
x: Loss of power assist or a 'Service Power Steering' message. AARP reports that the June 2026 recall covers about 1,077,000 2021–2025 Wranglers and Gladiators whose electro-hydraulic pump connection can overheat and start a fire, even when parked. Owners were told to park outside until it's fixed, and at least 51 fires were linked to the fault. Line wrenches · drain pan · sockets · the specified pow

t: EcoDiesel: fuel-pump recall and fuel-filter service
x: Stalling, hard starting or a diesel smell. Pickup Truck + SUV Talk lists recall 23V-263 for possible high-pressure fuel pump failure on some 2021–2023 EcoDiesels, where debris in the fuel system can cause a stall or a fuel leak. Filter wrench · drain pan · rags · service manual for the priming procedure.

A dropping coolant level, a sweet smell, or crusty residue around the turbo coolant lines or the coolant bottle hoses on a 2.0 turbo (the 4xe uses the same 2.0 turbo engine). Pickup Truck + SUV Talk lists a TSB for turbo coolant return line leaks. Cooling-system pressure tester · hose-clamp pliers · drain pan · Mopar OAT coolant.

Rear sag, bottoming out on washboard, or the truck sitting on its bump stops once the drawers, fridge and water are loaded. Payload can be as low as 880 lb (Quadratec lists that for the 2020 Sahara four-door). Floor jack and stands · sockets · torque wrench · access to a vehicle scale.

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: On a Rubicon, 35s. Driving Line ran 35x12.50R17s on a stock-height JL Unlimited Rubicon with bump-stop spacers and the factory flares. They cleared on level ground but hit the inner fenders when flexed. 3,500 lb for most four-doors. From 2024, Hagerty says the full-float Dana 44 HD rear axle raises that to 5,000 lb on non-4xe trucks with the eight-speed automatic.
Quadratec lists 1,190 lb for a 2020 Sport four-door, 880 lb for a Sahara, 892 lb for a Rubicon and 1,351 lb for the 2021 Rubicon 392. The door sticker on your truck has the real figure.

t: Is the 4xe safe to buy after the fire recalls?
x: Yes, once the recall work is done. The October 2024 recall covered 154,032 Wrangler and Grand Cherokee 4xe models, with a software update and, where needed, a battery replacement. Owners were told to park outside and stop charging until it was fixed. Confirm completion on NHTSA, and test that the truck charges.

t: How far does the 4xe go on electricity?
x: The EPA rates it at 21 miles and 49 MPGe on its 17 kWh battery. Hagerty says the 2024 update recalibrated E-Save mode to recover energy about 50 percent more effectively.
Not any more. Jeep announced final editions for 2024 and 2025, then in August 2025 CEO Bob Broderdorf said, 'We will extend the availability of the 392 on Wrangler,' and announced a V8 Gladiator too.

t: What oil does each engine take?
x: 3.6: 5 quarts of 0W-20 (MS-6395). 2.0T: 5 quarts of full-synthetic 5W-30, API SN PLUS (MS-13340). 3.0 EcoDiesel: 9 quarts of 5W-40 synthetic (MS-12991). For the 4xe and the 392, use the owner's manual [CONFIRM IN MANUAL].

t: How did the JL Unlimited do in crash tests?
x: Badly in one test. In the IIHS small-overlap test, a 2020 Unlimited's front axle tucked under the structure and the truck tipped onto its side. A 2022 retest ended the same way, so it was rated Marginal both times. Side-curtain airbags arrived with the 2024 refresh.

t: Does the JL Unlimited get death wobble?
x: It can, like any solid-axle Jeep. Early trucks got a free stronger damper in 2019. The cure is a tight front end: track bar, tie-rod ends, ball joints, bushings and bearings, followed by an alignment.

t: What do I need to know about the power-steering recall?
x: Recall 26V-363 (June 2026) covers about 1,077,000 2021–2025 Wranglers and Gladiators. A high-resistance connection at the electro-hydraulic pump can overheat and start a fire even when parked, and owners were told to park outside until dealers can inspect and repair it free.

It started as a 1951 prototype called the BJ, went into regular production in 1953, and picked up the name Land Cruiser in June 1954 — coined by Toyota's Hanji Umehara. What followed is one of the longest-running nameplates in the business and a lineage that splits, roughly, into two tribes: the utilitarian short- and long-wheelbase workhorses, and the station wagons that slowly learned to carry f

FJ40 BJ40 The two-door, short-wheelbase icon on leaf springs and F/2F straight-sixes — the truck that made the Land Cruiser name in America. The FJ40 is a farm implement that accidentally became a fashion icon: leaf springs, a straight-six with the manners of a tractor and steering vague enough to count as a suggestion. It is also the reason anybody outside Japan cares what a Land Cruiser is.

Grease and gear oil oozing from the knuckle wiper seals, a mix of grease and 90-weight inside the knuckle, or play when you lift a front wheel and shove it. Hub socket · brass drift · spring scale · seal driver · torque wrench · Cruiser Corps knuckle kit 514-108 (1958–9/1975) or 514-109 (9/1975–1/1990) · OEM knuckle wiper kit · moly grease

Loud ticking from the top end (loose valves), or poor running and burned valves (tight valves, which are the ones to worry about). Feeler gauges (fresh ones; soft gauges bend) · 17 mm wrench (a 17/19 mm socket-ended flex wrench helps) · new valve cover gasket and acorn-nut washers

Hesitation, stumbling, rough idle or stalling at low rpm on a truck with an original carburetor. Screwdrivers · carb cleaner · correct Keyster rebuild kit (by carb number, e.g. 21100-60280 for 9/1973–9/1975)
Drum brakes that pull, fade or need constant adjustment on a 1960–1975 truck. Hub tools · grinder · flare-nut wrenches · brake bleeder · Cruiser Corps kit A151 (front, 8/1970–9/1975) or similar

Sagging springs, cracked leaves, or a rear shackle that flips over center on a lifted truck. Jacks and stands · breaker bar · welder (anti-inversion plates) · ARB/OME kit (e.g. ARB-103 for 1975–8/1980) · urethane bushing kit A216
Soft or holed floors, often found with rotten body mounts on 1979–84 trucks. Cut-off wheel · MIG welder · clamps · seam sealer · Cruiser Corps 605-111L (left front, 1979–1984 FJ40/FJ45)

Excessive play or backlash at the wheel after tie rods and the center arm have been checked, or fluid weeping from a factory power-steering box. Pitman arm puller · seal kit 520-139 (1979–10/1984 FJ40/45) or conversion kit 524-117
Screaming highway rpm on 33s with a 1:1 top gear. Transmission jack · H55F (input shaft to suit the engine) · oiler pipe · shifter · linkage kit · gaskets

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: The 'old tried and true' answer on IH8MUD is 31x10.50R15 on stock wheels and suspension. 33x9.50R15 is a popular size on stock 15-inch rims too, but owners report rubbing at the rear over bumps or at full flex. One fixed it with 1-inch spacers under the bump stops, and another had to adjust the front steering stops. One member said 33x10.50s looked 'pretty stuffed.'

t: Which years should I look for?
x: Most buyers prefer 1976-and-later trucks for front disc brakes and the 4.2 L 2F. 1979 added optional power steering and A/C and taller 3.70 gears in the US. IH8MUD veterans like the '78 and would consider 1979–83 at the right price, but note that 1980-and-later bodies seem to rust more readily.

The four-speed arrived with the 2F in 1975 in the US. Most owners prefer it, especially on 33-inch tires. If you want overdrive, the H55F five-speed swap is well documented, though it takes floor, crossmember, linkage and driveshaft work.

t: Did the US get diesel FJ40s?
x: Not for the general public. Diesel 40s were never sold to US retail buyers, though some arrived as mine trucks. Canada was the exception in 1984, when it got the BJ42 diesel with an overdrive five-speed for about CA$14,000.

Only as an option on petrol FJ40s from 1979. Earlier trucks have manual steering, and many owners fit a GM Saginaw power-steering conversion. It isn't a casual bolt-on, and Cruiser Corps recommends professional installation.

They work, but they need constant adjustment. Front discs came on US trucks in 1976. Bolt-on conversion kits exist for 1970–75 trucks, and IH8MUD has a write-up using mini-truck knuckles with later Land Cruiser calipers and rotors.

The common choice is an Old Man Emu 2-inch kit with greaseable anti-inversion shackles. For bigger lifts, some owners go spring-over-axle, which IH8MUD members say gives roughly 6 inches and is usually paired with power steering.

t: Should I swap in a V8?
x: Plenty of owners have. Hagerty notes many FJ40s got small-block Chevy V8s on the secondary market. The stock six is durable, though, and a healthy 2F with good compression will run a long time.

Yes. Toyota announced GR Heritage Parts reproductions for the 40 Series in 2021, starting with engine, driveline and exhaust parts. Specialists such as Cruiser Corps, CruiserTeq, Cool Cruisers of Texas and JT Outfitters stock everything from knuckle kits to floor pans.

It depends heavily on condition and originality. In 2019 Hagerty put the average #2-condition FJ40 at $47,375, after a 7.6 percent drop since 2016, with a 1968 at $49,100 and a 1975 at $44,800. Retro Rides says tidy Australian examples run roughly AU$30,000–50,000 and that US prices are far higher.

t: Suspension Lift — Old Man Emu 2" kit (via Cruiser Corps), OME FK08 anti-inversion plates
x: Fresh springs and shocks fix the sag and harsh ride of 40-year-old leaves, and 2 inches clears 33s more comfortably. Greaseable anti-inversion shackles stop the rear shackle flipping over center.

t: Disc Brakes — Cruiser Corps disc conversion kits
x: Pre-1976 trucks stop on four drums. A front disc conversion is the single biggest safety upgrade.
Factory steering boxes develop play, and manual steering is heavy on big tires. A Saginaw conversion is the common fix.

t: Roll Cage & Armor — Metal Tech 4x4 — FJ40 full roll cage, Metal Tech 4x4 — Land Cruiser parts
x: The factory roll bar is a start. Full cages, overhead bars and tube doors add protection for rock work.

t: Restoration & Oem Parts — Cruiser Corps — 40 Series, CruiserTeq (Cruiser Outfitters) — 40 Series, Cool Cruisers of Texas, JT Outfitters
x: Body panels, seals, knuckle kits and trim keep a 40-plus-year-old truck original and on the trail.
For a full rebuild, specialist shops build everything from stock restorations to modern-drivetrain FJ40s.

2F: 7.8 L (≈8.2 qt) with filter · F: 7 L · factory spec API SC/SD (use a modern oil suited to a flat-tappet engine) One IH8MUD owner warns the owner's manual figure led him to overfill; another always uses 8 qt in a 2F with a filter change. Fill to the dipstick, not the book. New drain-plug washer every time.
Paper element in the factory air cleaner Replace it before you judge how the carburetor runs.
Plugs, points (where fitted), cap & rotor · gap and dwell [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Check fuel and ignition basics before blaming the carburetor.

Adjustable rockers · clearances [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] The F and 2F have adjustable rockers that need periodic checks; tight valves are the ones that burn. Valve layout front to back is E-I-I-E-E-I-I-E-E-I-I-E.

Ethylene-glycol coolant · 2F: 16.5 L (the original F table lists 15.2 L) The early F-engine table even lists plain water; use proper ethylene-glycol coolant now, flush until it runs clear, fit a fresh thermostat and check the bypass hose.
API GL-4, SAE 90 · J30 3-speed 1.7 L · H41 4-speed 3.1 L A swapped-in H55F five-speed takes 4.9 L (60/70-series table) and needs its fifth-gear oiler.
API GL-4, SAE 90 · 1.7 L (2.1 L with PTO) A PTO winch also has its own gearbox: front winch GL-4 SAE 90, 600 cc.
API GL-5 hypoid 80W-90 · 2.5 L each · LSD oil for limited-slip Gear oil mixed into the knuckle grease points to failed inner axle seals.
Molybdenum-disulfide lithium-base grease, NLGI-2 Weeping at the wiper seals or a mix of grease and 90-weight inside means a knuckle rebuild.
Manual box: API GL-4 SAE 90, 600 cc · power steering (1979–84): ATF Dexron, 0.8 L total Top up the manual box through its fill plug; most play is in the box, center arm and tie-rod ends.
DOT 3 (SAE J1703) Bleed every corner and look for weeping wheel cylinders on drum-brake axles.
Chassis: moly lithium NLGI-2 · driveshafts & wheel bearings: lithium multipurpose NLGI-2 Grease the spring pins/shackles (greaseable pins if fitted), driveshaft U-joints and slip yokes.
Inline filter Do it before or with any carburetor rebuild.
V-belts and radiator hoses · gear-driven camshaft, so no timing belt The F-series engine drives its camshaft by gears, so there's no timing belt or chain to schedule.

The FJ45 is the 40 Series stretched until it could carry a squad or a pallet; the FJ55 is what happened when Toyota decided American families wanted one too. t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: We couldn't find a solid FJ55- or FJ45-specific consensus. They use 40 Series axles, and for the stock FJ40, IH8MUD's 'tried and true' size is 31x10.50R15, with 33x9.50R15 fitting but rubbing at full flex. Try any size on your own truck before committing.

t: What's the difference between an FJ45 and an FJ55?
x: The FJ45 is the long-wheelbase version of the 40 Series: pickups and cab-chassis on 2,950 mm and an early four-door wagon on 2,650 mm. The FJ55 (1967–80) is a purpose-built four-door wagon on a 2,700 mm wheelbase with its own fully boxed frame.

t: Why is it called the Iron Pig?
x: Hagerty traces the name to the FJ55's front end, where the two-tone paint made it resemble a pig's snout. Wikipedia also records 'Moose.'

1975–80 trucks have the 4.2 L 2F, a four-speed and front disc brakes, and the domed hood is the easy tell. Earlier trucks use the 3.9 L F and a three-speed whose first gear has no synchro, which some collectors prefer for originality.

Not complete ones. Hagerty says replacement panels generally don't exist and missing metal usually has to be fabricated, and trim and weatherstripping are hard to find. Cruiser Corps does sell FJ55 repair sections, including outer rockers and lower-fender patch panels with the inner brace. Buy the most solid truck you can afford.

t: Are the drum brakes good enough?
x: Hagerty says stock drums are adequate if they're in good order and the powertrain is stock. Disc conversions are common and parts are easy to find.

Old Man Emu makes 2-inch kits for the FJ45 (1963–80 and 1980–84), sold through specialists such as Cruiser Corps, with greaseable shackles and a steering damper. Confirm fitment for an FJ55 before ordering.
Yes, with basic care. Hagerty calls the F and 2F durable with basic maintenance and periodic valve adjustments, and says mechanical repairs are easy and cheap compared with rust repair.

In Hagerty's FJ55 buyer's guide (first published in 2021 and updated in 2023), the median value for all conditions was $34,500 and for #2 condition $46,300, with quoted values up 65.8 percent since 2020. Its earlier wagon-values piece mentioned private sales approaching six figures.

t: Were FJ45s really used by armies?
x: Yes. Truck Encyclopedia describes the super-long-wheelbase FJ45 as a major military export used as a troop carrier, and the Irish Army took 77 FJ45s in 1977.

The FJ60 is the Land Cruiser that learned to carry a family and a cooler without forgetting it was a truck. The FJ60 (US 1981–87) has round headlights, the carbureted 4.2 L 2F and a four-speed manual. The FJ62 (1988–90) has fuel injection, an automatic, square headlights and a plusher cabin. Hagerty calls the FJ60 the more collectible. The FJ62 is easier to live with in traffic.

t: Did US FJ60s get a five-speed?
x: No. US trucks used the H41F/H42F four-speed. The H55F five-speed went into other markets from 1982–83, and swapping one in is close to direct on post-April-1985 US trucks.

t: What's the High Altitude Compensation system?
x: It's emissions equipment on 1981–87 trucks that Corsetti says advances ignition timing above about 3,930 feet. A Weber carburetor bypasses it and costs performance, so Corsetti recommends keeping the factory carb.
Corsetti lists 3,500 lb.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: Corsetti lists 11 mpg city and 18 highway with a 23.8-gallon tank. In practice, bigger tires and a roof rack make it worse.

t: How do I tell if the engine is tired?
x: Do a compression test. Corsetti's benchmarks for a 2F are about 160–165 psi when excellent, caution under 120 and walk away under 100, with no more than 10 percent spread. The 2F reportedly reaches 300,000 miles with care.

The classic setup is an Old Man Emu 2-inch kit with greaseable shackles and a steering damper. Kits are split by build date (before or after April 1985) and load rating. Corsetti fits an OME steering damper even on unlifted trucks.

t: Can I import a diesel HJ61?
x: None were sold new in the US, but the 25-year rule now covers every 60 Series. Silodrome calls the 12H-T-powered GX the most desirable 60. Check EPA and state registration rules before buying.

Hagerty's wagon-values piece (around 2020) put the median quote for FJ60s and FJ62s at $18,500, called the FJ60 the pick for collectibility and said demand appeared to be overtaking Jeep Grand Wagoneers. Rust-free restored and restomod trucks sell for much more.

FJ62 3F-E 4.0 I6 The 60 grows up: fuel-injected 3F-E, automatic gearbox, square headlights and the first push upmarket. The FJ62 is where the Land Cruiser put on a collared shirt: fuel injection, an automatic, square headlights and power everything, all on the same leaf-sprung frame that crossed the Outback. It is the easiest old Cruiser to drive every day, and one of the hardest to find without r
Rough or hunting idle, hesitation, or a hiss under the hood. Vacuum gauge · smoke tester or carb cleaner spray · vacuum diagram · hose and clamps

t: Diagnose oil leaks before pulling the transmission
x: Oil drips at the bellhousing or under the engine. Degreaser · torque wrench · valve cover gasket · UV dye (optional)
Grease sludge leaking from the steering knuckles. Spring scale · seal driver · Cruiser Corps kit 595-102 or 514-109 (to 1/1990) · knuckle shim and gasket kit 595-101 · moly grease
Sagging springs, worn shocks, or front-end shake after bumps. Jacks and stands · breaker bar · ARB-111 (medium load) or equivalent kit · grease gun
Fluid on the driver's-side axle and spring, low fluid, or a groaning pump. Line wrenches · Pitman arm puller (box removal) · power-steering fluid · drain pan

t: Rust repair at the rear wheel wells
x: Bubbling at the rear wheel arches, a patched-feeling inner well, or a mud flap that sits unevenly. Cut-off wheel · MIG welder · seam sealer · rust converter and cavity wax

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: On a stock FJ62, one IH8MUD member runs 33x9.50s with no problems. 33x10.50 might fit, but 33x12.50s won't without a lift. Many owners choose 31x10.50R15, which looks right at stock height or on an OME lift. Corsetti says not to go wider than 10.5 in or taller than 33 in on a factory rim, and Cruiser Corps advises against tires wider than 10.5 in on the 15x5.5 OEM steel wheel.

The FJ62 has fuel injection, 155 hp, an automatic and a plusher cabin, so it's easier to drive every day. The FJ60 has the carbureted 2F, a four-speed manual and round headlights. Hagerty calls the FJ60 the more collectible of the two.

t: Is the 3F-E the same engine as an early 80 Series?
x: Yes. IH8MUD members note that in US trucks the 3F-E was used only in the FJ62 and the 1991–92 FJ80, so parts and knowledge carry across.

t: Can I convert it to a manual?
x: Yes, with an H55F five-speed, but it's a big job. You'll need a manual bellhousing, flywheel, clutch, pedal and hydraulics, crossmember and floor modifications, shift linkage, driveshaft changes and some wiring.
Corsetti lists 3,500 lb, the same as the FJ60.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: Corsetti lists 12 mpg city and 19 highway with a 23.8-gallon tank. Real-world numbers on bigger tires are lower.

t: Is a little oil leak normal?
x: On a truck this age, mostly yes. As one IH8MUD member put it, 'any '88 Cruiser is going to leak some oil, from somewhere.' Check the pan bolts and valve cover gasket before assuming it's the rear main seal.
The common setup is an Old Man Emu 2-inch kit for 4/1985–1/1990 trucks, in light, medium or heavy load ratings, with greaseable shackles and a steering damper.
The Japanese-market version introduced in 1987 with the 3F-E. Wikipedia says it let the Land Cruiser be sold in Japan as a passenger vehicle rather than a commercial one.
