3F-E: 7.8 L with filter change (Toyota publications via IH8MUD); IH8MUD owners quote 8.2 qt as the official figure · viscosity [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Fill to the dipstick, not a number: the oil cooler holds some oil, and IH8MUD owners report 7–8.5 qt depending on how fully it drained. Pre-filling the filter helps.
Paper element for 3F-E Check the rubber intake hose for cracks while the lid is off; an air leak after the meter can upset the EFI.

Plugs, wires, cap, rotor and PCV valve The F-series is an OHV engine (Wikipedia), so there is no timing belt to budget for. IH8MUD members start rough-idle hunts with a tune-up and a full set of vacuum hoses.

Ethylene-glycol coolant · 16.5 L (Toyota publications via IH8MUD) Replace any hose that is hard or swollen, and check the upper thermostat housing and radiator for old repairs; overheating history matters on a big iron six.

Dexron II ATF · 5 L drain-and-refill, 15 L dry fill (Toyota publications via IH8MUD) A drain-and-refill only changes about a third of the fluid, so do two or three a few hundred miles apart on unknown fluid rather than a pressure flush. Drop the pan and change the strainer once.
API GL-4 or GL-5, SAE 90 · 2.1 L with the A440F (Toyota publications via IH8MUD) Fill until it runs out of the fill hole, and remove the fill plug before the drain plug.
API GL-5 hypoid gear oil, SAE 80W-90 · 3.0 L (Toyota publications via IH8MUD) Milky oil means water got in through the breather or seals, common after deep crossings.
API GL-5 hypoid gear oil, SAE 80W-90 · 2.5 L; LSD oil if fitted with a limited-slip (Toyota publications via IH8MUD) Check the pinion seal and axle-end seals for weeps while you're under there.

Molybdenum-disulfide lithium-base grease, NLGI-2 (Toyota publications via IH8MUD) Grease weeping from the knuckle wipers is the classic 60-series leak (Corsetti). If the knuckle grease is runny, gear oil is getting past the inner axle seal.

Dexron or Dexron II ATF · 0.81 L total, 0.39 L reservoir only (Toyota publications via IH8MUD) Check the box, pump and hoses for weeps at the same time; leaks often show on the driver's-side axle and spring.
DOT 3 / SAE J1703 (Toyota publications via IH8MUD) Old fluid in a 30-year-old system means sticky calipers and corroded lines; inspect the hard lines while bleeding.

Driveshafts: lithium-base NLGI-2 · steering link ends: moly lithium NLGI-2 (Toyota publications via IH8MUD) Grease the U-joints and slip yokes. Greaseable shackles and pins, like those in OME kits, need regular grease too.
EFI in-line filter for FJ62 An old filter starves the EFI and can mimic a rough-idle or vacuum problem.

J70 76 78 79 The heavy-duty workhorse — wagons, troop carriers and pickups — still built for Africa, Australia, Latin America and the Middle East, and back on sale in Japan since 2023. The 70 is the Land Cruiser Toyota forgot to stop building, and nobody who needs one has ever complained. Leaf springs, a part-time transfer case, manual hubs and a cabin with all the sound deadening of a grain silo:

t: Adjust or replace the front wheel bearings
x: A hum from the front that becomes a growl, then a howl, and gets louder with speed. With the wheel off the ground, there's play when you rock it at 12 and 6 o'clock. 54 mm hub socket · torque wrench · bearing grease · new tapered roller bearings and seals if replacing.

t: Stop dust getting past the airbox (1VD V8)
x: Red dust on the clean side of the filter, MAF sensor faults, limp mode in the middle of a dusty trip, or a noisy turbo. Screwdriver · torch · MAF cleaner · replacement seal or aftermarket airbox.

Wind noise that gets worse with age, whistling at town speeds, diesel fumes in traffic, and a dusty dash after a day on dirt roads. Trim tool · bulb-type door seal kit · adhesive if the kit calls for it.

t: Refill the manual gearbox with the right oil
x: Crunching shifts, especially between second and third. Drain and fill plug wrenches · fluid pump · GL-4 75W-90 gear oil.

t: Repair a cracked rear spring hanger
x: A clunk from the rear under heavy load, such as towing up a hill, and a wandering feel in corners if the crack has grown. Welder and grinder (or a fab shop) · bracing plates · GVM-rated springs.

t: Upgrade the clutch on a tuned V8
x: Revs climb while acceleration stays the same or drops off, the clutch bites only near the top of the pedal, and shifts start grinding. Transmission jack · clutch alignment tool · heavy-duty clutch kit.
Hard starting, slow charging of auxiliary batteries and charging warnings on the dash. Basic hand tools · low-pressure hose · uprated alternator if needed.
The cabin never gets cool on a hot day, and the back seat of a 79 dual-cab is miserable. Soft brush and hose · plug-in AC controller.

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: The IH8MUD consensus for a stock-height long-wheelbase 70 is 235/85R16, about 31.7 inches. 285/75R16 (33 inches) will go on, but on factory steel wheels owners report it rubs on the inside at full lock unless you change wheel offset. Short-wheelbase owners in the same thread treat 255/85R16 (about 33 inches) as the sensible upper limit, and the one running them has a lift. Sagging old springs make

t: Can I buy one in the US?
x: Not new. Toyota never sold the 70 in the United States. Canada got a few BJ70s for the 1985–87 model years and, as of 2022, Canadian mining companies could still buy them. Americans import older trucks under the rule NHTSA set in 1989 exempting vehicles more than 25 years old.

Body and wheelbase. Since 1999, 78 is the long-wheelbase troop carrier and 79 the long-wheelbase pickup (single and, from 2012, dual cab); the 76 is the four-door wagon. Earlier, 70/71 were short wheelbase, 73/74 medium, 75 long, and 77 a semi-long wagon.

t: Which years and engines are best?
x: Unsealed 4X4 says many enthusiasts prefer the 2007–2016 V8s, which don't have a DPF, but that service history matters more than the year. For US imports, the age rule means older trucks, typically with the 1HZ, 2H, 3B or 13B-T diesels or the 3F and 1FZ petrol sixes.
Selectable front and rear lockers were factory options in some markets. Otherwise ARB Air Lockers and Harrop electric lockers are the common add-ons; one IH8MUD owner runs Harrop E-lockers in a BJ74.

Rarely. Most 70s are manual, but a four-speed auto was offered on a few versions: FJ73 (1985–1992), BJ74, HZJ73/77 (1990–1999) and HZJ74/76K (1999–2004). The 2.8 L four that arrived in 2023 came with a six-speed automatic.
Australian V8s got a diesel particulate filter from September 2016 to meet Euro 5. Earlier V8s don't have one. Unsealed recommends a good highway run every 1,000–2,000 km to let it regenerate.

t: Why are the rear wheels inboard of the fronts on V8 trucks?
x: To make room for the 1VD-FTV, Toyota fitted a wider front axle and frame in 2007, which left the front and rear tracks different. Superior Engineering's coil conversion is one of the aftermarket fixes Unsealed mentions for equalizing them.

In Australia, yes. V8 wagon and troop carrier production ended in September 2024, and the GXL pickups were the last V8s, shipping until late 2025. The 2.8 L four replaced it: 201 hp and 369 lb-ft with the six-speed automatic, or 332 lb-ft with the five-speed manual added in October 2024.

Overall, yes, says Unsealed: a strong engine and a tough driveline, with many trucks running very high mileage. The known weak points are mostly about use and comfort: DPFs on late V8s, clutches on tuned trucks, gearbox synchros, front wheel bearings, dust past the airbox, leaky door seals, weak AC and frame cracks on overloaded pickups.

t: Leaf springs or coils up front?
x: Leaf springs up to the 1999 facelift, then coils with leading arms. The rear stayed on leaf springs.

t: Suspension & Gvm — Old Man Emu (ARB), Superior Engineering — coil conversions
x: Many 70s are either overloaded or riding on springs rated for loads they never carry. Matching the springs to the real load, or fitting a GVM upgrade, fixes ride and safety. A coil conversion is the expensive way to fix both ride and track width at once.
Factory lockers were only offered in some markets. Selectable air or electric lockers turn an open-diff 70 into a proper rock truck.

t: Seats & Sound Deadening — Black Duck seat covers, Carbuilders (sound deadening)
x: Unsealed's fix for the cabin: thicker seat covers (Black Duck's add about 20 mm of padding), or full replacement seats, plus sound-deadening mats.

t: Bumpers & Armor — Cruiser Outfitters — 70 Series front bumper, Cruiser Outfitters — 70 Series dual swing-out rear bumper
x: A winch bumper up front and a swing-out at the back are the standard build for a working or touring 70.
Raises the intake for water crossings and dusty roads, and pairs well with a properly sealed airbox on the V8.

t: Oem & Rebuild Parts — Cruiser Outfitters (CruiserTeq) — 70 Series, Cruiser Corps — 70 Series
x: For imported trucks in North America, specialist Land Cruiser parts houses are the easiest route to genuine and OEM-supplier parts.

Inspect the clean side of the filter Unsealed: the 1VD airbox seal lets dust past the filter, causing MAF faults and turbo wear. Dust on the clean side means fit a sealed aftermarket airbox now.
Diesel filter element; drain the separator Imported or outback-fuelled trucks may have seen dirty diesel; cheap insurance for injectors.

Steering knuckles: moly-disulfide lithium grease NLGI-2 · wheel bearings: lithium multi-purpose NLGI-2 (Toyota publications via IH8MUD) Unsealed: the tapered-roller hubs often just need the 54 mm locknut nipped up and fresh grease, and owners do the swivels at the same time.
Dexron-II ATF on older 70s (Toyota publications via IH8MUD) · V8: [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Check the box and hoses for weeps, and the drag link and tie-rod ends for play while you're there.
DOT 3 or 4, SAE J1703 (Roughtrax) A soft or high-biting clutch on a tuned V8 is the clutch itself (Unsealed), not the fluid; test it under load.
Propshaft U-joints: lithium-base NLGI-2 (Roughtrax) Unsealed says to check the rear spring hangers for cracks at every service, especially on utes that have been run over GVM.

t: Timing belt (1HZ and other belt-driven diesels)
x: The 1HZ drives its camshaft with a timing belt (Wikipedia) · interval [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Confirm whether your engine uses a belt before budgeting; kits with the water pump are available for the 1HZ.

Late-2016-on V8s have a DPF (Unsealed) Unsealed: short-trip DPF trucks clog. Rinse the low-mounted alternator with a low-pressure hose after muddy trips, and fit a DC-DC charger for big auxiliary batteries.

FJ80 FZJ80 HZJ80 HDJ80 Coil springs, full-time 4WD, solid axles at both ends and optional triple lockers — for many owners, the last 'real' Land Cruiser. The 80 is what happens when an engineering team is told to build a family wagon and quietly builds an expedition vehicle instead. Coil springs, solid axles, full-time four-wheel drive and, if you found the right one, three lockers — it is the las

Gear oil and grease caked on the outside of the knuckles, runny grease at the knuckle fill plug, wheel-bearing play or noise, or a seal that started weeping after the last service. 54 mm (2-1/8") hub socket · torque wrench to 100 ft-lb · brass drift · seal puller and driver · snap-ring pliers · 6–12 lb spring scale · Cruiser Outfitters FA9097 kit (Koyo knuckle bearings, NOK inner axle and hub seal

A coolant leak low on the driver's side of the engine, or an original-looking hose clamp on a high-mileage truck. Members warn a failure on the trail can leave you completely stranded, which is why many replace it before it fails. Basic hand tools · hose pick · coolant · new hose (owners report using Gates heater hose) and clamps; aftermarket bypass kits are also available.

Intermittent no-crank: you turn the key and get a click, or nothing, until the third or fourth try. 10 mm (battery), 12 mm (dipstick tube), 14 mm (terminal nuts), and 17 mm plus 19 mm spanners for the bell-housing bolts, per the IH8MUD write-up · small socket or screwdriver for the three contact-cover screws · starter contact set and plunger. The intake manifold stays on.

t: Power-steering leak? Check the reservoir first
x: Power-steering fluid weeping around the top of the system. It's often blamed on hoses or the pump, but Unsealed 4X4 says the usual culprit is the rubber seals inside the reservoir. Basic hand tools · small pry tool and crimping pliers · replacement reservoir seals · power-steering fluid.

t: Rear axle seals and bearings (1991–92 semi-float)
x: Gear oil soaking the rear drum brake, cracked or contaminated shoes, and grabby rear brakes at low speed. Slide hammer or bearing puller · seal and bearing drivers · bearing 90365-47013 and seal 90311-47001 (as listed in the IH8MUD thread) · rear shoes and hardware · gear oil. Later full-float trucks use a different hub-and-seal procedure.

t: Diagnose coolant in the oil before tearing down
x: Milky oil, a dropping coolant level, coolant weeping where the head meets the block, or a radiator that's already been replaced. Compression and leak-down testers · cooling-system pressure tester · combustion-leak (block) tester · if needed, an OEM head gasket set and the service manual.

t: Reinforce the frame at the steering box
x: Cracks in the frame around the steering-box mounts, a loose-feeling steering box, or wandering steering on a truck with big tires. Welder and grinder (or a fab shop) · reinforcement plate · torque wrench.

t: Re-set the rear brake proportioning valve after a lift
x: Weak rear braking or a changed pedal feel after lifting the truck, because the load-sensing proportioning valve (LSPV) now reads the truck as lightly loaded. Wrenches · ruler or calipers · paint pen to mark the start point.

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: The safe answer from IH8MUD is 285/75R16, about 33 inches, which fits a stock 80 without drama. Owners also report 305/70R16 and 295/75R16 fitting, though wheel width and offset matter as much as the tire size. 35s 'fit, but rub like mad' on a stock truck. Christo Slee's advice is that 35s work with a 2-inch Old Man Emu lift, but you'll probably rub at full flex unless you lower the bump stops. St

t: FJ80 or FZJ80 — which should I buy?
x: For most people, the 1993–1997 FZJ80. Its 4.5 L 1FZ-FE makes 212 hp against the 3F-E's 155, it could be ordered with front and rear lockers, and ABS trucks got a full-float rear with disc brakes. The 1991–92 FJ80 is simpler and cheaper but slower, with a semi-float rear and drum brakes. Collectors like 1994: big engine, lockers, and the last of the TOYOTA-lettered grilles.

Factory electric front and rear lockers were an option on US trucks from 1993 to 1997; 1991–92 trucks didn't offer them. Every 80 has a center differential that can be locked. Retrofitting factory lockers means welding, the locker ECU, harnesses and new axle shafts, so Slee says ARB Air Lockers are usually the cheaper route.

t: Can I lock the center diff in high range on a 1993–97?
x: Slee's guide says the center-diff lock switch was standard on 1991–92 US trucks and omitted from 1993 on the full-floater, disc-brake trucks, though the wiring stayed in the harness. Adding the switch lets you lock the center diff in high range; Slee also says unplugging a connector on the transfer case gives control of the lock in low range.

Kelley Blue Book lists a 5,000 lb maximum for the 1997 model. IH8MUD members quoting the owner's manual cite 3,000 lb normally and 5,000 lb with the tow package. Don't tow from the four bolt holes in the rear crossmember: Slee notes they aren't rated for towing in the US, so use a frame-mounted receiver.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: Not much. KBB lists the 1997 at 12 mpg city and 14 highway (13 combined) on a 25.1-gallon tank. Bigger tires, armor and a roof rack only make it worse.

t: Should I re-gear for bigger tires?
x: 1FZ-FE trucks came with 4.11 gears on stock 275/70R16 tires. Slee says to drop to 4.56, 4.88 or 5.29 if you go up in tire size, and suggests driving a truck with the setup you're considering first. Slee's own 4-inch, 35-inch-tire build uses 4.88s with ARB lockers.

The classic choice is an Old Man Emu kit of about 2 inches. Slee's own 4-inch kit, with coils, machined radius arms and an adjustable Panhard bar, is designed for up to 35-inch tires. Bigger lifts usually need extended brake lines (Metal Tech sells them for 3–6 inch lifts), adjustable rear links, and a proportioning-valve reset.

t: What fluids and capacities does it take?
x: Rough Trax 4x4's FZJ80 data lists 7.4 L of engine oil with the filter, 13 L of coolant, 1.4 L in the transfer case, 2.7–2.8 L in the front diff, 3.0–3.25 L in the rear diff, and 6.0 L for an automatic sump drain. A Toyota-sourced table compiled on IH8MUD gives 1.7 L for the HF2AV transfer case and only 1.9 L for an A343F drain-and-refill, so the transmission figure in particular is [CONFIRM IN MAN

t: Is it reliable? What actually breaks?
x: It's a tough truck, but now it's a 30-year-old one. The usual list: head gaskets on the 1FZ-FE, leaking knuckle seals, wheel bearings, frame cracks around the steering box, worn starter contacts, the 'pesky heater hose,' power-steering leaks, power windows, fraying seat belts and cracked dashes. Toyota fitted larger brakes from October 1992, so the 1991–92 trucks stop noticeably worse.

t: Is a Lexus LX 450 the same truck?
x: Mechanically, yes. The LX 450 (1996–97 US) is an FZJ80 with softer suspension, a plusher cabin, body cladding and its own grille and wheels, with the same 1FZ-FE engine.

t: Suspension Lift — Old Man Emu (ARB), Slee Off-Road, Metal Tech 4x4 — 80 Series rear links
x: A 2–3 inch lift with fresh coils and shocks restores ride height lost to sag and armor, and clears 33s. Bigger lifts need correction parts such as adjustable links and longer brake lines.
Only some 1993–97 trucks got factory lockers. Air lockers are the usual way to add selectable lockers to an open-diff truck, and are cheaper than retrofitting the factory ones.

t: Armor: Sliders & Bumpers — Slee Off-Road — sliders, Slee Off-Road — front bumpers, Metal Tech 4x4
x: The factory running boards dent on the first rock, and the long rear overhang drags. Sliders, a winch bumper and a swing-out rear bumper are the standard build.
The stock intake is in the passenger front fender. A snorkel moves it to the roofline for water crossings and dust.

t: Storage & Sleeping — Slee Off-Road — drawer systems
x: Many owners pull the third row and fit drawers with a fridge slide. Add a bed extension and Slee's guide says you get a flat bed of roughly 180 × 145 cm.

t: Oem & Rebuild Parts — Cruiser Outfitters (CruiserTeq), Cruiser Corps
x: Knuckle kits, seals, bearings, steering and driveline parts in OEM or OEM-supplier quality, which is what keeps a 30-year-old 80 on the trail.

1FZ-FE: API SH grade, 7.4 L (≈7.8 qt) with filter · 3F-E: 7.8 L (≈8.2 qt) with filter Timmy the Toolman's FZJ80 service uses Toyota filter 90915-YZZD3 and drain-plug washer 90430-12031, with the drain plug at 20 ft-lb.
Paper panel element Cheap insurance on a truck with unknown history — a dirty element is one of the 'owner neglect' signs Slee tells buyers to look for.
FZJ80: Denso/OEM plugs · FJ80: NGK · gap [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Both engines are distributor-fired, so do cap, rotor and plug wires at the same time.

Ethylene-glycol Toyota coolant · FZJ80 13.4 L / FJ80 19.5 L (with front & rear heaters) Timmy the Toolman refills with Toyota Red and lists thermostat 90916-03117 and gasket 16346-66020 for the FZJ80. Slee says to check the overflow bottle for deposits and look for a replaced radiator as overheating clues. Inspect the PHH while it's drained.

ATF Dexron II spec (Dexron III / Valvoline MaxLife used as backward-compatible substitutes) · FJ80 (A440F): 6 L drain-and-refill, 15.4 L dry · FZJ80 (A343F): Toyota table on IH8MUD says 1.9 L drain-and-refill, Rough Trax says 6.0 L [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] A pan drain only replaces a fraction of the fluid. FZJ80 drain-and-refill quantity [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]; Timmy the Toolman buys three gallons for a f

API GL-4/GL-5 SAE 75W-90 · 1.7 L (HF2AV) / 1.3 L (HF2A) The fill plug is the 24 mm plug at about 8 o'clock looking from the rear (IH8MUD). Drain/fill plugs 27 ft-lb, gasket 90430-18008 (Timmy the Toolman).

API GL-5 hypoid 80W-90 · 2.8 L listed — fill to the bottom of the fill hole Owners on IH8MUD report a locking front diff drains close to 4 qt and takes about 3.75 qt, more than the book figure, so buy extra. Drain/fill plugs 36 ft-lb (Timmy the Toolman). Milky or very high oil can mean water or knuckle-seal trouble.

API GL-5 hypoid 80W-90 · 3.25 L (FZJ80); FJ80 table lists 2.8 L · LSD oil if limited-slip Factory-locker trucks: if the locker won't engage, Slee's guide points to an actuator rebuild rather than the diff itself. Semi-float 1991–92 axles leak gear oil onto the brakes when the outer seals go.

Molybdenum-disulfide lithium-base grease, NLGI-2 Slee's check: pull the square knuckle fill plug and sample the grease. Runny grease means diff oil is getting past the inner axle seal, and caked grease outside the knuckle means the seals failed long ago — plan a full knuckle rebuild.
ATF Dexron II · 0.75 L total (FJ80 table) If it's weeping at the top, Unsealed 4X4 says the reservoir's internal seals are the usual culprit before hoses or the pump.
DOT 3 (SAE J1703 / FMVSS 116) Re-check the rear LSPV setting if the truck has been lifted (see the repair above).
Lithium-base multipurpose grease, NLGI-2 Grease the U-joints and slip yokes and check them for play.
Toyota canister filter Different filters for 1991–92 FJ80 and 1993–97 FZJ80.

Accessory belts and coolant hoses · the 1FZ-FE uses a timing chain, not a belt Replace the PHH and the bypass hose just above and forward of it while you're there. IH8MUD members report using Gates heater hose and good clamps instead of a $45 bypass kit.

UZJ100 FZJ105 HZJ105 HDJ100 The big wagon goes upmarket: V8 power (and, for the US, independent front suspension) and the basis for the Lexus LX 470. The 100 is the Land Cruiser that went to finishing school: a V8, independent front suspension and a cabin you could take to the opera. The purists sulked, and it turned out to be one of the most durable big wagons on the trail. Budget for the timing

t: Timing belt, water pump and thermostat (the 90k service)
x: No symptoms until it breaks. It's on the service schedule at 90,000 miles, so a truck without receipts is due. 3/4-in drive breaker bar and cheater · crank-holding tool · pulley puller · seal puller · thread locker · FIPG gasket maker. IH8MUD parts list (check fitment for your year): water pump 16100-59275-83, timing belt 13568-09070, serpentine belt 90916-02586, thermostat 90916-03100 + gasket 16
None until a brittle tee cracks and you lose coolant, possibly a long way from home. Step stool · pliers · flat screwdriver · soapy water · Toyota pipe tee 87248-60460 (x2).

t: Press in new lower ball joints
x: Clunks over bumps, play at the bottom of the knuckle, or simply a high-mileage truck with original joints. 20-ton shop press · 22, 19, 14 and 24 mm sockets · snap-ring pliers · sledge or pickle fork · lower ball joint (e.g. Cruiser Outfitters SUS43340) · factory manual section SA-73.

The solenoid clicks but the starter doesn't turn, usually on a cold start, then it fires after two or three tries. 10, 12 and 14 mm wrenches and sockets · camera for reference photos · starter contact and plunger kit · new intake gaskets.

Old, dark fluid, a truck that's slow to level, or a lift via the height-sensor links that has left the reservoir low. 10 mm wrench · clear tube and catch bottle · fluid extractor or turkey baster · Toyota AHC fluid.

t: Check spark plugs for walking out
x: A tick-tick or pop-pop at cold start that sounds like an exhaust leak and, as the plug loosens, doesn't go away when warm. Premature coil-boot and coil failures. Spark-plug socket and extension · torque wrench (inch-pound range) · dielectric grease for the coil boots.

t: Set the front ride height at the torsion bars
x: A front end that has settled or sits lower than the rear, or new tires that need more clearance. Socket and long extension · tape measure · anti-seize · Old Man Emu torsion bars (303001) and rear coils (2865) if upgrading.

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: The 100-series FAQ answer on IH8MUD is 285/75R16 on 16-inch wheels or 285/65R18 on 18s, both about 33 inches. 295/75R16s do fit, with half an inch to an inch of clearance at full turn, but owners call it tight. Even 285/75s can be snug at the rear: one owner measured 3/4 inch to the plastic wheel-well liner.

Every 100 has a center differential you can lock. A rear electric locker was a factory option only for 1998 and 1999. From 2000 Toyota relied on A-TRAC traction control instead, so ARB Air Lockers are the usual retrofit.

t: What's the deal with the 1998–99 front differential?
x: Those years have a two-pinion front diff, and Wikipedia says the pinion could flex away from the ring gear under shock loads. Most reported failures are on 1998–99 trucks. Toyota fitted a four-pinion diff from the 2000 model year, and failures dropped.

t: When is the timing belt due?
x: At the 90,000-mile service. Owners replace the belt, water pump, thermostat and often the idlers, tensioner and cam and crank seals at the same time. IH8MUD has a full parts list and several step-by-step write-ups.

It depends what you want. 2003 and later trucks have the five-speed A750F, stronger driveshafts and 4.10 gears, and late trucks have the 275-hp VVT-i engine. 1998–99 trucks are the only ones with the optional rear locker, but they also have the weaker front diff and, Slee notes, throttle-sensor faults that can stop the truck responding to the pedal.
Kelley Blue Book lists 6,500 lb for 2002–2006 models (5,500 lb for a 1999). From 2003 a bolt-on factory hitch was offered, and the rear crossmember was changed to take it.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: KBB lists 12 mpg city and 15–16 highway, with a 25.4-gallon tank on a 2005. Lifts, 33s and a roof rack make that worse.

The LX 470 had Active Height Control and adaptive damping as standard from 1998, and owners report it was also optional on some Land Cruisers. It works well when maintained. Keep up with fluid flushes (owners cite 60,000 miles), and to lift an AHC truck you can adjust the height-sensor links, as IH8MUD's FAQ covers.

Yes, the 105 (FZJ105 and HZJ105), with coil-sprung solid axles at both ends and straight sixes carried over from the 80. It was never sold in the US; it went to Africa, Australia, Russia and South America.

t: Is the Lexus LX 470 the same truck?
x: Mechanically, yes: same chassis and drivetrain. The LX 470 adds body cladding, a plusher cabin and standard AHC with adaptive damping. Slee notes that it often got features before the Land Cruiser did.

The common setup is Old Man Emu: uprated torsion bars up front, matching coils at the rear and new shocks, sold as a kit of about 1.5 inches. The torsion-bar adjusters handle front height. IH8MUD's FAQ also links a thread on Slee's front diff drop, and any height change needs an alignment.

t: Suspension Lift — Old Man Emu (ARB), Cruiser Outfitters — OME 100 Series kit with torsion bars, Slee Off-Road — suspension
x: Fresh torsion bars, coils and shocks undo years of sag and clear 33s. Getting the front and rear heights to match the truck's load is most of the job.

t: Rock Sliders & Armor — Metal Tech 4x4 — 100 Series sliders, Slee Off-Road — sliders, Slee Off-Road — front bumpers
x: The factory running boards bend on the first rock, and the IFS front end appreciates a skid plate.
Only 1998–99 trucks offered a factory rear locker. Air lockers add front and rear lockers to the rest.
The stock intake is in the passenger front fender. Slee notes that on US trucks the power antenna has to be swapped for a whip antenna to fit a snorkel.

t: Storage & Sleeping — Slee Off-Road — drawer systems
x: Pull the third row, fit drawers with a fridge slide and add a bed extension: the same recipe as the 80.

t: Oem & Rebuild Parts — Cruiser Outfitters (CruiserTeq) — 100 Series, Cruiser Corps — 100 Series
x: Timing-belt kits, ball joints, wheel bearings and suspension in OEM or OEM-supplier quality.

SAE 5W-30 · ≈6.8 L with filter (Roughtrax); Amsoil lists 7.2 qt for 2005–07 VVT-i trucks The IH8MUD 90k list gives the dealer filter as 90915-YZZD3 and says a larger JDM filter (90915-20004) is available and preferred by some owners.
Air filter 17801-50040 (IH8MUD 90k list) The cabin filter is easy to forget; IH8MUD's 100-series FAQ links an LX 470/Land Cruiser cabin-filter DIY.
Iridium 90080-91180 ×8 · factory torque 13 ft-lb (IH8MUD) While the coils are out, check every plug for tightness: a tick or pop at cold start can be a plug walking out of the head.

t: Timing belt, tensioner, idlers & water pump
x: Belt 13568-09070 · tensioner 13540-50030 · idlers 13503-0F010 / 13505-0F010 · pump 16100-59275-83 (IH8MUD 90k list) Do the thermostat (90916-03100), cam seals and crank seal while you're in there. IH8MUD members say the cam seals are more work on the 2005–07 VVT-i engine.

≈15 L (Roughtrax). 1998–2003: Toyota red Long Life Coolant · 2004–07: pink Super Long Life Coolant, premixed (Slee) Replace the plastic heater-hose tees (87248-60460) preventively; IH8MUD says they go brittle and can dump the coolant. Radiator hoses 16571-50150 / 16572-50150 and the bypass hose are worth doing with the timing belt.
Serpentine belt 90916-02586 · belt tensioner 16620-0W101 (IH8MUD 90k list) The serpentine belt comes off for the timing belt anyway, so replace it and spin-check the idler and tensioner.

A343F (1998–2002): Toyota T-IV, ≈2.0 L per drain-and-fill · A750F (2003–07): ≈3.0 L per drain-and-fill, ≈10.6 L dry; ATF WS on trucks without a dipstick (Roughtrax) Slee: from 2004 the dipstick was deleted (level is set at the overflow plug) and ATF WS is not interchangeable with T-IV or Dexron. A drain-and-fill only swaps the sump portion, so repeat it rather than doing one big flush on unknown f

GL-5 75W-90 · 1.4 qt (IH8MUD DIY); Roughtrax lists 1.5 L HF2A full-time case, no viscous coupler (Slee). Crack the 24 mm fill plug before the drain, torque the drain plug to 27 ft-lb and don't overtighten: the case can crack. Synthetic can quiet cold-morning whine.

GL-5 80W-90 hypoid · 1.8 qt (IH8MUD write-up); Roughtrax lists 1.6 L The IFS front diff has Allen-head plugs and too little clearance for squeeze bottles, so bring a pump. Two-pinion on 1998–99, four-pinion from 2000 (Slee).

GL-5 80W-90 hypoid (LSD-rated per the write-up) · 3.5 qt (IH8MUD); Roughtrax lists 3.2 L, 3.3 L for LSD 9.5-inch ring gear. 1998–99 trucks could have the optional electric rear locker, so test that it engages (Slee).
Dexron-III ATF (Amsoil lookup) · capacity [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Rack-and-pinion IFS; Slee notes variable-gear steering arrived later in the run.

DOT 3 (Amsoil lookup; Roughtrax allows DOT 3 or 4) The 100 has a hydraulic brake booster with an electric pump: bleed with the key ON so the pump runs, and expect the ABS and brake lights to come on during the job. IH8MUD members bleed front left, front right, then the rears, and the factory manual describes extra steps for bleeding the actuator.

Toyota AHC fluid 08886-01805 (2.5 L can) · ≈4.5 L system, forum estimate (Roughtrax) Never top up with brake fluid; one IH8MUD owner's truck went soft after a dealer did. Bleed each corner with the engine off and the suspension in N.
Lithium-base NLGI No. 2 for the U-joints (Roughtrax) IH8MUD's FAQ links a driveshaft lubing schematic; any hand grease gun fits the zerks.

UZJ200 VDJ200 The V8 flagship and the last full-size Land Cruiser wagon sold in North America before Toyota pulled it after 2021. The 200 is a nearly three-ton bank vault with a 5.7-liter V8 and a crawl-control button, and it is far better in the dirt than anything with a heated steering wheel has any right to be. It was also the last of its kind in America: when it left after 2021, the big V8 Lan

Dried pink coolant trailing down the front of the engine from the water-pump weep hole, and a slowly dropping coolant level. Basic metric sockets · belt tool · coolant catch tub · Aisin water pump and gasket · Toyota long-life coolant · fan bracket if contaminated.

A check-engine light, often with the slip light flashing and 'Check VSC' on, that may come and go, especially in cold or damp weather. Codes such as P2438 (pressure sensor circuit high, bank 2). Owners on Tundra sites also report P2440–P2443. OBD-II scanner with Toyota enhanced codes · multimeter · factory wiring diagram.

t: Close the KDSS valves after suspension work
x: Alarming body roll on uneven roads, or a truck that feels wrong right after a lift or shock install. 5 mm hex key · wheel chocks · torch.
A clunk when you come to a stop, as if you'd nudged the car ahead, and another clunk when you pull away. Grease gun with a needle or angled coupler · quality chassis grease · creeper.

t: Swap to an aluminum oil filter cap
x: A plastic cap that rounds off, lets the wrench slip, warps or cracks after many heat cycles. Flat screwdriver · cap-type filter wrench · aluminum cap 15620-31060 (as listed in the IH8MUD thread).

t: Add rear air helper springs for towing
x: Almost 4 inches of sag at the hitch with a 5,000 lb trailer and about 600 lb of tongue weight, even with weight distribution set up. Jack stands · long pry bar · Firestone 4164 air-bag kit · Air Lift 25804 compressor · Air Lift 21838 union tee · RTV · zip ties · marine grease.
Red dust on the clean side of the filter, MAF faults, limp mode and, in bad cases, a failed right-hand turbo. Screwdriver · torch · MAF cleaner · grease or an aftermarket airbox.

Rough idle, smoke, poor fuel economy, sludge in the intake and DPF trouble, often caused by leaking injector seat washers. Workshop manual · injector puller · new injectors and updated washers (all eight) · a diagnostic tool to code the injectors.

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: On IH8MUD, one owner says 285/65R18 'will fit fine with zero rubbing' on a stock truck and 285/70R18 'will rub a bit but should be manageable'; others in the same thread report the 285/70 needs heat-gunning and trimming of the plastic, so treat 285/65R18 as the no-work size. One owner running 285/70R17s on aftermarket wheels reported light rubbing on the plastic liner, fixed with a heat gun. The t

KBB lists 8,500 lb for 2008, 8,200 lb for 2015 and 8,100 lb for 2016–2021. An IH8MUD owner with a 2013 quotes 8,500 lb with an 850 lb maximum tongue weight. Weight distribution helps the short 112-inch wheelbase, and rear air helpers fix sag.

2008–2015 trucks have the AB60F six-speed with 3.90 gears. 2016–2021 trucks have the AE80F eight-speed with 3.30 gears and bigger front brakes. If you plan big tires on an eight-speed truck, re-gearing (Nitro's 4.88s are a common choice) restores the lost low-end response.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: KBB lists 13 mpg city and 18 highway (15 combined) for most years, and 13/17 (14 combined) for 2021, on a 24.6-gallon tank. Toyota's 2013 press release specifies regular 87 AKI gasoline, not premium.

US trucks have full-time four-wheel drive with a lockable center differential, plus A-TRAC, CRAWL and (from 2013) Multi-Terrain Select. Front and rear lockers are aftermarket; ARB Air Lockers and Harrop E-lockers are both common in IH8MUD build signatures.

t: What is KDSS, and does it complicate a lift?
x: The Kinetic Dynamic Suspension System lets the wheels articulate more off-road while controlling body roll on the road. It complicates lifts a little: the KDSS valves are opened during suspension work and must be closed afterward. IH8MUD has a warning thread from an owner whose shop left them open.

t: Was there a diesel in the US?
x: No. North America only ever got the 5.7-liter 3UR-FE petrol V8. The 4.5-liter twin-turbo 1VD-FTV diesel was sold in Australia, Europe, the Middle East and elsewhere.

On US 3UR trucks: water pumps around 100,000 miles, secondary air-injection faults, plastic oil filter caps and dry U-joints. On diesels: injectors, the DPF and EGR on 2015-on trucks, and dust past the airbox. Unsealed also notes some 200s have a vibration that owners argue about.

t: What's special about the Heritage Edition?
x: Built for 2020 and 2021 to mark 60 years since the FJ40: two rows of seats, black or white paint, bronze BBS forged wheels, a Yakima MegaWarrior basket, no running boards or side moldings, and a vintage Land Cruiser badge. Wikipedia says 1,200 were built for the 2020 model year.

t: Why did Toyota stop selling it in the US?
x: In December 2020 Toyota told Road & Track that the Land Cruiser would end in North America after 2021. The name came back in 2024 on the smaller 250 Series, and the 300 Series flagship isn't sold in the US.

t: Is the Lexus LX 570 the same truck?
x: It shares the platform and the 3UR-FE (Lexus rates it at 383 hp and 403 lb-ft), but the LX 570 adds standard AHC height control and adaptive damping, 20-inch wheels and a lot more leather.

t: Suspension Lift — Old Man Emu (ARB), ICON Vehicle Dynamics, Slee Off-Road — suspension
x: A two- to three-inch lift with better shocks clears 285/70s and bigger. On KDSS trucks, close the valves afterward. Many IH8MUD builds pair a lift with aftermarket upper control arms.

t: Rock Sliders & Skids — Metal Tech 4x4 — 200 Series sliders, Slee Off-Road — sliders
x: The running boards are decoration. Sliders protect the rockers, and a full skid set protects the IFS, engine and transmission.

t: Gears & Lockers — Nitro Gear & Axle, ARB Air Locker, Harrop
x: Bigger tires dull the 3.30-geared eight-speed in particular. Re-gearing to 4.88 and adding selectable lockers is the classic 200 build.

t: Bumpers & Winch — Slee Off-Road — front bumpers
x: A winch-capable front bumper, plus a rear bumper with a tire carrier to free up cargo space.

t: Snorkel — Safari 4x4 Engineering, Slee Off-Road — snorkels
x: Raises the intake for water crossings and dust; IH8MUD's technical FAQ includes a Safari snorkel install. On diesels, pair it with a properly sealed airbox.

6,000 lb, according to Toyota, and the 1958 grade comes with a trailer brake controller. Owners note that a small engine doesn't give much engine braking, so on long grades use the transmission and low range rather than the service brakes alone.

t: What fuel economy and range should I expect?
x: The EPA rates it at 22 city, 25 highway and 23 combined. Car and Driver averaged 20 mpg, and Flexmotor saw about 21 off-road and 24 on the highway. The tank holds 17.9 gallons, which is why long-range tanks and jerry cans are popular.
Every US grade has a locking center differential and an electronic locking rear differential. There's no factory front locker. Slee's AT37 build added an ARB Air Locker up front.

t: Why only a four-cylinder hybrid? Can I get the diesel?
x: North America and China only get the 2.4-liter i-FORCE MAX hybrid. The 2.8-liter diesel, the 2.7 petrol and the non-hybrid 2.4 turbo are sold elsewhere. If you want a V6 on this platform in the US, the Lexus GX 550 has a 349-hp 3.4-liter twin-turbo.

t: Is it a 'real' Land Cruiser or just a Prado?
x: It's a Prado, and the Prado has always been a real Land Cruiser: ladder frame, live rear axle, full-time 4WD with low range. It shares the GA-F platform with the 300 Series, and its 112.2-inch wheelbase is the same figure the 80 Series introduced. It's smaller than the 200 Series it replaced in the US and seats two rows, not three.

t: Which grade should I buy for off-road use?
x: The 1958 is the cheapest way into center and rear lockers, but it doesn't offer the Stabilizer Disconnect Mechanism, which gives the front axle more articulation. The Land Cruiser grade (and the 2024 First Edition) can have SDM and comes on wider 265/70R18 tires. For 2027 the 1958 starts at $58,180 and the Land Cruiser at $64,255 (base MSRP).

t: What oil and fluids does it take?
x: 0W-20 engine oil (owners report about 5.9 quarts with the filter), 75W-85 GL-5 in the differentials according to the manual, and Toyota 75W 'LF' in the transfer case. Check the owner's manual for your truck's exact figures.

ICON sells 1.25–3 inch systems for the 250, Dobinsons offers a 2-inch kit, and Slee's dealer build used an ADS 2.5-inch system. Threepiece tested a 1.5-inch Tuff Country leveling kit with 285/70R17s and reported no rubbing.

t: Is the new raised air intake a snorkel?
x: No. The $980 factory raised intake offered for 2027 isn't watertight, so Motor1 notes it doesn't improve wading the way a sealed snorkel would. It helps with dust.

It's early days. Recalls so far are an instrument-cluster software update, a corrected load-capacity label, a rear-camera fix, and an interim fuel-pipe connector notice. Common owner complaints are front-brake squeal in reverse (fixed by a TSB), 12 V battery drain, and hybrid-battery fan warnings. The US 250 doesn't use the V35A V6 involved in the LX and Tundra bearing recalls.

VJA300 FJA300 GRJ300 The current global flagship, unveiled in June 2021 — and not sold in the US or Canada. This is the Land Cruiser the rest of the world gets and America has to admire from a distance. It's lighter, stiffer and quicker than the 200, and its engineers used a 30-year-old 80 Series as the benchmark. The only way to buy one in the US is with a Lexus badge on the front.

x: IH8MUD owners report 275/70R18 (about 33.3 inches) and 285/70R18 KO3s (about 33.7 inches) with no rubbing on stock suspension. One LX owner with 275/70R18s had no rub at any AHC height, at full lock, in drive or reverse. 295/70R18s on stock wheels have been reported on an LX 700h Overtrail, and Dissent Off-Road told a member that 35s on a +40 mm offset wheel fit with minimal to zero trimming.

t: Can I buy a 300 Series in the US?
x: Not new. It isn't sold in the US or Canada, and the 25-year import rule rules out bringing one in for decades. The Lexus LX 600 and LX 700h are the same truck under the skin and are sold in North America.

t: Why didn't Toyota sell it in America?
x: Wikipedia cites slow sales of the 200 Series and limited production capacity. The smaller 250 took over the Land Cruiser name in the US for 2024.

It depends on the market: a 3.4-liter twin-turbo petrol V6 (409 hp), a 3.3-liter twin-turbo diesel V6 (304 hp), a carried-over 4.0-liter V6 in some places, and since 2025 a 457-hp V6 hybrid. All but the 4.0 use a 10-speed automatic.

Every 300 has a lockable center differential. The GR Sport adds front and rear lockers. On the Lexus side, the LX 700h Overtrail has all three, and Wikipedia also lists a Japan-only LX 'Offroad' trim with three.

t: How much lighter is it than the 200?
x: About 200 kg (440 lb), thanks to the redesigned GA-F frame and laser-welded mixed-metal construction. The V6s are also lighter than the V8s they replaced and sit further back.

The US LX 600 shares the V35A with the Tundra, and both are covered by recalls 24V381 and 25V767 for machining debris that can ruin the main bearings. Later engines were built with improved processes or an improved main bearing, and some are still under investigation. Owners routinely do early oil changes and oil analysis.

t: What did Toyota use as the benchmark?
x: The 80 Series. Chief engineer Takami Yokoo said the 80 still had 'the best rough road performance of any Land Cruiser,' and the 300 keeps the wheelbase the 80 introduced.

t: How long was the waiting list?
x: In January 2022 Auto Bild reported Toyota Japan quoting waits of up to four years for new orders.
ANCAP's 2022 rating, aligned with Euro NCAP, scored 89% for adult occupants, 88% for child occupants, 81% for vulnerable road users and 77% for safety assist.

Land Rover started in 1948 as a stopgap: Rover's chief designer Maurice Wilks proposed a light agricultural and utility vehicle, and the first prototype was skinned in Birmabright aluminium alloy because steel was rationed and aluminium wasn't. It was launched at the Amsterdam Motor Show in April that year, and the Series I, II, IIA and III that followed ran until 1985. In 1983 the One Ten arrived

Series I Series II Series IIA Series III 88 109 Leaf springs, aluminium panels, selectable 4WD: the agricultural original that put the world's backcountry on wheels. A tractor that learned to do 55 mph, built from aluminium because steel was rationed, and still the vehicle that taught most of the world what a 4x4 is. Slow, loud, honest, and fixable with the tools in a farm shed.

t: What's the difference between a Series I, II, IIA and III?
x: Series I (1948–58) has flat sides and 80, 86/88 or 107/109-inch wheelbases. Series II (1958–61) brought the wider 'barrel side' body and the 2.25 petrol. Series IIA (1961–71) looks almost identical but added the 2.25 diesel and the 2.6 six, and late home-market IIAs have headlamps in the wings. t: Were Series Land Rovers sold new in the US?
x: Yes, but not many. Factory sales to North America ended in 1974. Only 811 of the long-wheelbase IIAs with the 2.6 six were NADA (North American Dollar Area) trucks, the only long-wheelbase models built for the US and Canada.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: Owners on AULRO report roughly 14–17 mpg (imperial) for a 2.25 petrol in normal use, with a best of about 21 mpg at a steady 50 mph in a short-wheelbase truck. Loaded, hilly driving pulls it back toward 14. In US gallons, knock about a sixth off those figures.

Owners on the Rovers North forum put the comfortable cruise for a 2.25 petrol at 55–60 mph. With a Fairey overdrive, 60–65 on the flat is realistic. One owner advises 3,000–3,400 rpm for the four-cylinder petrol and warns that sitting at 4,000-plus wears engines out faster.

t: Why do Series rear half-shafts break?
x: Partly the design of the shafts and partly overloading in commercial use. Land Rover strengthened the axles and hubs in 1980 and increased the driveshaft spline count from 10 to 24 in 1982. Forum members say shafts usually break at the differential end, and worn drive flanges announce themselves with a clunk well before they strip.

t: Should I fit free-wheeling front hubs?
x: Rovers North advises against it on Series IIA/III swivels with the Railko bush: running the hubs unlocked stops the front driveline turning, which it says starves the swivel ball, Railko bush and front propshaft of lubrication. If you fit them anyway, lock them in regularly.

t: Petrol or diesel? Soft top or wagon?
x: On value, Hagerty found petrol trucks worth about 6% more than diesels and soft-tops about 2% more than wagons. In use, the 2.25 petrol is the more pleasant road engine; the early 2.0 and 2.25 diesels are slow even by Series standards.

The aluminium body doesn't rust but corrodes where it touches steel. The steel parts do rust: rear crossmember, outriggers, chassis box sections above the bump stops, the lower bulkhead and footwells, door hinge areas and door bottoms.

t: Can I put tubeless tyres on the original wheels?
x: Not properly. Original Series rims are tube-type. Tubeless radials need wheels with safety humps, which later Defender wheels have. Don't fit inner tubes in tubeless wheels.
Just under 600,000 by February 1968, more than 70% of them exported. The 1,000,000th Land Rover was built in 1976, and about 440,000 Series IIIs were made between 1971 and 1985.

t: Can I import a Defender into the US?
x: Yes, if it's at least 25 years old counted from its date of manufacture: NHTSA lets those vehicles in without meeting FMVSS (declared under Box 1 on the HS-7). Newer trucks must comply, which a classic Defender can't. Check EPA and your state's emissions rules too, and make sure the VIN, chassis number and build date line up.

Everything built at least 25 years before the import date, so in late 2026 that's trucks built up to late 2001. That covers 200Tdi, 300Tdi, V8 and early Td5 Defenders (the Td5 arrived in 1998). The Ford 'Puma' Defenders from 2007 won't start qualifying until 2032.

North American Specification Defenders were the ones Land Rover sold new in the US and Canada: 525 1993 Defender 110s (500 US, 25 Canada) and Defender 90s from 1994 to 1997, all V8. About 7,059 were built in total.

t: Why did Land Rover stop selling the Defender in the US after 1997?
x: Regulations taking effect for 1998, including airbag and side-impact door requirements, made it too expensive to keep the old body compliant. The Defender name returned to US showrooms in 2020 on the all-new L663.

For a gray-market truck, the 300Tdi is the simple, mechanical favourite; check the revised timing kit has been fitted. The 200Tdi is cruder but similar. The Td5 is more powerful (122 hp) but electronically managed, so check for oil in the injector loom. In the US, NAS trucks are all 3.9/4.0 V8, which is thirsty but easy to service.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: ECD estimates 12–16 mpg for the factory V8 (12–14 in real-world use), 23–27 mpg for the 300Tdi, 22–26 mpg for the Td5 and 20–25 mpg for the Puma diesels; it doesn't say how they were measured. Roof racks, big tyres and a heavy right foot will take you well under those.

t: How much can a classic Defender tow?
x: CarsGuide lists 3,500 kg (7,716 lb) braked for 2004 Defender 90, 110 and 130 variants, and GoAuto gives the same 3,500 kg braked / 750 kg unbraked for the 2009 Defender 90. Unbraked trailers are limited to 750 kg. Check your own truck's plate and handbook; the rear crossmember condition matters more than the brochure number.

t: When do I lock the centre diff?
x: Whenever you expect prolonged wheelspin: mud, snow, ice, sand, steep loose climbs. The LT230's stock centre diff has small gears that can fail if a front wheel spins for long, and the diff lock removes that risk. Unlock it on grippy surfaces to avoid driveline wind-up.

The aluminium panels don't rust, but they oxidise, lifting paint and eventually perforating. The steel parts rust: chassis rear crossmember, outriggers, bulkhead footwells and corners, door frames and hinge mounts. Budget for welding unless the truck already has a galvanised chassis.

t: Suspension Lift — Old Man Emu (ARB), Terrafirma
x: Stock springs sag with age and accessories. Heavier springs and better shocks restore ride height and add an inch or two for 255/85 tyres.
Open diffs front and rear; an air locker or ATB limited-slip transforms progress on articulated ground.
Rebuilt or brand-new LT230s, taller ratios for big tyres, ATB centre diffs and heavy-duty 300M shafts.

x: Seals, swivel kits, panels, NAS-specific trim, timing kits: these are the US and UK catalogues the community actually uses.
When the frame is past welding, a hot-dip galvanised replacement chassis is the permanent fix.
The NAS trucks wore cages from the factory; external and internal cages are a common addition for serious trail use.

t: Can I put a rooftop tent on it?
x: Yes. Land Rover quotes a static roof load of up to 661 lb (300 kg) and a dynamic load of up to 370 lb on the 110 and 130 (260 lb on the 90) with off-road tyres and the Expedition Roof Rack. V8 models have no dynamic roof rating, and the OCTA's is zero in OCTA mode.
All 110 models have air as standard. The 90 can have coils or air. Coil 90s give 226 mm of ground clearance against 291 mm maximum for air, and lose the height-adjustable modes.
It has a lockable centre differential and a locking rear differential (Land Rover's Electronic Active Differential), plus brake-based torque vectoring and a two-speed transfer case.
Yes. A front-mounted 4,536 kg (10,000 lb) load-rated winch is officially supported, which is unusual for a unibody.

t: How often should I change the oil?
x: The headline service interval is up to 21,000 miles or two years, but Defender2.net members point out that oil changes are flagged by a separate condition-based counter, often around 15,000 miles for diesels in mixed use. Many enthusiasts change oil every 7,000–10,000 miles regardless.

US trucks launched with 2.0 four-cylinder and 3.0 six-cylinder engines, and Land Rover USA's current 110 spec page lists only the 3.0 six, with the OCTA sold as its own model. In Europe and Australia the D250/D300 diesels are the long-distance favourites, though the mild hybrids have had DC-DC converter failures and the diesels have DPF and EGR sensor faults.

It's better than its reputation off-road and worse than a Toyota in the workshop. A TFL review collected early-ownership faults, and common owner reports include DC-DC converters on MHEVs, PM/EGR sensor codes on diesels, steering knocks and several recall campaigns. Keep it on warranty or budget for a diagnostic tool and a good specialist.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: Official NEDC figures range from about 7.6 L/100 km (31 mpg US) for the 3.0 diesels to 9.9 L/100 km (24 mpg US) for the P400 and 12.1 L/100 km (19 mpg US) for the P525 V8. One D300 owner reported 40 mpg (imperial) cruising at 110 km/h across France.

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?

Owners do run 33s and bigger with lifts; one member says 35s want at least a 4.1 and ideally a 4.37 ring and pinion.

t: When was it sold in the US?
x: From the 1994 to 1998 model years, always with the V8: 3.9 litres with Lucas 14CUX injection at first, then the GEMS-managed '4.0' (same 3,946 cc) from 1996 for OBD-II.

t: How is it related to the Range Rover Classic and Defender?
x: It uses the Range Rover Classic's chassis, suspension and four-wheel-drive system, much of its body structure, and the same LT230 transfer box and Tdi engines as the Defender of the same era.

t: Can I import a diesel Disco 1 into the US?
x: Every Discovery Series I was built by 1998, so all of them are now more than 25 years old. NHTSA allows vehicles at least 25 years old (from date of manufacture) to be imported without meeting FMVSS; check EPA and your state's rules and make sure the VIN and build date line up.

The 300Tdi is the enthusiast favourite: mechanical, economical and shared with the Defender, though it needs the revised timing kit. The 200Tdi is cruder but similar. The V8 is smoother and easy to source in the US but thirsty and sensitive to cooling problems.

t: What fuel economy should I expect from the V8?
x: Not much. One owner of a 3.9 V8 reported about 10.5 mpg (imperial) at 100–120 km/h and was trying to get closer to 14. Tired V8s lose economy as the camshaft wears, according to experienced members.

Two inches is the common, sensible lift using longer springs and extended shocks; owners advise lowering the bump stops so the body isn't damaged at full compression. Owners running bigger lifts fit caster-corrected (6-degree) arms and wide-angle propshafts, and regear for big tyres.
Yes, badly. The usual places are the sills, rear floor and boot floor, inner wings, body mounts and the rear chassis around the crossmember. Three-doors are reported to be worse.

The plastic surround leaks where it meets the metal roof, the frame seal is flimsy, and the drain tubes and cups split with age. LandyZone owners call the drain installation 'appalling'. Resealing and new drains usually cure it.

t: Which Discoveries did the Camel Trophy use?
x: The Discovery was the main Camel Trophy vehicle from 1990 to 1997: 200Tdis from Siberia (1990, three-door) to South America (1994), then 300Tdis from 1995 to Mongolia in 1997. Japan and Germany also got Sandglow Camel Trophy special editions.
A badge-engineered Discovery 1 sold in Japan by Honda, a product of Rover's cross-holding with Honda that ended when BMW bought Rover in 1994.

The first LX 450, which reached US buyers as a 1996 model, was almost entirely the J80 Land Cruiser with leather, wood and a new grille. t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: The stock size is 275/70R16. On a stock-height 80 Series or LX 450 with healthy springs, the usual answer is 285/75R16, about 33 in. Owners report it works, with some rubbing possible at full flex or full lock. Anything bigger starts rubbing. Slee's guide notes that 35s are possible with a 2-in Old Man Emu lift, but expect to rub when crawling unless you lower the bump stops.

A 1997 spec sheet lists a 2,268 kg (5,000 lb) maximum trailer weight. Slee warns that the four bolt holes in the black rear crossmember (covered by trim on the LX) aren't rated for towing in the US, so use a frame-mounted receiver hitch.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: The EPA rates both years at 12 mpg city, 14 highway and 13 combined on regular fuel. Bigger tires and a roof rack push that lower.

t: What fluids and capacities does it take?
x: According to AMSOIL's 1997 LX 450 lookup: engine oil 7.8 qt with filter (10W-30 above -18°C, 5W-30 below 10°C). Coolant 14.8 qt with the front heater only, or 15.9 qt with front and rear heaters. The A343F transmission takes 11.6 qt total. The transfer case takes 3.6 pt of GL-4 or GL-5 gear oil. The front diff takes 5.5 pt (with locker) or 5.9 pt (without) and the rear diff 7 pt, both GL-5 90-weig

Every LX 450 has a center differential that locks automatically in low range. Electric front and rear axle lockers were a factory option, and BaT listings describe triple-locked trucks. If yours has them there are locker controls on the dash. Test them in low range on a loose surface before you buy. For unlocked trucks Slee recommends ARB Air Lockers, which cost less than retrofitting the factory

t: Can I lock the center diff in high range?
x: Not from the factory. US trucks from 1993 on had the switch deleted but kept the wiring. A plug-in CDL switch (Slee TOY1002 for 1995–1997) adds high-range locking in under an hour.

t: How worried should I be about the head gasket?
x: Worried enough to budget for it, but not enough to panic. Expedition Portal regulars say 1995–1997 1FZ-FEs are the ones to watch, and that risk climbs past 150k and especially 200k miles, with overheating in hot climates as a trigger. A properly done gasket job with receipts adds about $1,500–$2,000 in value. Others note plenty of unreplaced gaskets go past 200k without trouble.

t: Should I regear for bigger tires?
x: The 1FZ-FE trucks come with 4.11 gears. Slee suggests regearing to 4.56, 4.88 or 5.29 when you go up in tire size. Opinions vary on the right ratio, so its advice is to drive a truck with the setup you're considering first.

t: What's the difference between an LX 450 and a 1996–1997 Land Cruiser?
x: Mechanically, very little. The LX has softer suspension, extra sound deadening, softer leather, auto climate control, a console subwoofer, body cladding, larger rear bumper corners and two-tone mud flaps. The LX mud flaps don't swap onto a Toyota. Parts and aftermarket kits for the FZJ80 fit both.

Old Man Emu coil-and-shock kits are the classic answer. Slee's guide mentions OME 2-in lifts with 35s, and owners run OME 850/864-series coils. Metal Tech 4x4 sells 1.5-in and 2-in front spacer plates, adjustable rear upper and offset lower links, sway-bar drop brackets and caster plates for the 80 Series and LX 450. If you lift the truck, readjust the load-sensing brake proportioning valve.

There are only two, and they're nearly the same. The 1996 and 1997 trucks both have the A343F, airbags and OBD-II. Buy the one with the best records, the healthiest knuckles and working lockers. Factory lockers add about $2,500 in value according to forum regulars, so a locked truck is worth the wait.

t: Suspension Lift — Old Man Emu, Metal Tech 4x4 (spacers, links, caster plates)
x: A mild lift with better shocks gets you on 33s without rubbing. Adjustable rear links and caster plates keep the geometry right as you go taller.
If the truck didn't come with factory lockers, air lockers are cheaper than retrofitting the electric ones, and the OEM switch and dash lights can be wired to run them.

t: Rock Sliders — Metal Tech 4x4 (80 Series / LX 450 sliders), Slee Off-Road
x: The cladding and running boards are fragile and the rocker panels are expensive. Frame-mounted sliders protect both and still work as a step.

t: Bumpers & Swing-Outs — Dissent Off-Road (LC80), Slee Off-Road
x: A real front bumper carries a winch and protects the radiator. A rear bumper with a swing-out carrier lifts a full-size spare off the ground.
The stock air intake is in the passenger front fender. A snorkel moves it to roof height for water crossings. Slee says to fit one for wading, not for the debated performance gains.

t: Maintenance Parts — Cruiser Corps (80 Series), CruiserTeq (80 Series & LX 450)
x: At this age the knuckles, hoses and seals matter more than the accessories. Specialist shops stock kits by chassis.
10W-30 (above −18°C) or 5W-30 (below 10°C) · 7.8 qt with filter Drain plug torque is 18 ft-lb. An oil analysis on the first drain gives a useful head-gasket baseline. Look for coolant in the oil.
1FZ-FE panel element Check the intake hose and boot for cracks. IH8MUD regulars list a worn intake hose as a common 80 Series fault.

Denso OEM plugs [CONFIRM GAP IN MANUAL] The 1FZ-FE uses a distributor and plug wires, so replace the wires with the plugs on an unknown truck. Spark plug tube seals stop oil pooling in the plug wells.

Toyota red coolant · 14.8 qt (front heater) / 15.9 qt (front + rear heaters) Overheating is what kills 1FZ head gaskets. Expedition Portal regulars say to use Toyota red only and to check the water pump, fan clutch and thermostat. A replaced radiator or crud in the overflow bottle are clues to past overheating (Slee).
Rubber hoses under the intake, driver's side The PHH and the bypass hoses above it can strand you when they fail. Original clamps mean original hoses.

Dexron III-type ATF (AMSOIL lists AF3 for the A343F) · 11.6 qt total fill A pan drain only replaces part of the 11.6 qt, so repeat the drain-and-fill a couple of times rather than pressure-flushing an old transmission.
GL-4 or GL-5 gear oil · 3.6 pt The center diff is viscous-coupled on these trucks. Note any binding or clunks in tight turns on pavement.

GL-5 90 (80W-90 below −18°C) · front 5.5 pt with locker / 5.9 pt without · rear 7 pt If the truck has factory lockers, test them in low range on a loose surface (Slee). Water in the gear oil means bad breathers or seals.

Moly grease in the birfields, MP grease in the wheel bearings Pull the square knuckle fill plug. Runny grease means diff oil is getting past the inner axle seals (Slee). See the knuckle rebuild above for preload specs.
DEXRON-III ATF Persistent leaks are often the reservoir seals, not the box or the hoses (Unsealed 4X4).

DOT 3 hydraulic brake fluid (AMSOIL application guide) Slee reports front pads lasting about 10–15k miles (1997 pads last longer). If the truck has been lifted, the load-sensing proportioning valve needs readjusting.
1FZ accessory belts
MP grease at every zerk, including the slip yokes Overland Tailor's IH8MUD write-up blames most 80 Series driveline vibrations and clunks on driveshafts that were never serviced.
OEM fuel filter · PCV valve

J100 UZJ100 2UZ-FE 100 Series Land Cruiser underneath, with the 4.7-liter 2UZ-FE V8 and hydraulic Adjustable Height Control (AHC) suspension. A 100 Series Land Cruiser with a hydraulic party trick: it rises on its toes to clear a rock, then kneels so you can load the groceries. Keep up with the AHC fluid and the timing belt and it may well outlast the people who sold it new.

A harsh or bouncy ride, dark or metallic-gray fluid in the reservoir, sluggish leveling, or a flush that's overdue (owners say Lexus recommends one every 60k miles). 10 mm wrench · clear tubing · catch bottle · fluid evacuator or turkey baster · penetrating oil · Toyota AHC fluid 08886-01805
You want more ground clearance in Normal without giving up AHC. 10 mm socket · cut-off wheel · aluminum flat stock · drill · AHC fluid · tape measure

t: Timing belt, water pump and 90k service
x: The mileage says 90k, 180k or 270k with no proof the belt was done, or there's a weeping water pump or a rough idler bearing. ¾-in breaker bar · crank-pulley holder and puller · seal puller · thread locker · FIPG · drain pan · FSM
Clicking or no-crank conditions that come and go and get worse until it won't start. Long extensions · magnetic pickup · 22 mm wrench (fuel line) · new intake gaskets · rags

A tick-tick-pop at cold start that can sound like an exhaust leak, a misfire or coil failure. In the worst case a plug blows out of the head and takes the threads with it. Spark plug socket · extensions · torque wrench (in-lb and ft-lb) · compressed air · plugs · coil boots
A tick from the engine bay that's loudest cold and fades as the manifold heats and expands. Penetrating oil · stud extractor · engine support or jack · new gaskets and studs

Power-steering fluid leaking from the rack boots, play in the steering or a heavy feel. Long extensions · universal joints · 17 mm line wrench · metric sockets · new oil-filter-housing gasket · rack bushings

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: The IH8MUD 100 Series FAQ answer is 285/75R16 or 285/65R18, both about 33 in, with no lift. An owner with a stock '99 found 295/75R16 a tight fit that might not clear at full bump and full lock. Stock sizes were 16-in wheels to 2002 and 275/60R18 from 2003.

t: How much can an LX 470 tow?
x: 6,500 lb with the towing package.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: The EPA rates a 2002 truck (four-speed) at 12 city, 15 highway and 13 combined. Five-speed trucks are rated 12 city, 15–16 highway and 13 combined. All run on regular fuel.

t: Is it a timing belt or a chain?
x: A belt. The 2UZ-FE is due every 90k miles. Owners replace the water pump, idlers, tensioner and thermostat at the same time, and often the starter or its contacts too, since the intake is already half apart.

If it's healthy, yes. It gives you adjustable ground clearance a spring truck can't match, and a fluid flush is a one-hour job. Owners whose AHC failed have switched to conventional suspension instead. One IH8MUD member went to Old Man Emu 2.5-in heavy springs and called it much cheaper than replacing AHC sensors and actuators, which another member described as very expensive.

t: How do I lift an LX 470?
x: The cheapest way is to adjust the AHC height-sensor links. That gives about 2 in up front (2.5 in with a trimmed heim joint) and about 1.75 in at the rear, or more with an extended bracket. Keep at least 70 mm of front droop for CV boot life, add a diff drop and get an alignment. The other route is removing the AHC and fitting conventional torsion bars, springs and shocks.

US trucks have a lockable center differential, plus brake-based A-TRAC from 2000. A factory rear locker was only offered on Canadian LX 470s in 1998–1999. Aftermarket air lockers are the usual upgrade.

Forum regulars favor 2000 and later for the stronger 4-pinion front differential, and 2003 and later for the A750F five-speed, which one member says makes a big difference. The 2006–2007 trucks add VVT-i and more power. The 2003–2007 trucks should also have had the steering-shaft recall done.

t: What's different from a 100 Series Land Cruiser?
x: The LX has the same drivetrain but different styling and equipment. It had AHC and AVS standard from 1998 (the Land Cruiser only got AHC as an option in 2006), front and rear automatic climate control, a power tilt and telescoping column, projector lows and fogs, body cladding and its own gauges and wheels.

t: Are there recalls I should check?
x: Yes. The big one is the July 2010 recall of about 39,000 2003–2007 LX 470s, which replaced the steering-shaft snap ring and added a retainer. There was also a 2004 US recall that added a resistor to dim daytime running lights that were too bright. In Australia, front rotor bolts and a dash wiring harness were recalled too.

t: What's that tick from the engine?
x: It could be either of two common 2UZ problems. A cracked driver's-side exhaust manifold ticks when cold and fades as it warms. A spark plug working loose makes a similar sound and is far more dangerous, because it can blow out of the head. IH8MUD members recommend checking the plugs first.

t: Suspension & Ahc — Metal Tech 4x4 (100 Series / LX 470 rear links), Old Man Emu
x: Adjust the AHC sensors for a lift, refresh the fluid and globes, or convert to conventional springs. Whichever route you take, adjustable rear links keep the rear axle centered once the truck is lifted.

t: Rock Sliders — Metal Tech 4x4 (100 Series / LX 470 sliders), Slee Off-Road
x: The cladding and running boards are expensive to replace. Sliders that bolt to the frame protect the rockers and can still work as steps.

t: Bumpers & Swing-Outs — Dissent Off-Road (LC100 / LX 470), Slee Off-Road
x: A modular front bumper protects the radiator and carries a winch, which matters on a truck this heavy. A rear bumper with swing-outs moves the spare up and out of the way.

t: Skid Plates — Dissent Off-Road (LC100 skids), Slee Off-Road
x: The IFS front differential and the transfer case sit low and exposed.
The stock intake is in the passenger fender. On US-spec trucks Slee notes the power antenna has to be swapped for a whip antenna.

t: Maintenance Parts — Cruiser Corps (100 Series), Cruiser Outfitters
x: Timing-belt kits, idlers, cam seals and plugs, stocked by people who know the chassis.

OEM belt 90916-02586 per IH8MUD 90k list

Fluid type per reservoir cap [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] The brake system uses a high-pressure pump and accumulator, not a vacuum booster. Follow the IH8MUD brake-flush procedure and take any ABS/BRAKE warning seriously.
UZJ100/LX470 fuel filter · PCV valve (1998–07/2002 part shown)

J200 URJ200 3UR-FE The 200 Series twin, powered by the 5.7-liter 3UR-FE V8 (383 hp in US/Canada trim). Nearly three tons of hydraulically levitated V8 that Car and Driver called the most desirable SUV on the planet. The punchline is that a used one often costs less than the Land Cruiser it's built on.

A wet line or pink crust along the top plastic tank next to the molded platform, slow coolant loss and a sweet smell after a drive. It's most often reported on 2008–2010 trucks. Basic metric sockets · drain pan · hose pliers · Toyota Super Long Life Coolant · new radiator (later part number)

Pink crust or drips around the water pump weep hole at the front of the engine. It's commonly reported on 2008 trucks. Metric sockets · fan clutch wrench · drain pan · new pump and gasket · Toyota SLLC

Pink coolant dripping from the top of the transmission hump at the back of the engine, with the water pump area dry. Long extensions · swivel sockets · gasket scraper · grey FIPG · union pipe O-rings · new intake gaskets

A clunk or 'thunk' when pulling away or stopping, driveline vibration and dry slip yokes. 12 mm and 14 mm sockets · 14 mm wrench · extensions · torque wrench · pry bar · paint pen · grease gun with MP grease

A sudden no-crank, usually with no warning. The failure is typically in the solenoid, the high-current relay built onto the back of the starter. Metric sockets · long extensions · battery terminal wrench · new or reman starter

Wet hydraulic fluid at line junctions or actuators, uneven leveling, a sagging corner or a harsh ride. Flashlight · mirror · Techstream-capable scan tool · factory repair manual

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: The stock size is 285/50R20. The practical limit is about 33 in, and even that meant moving the front fender liner forward about an inch on one IH8MUD member's LX. His 35x12.5R20 build needed the liner moved further, the sidestep return trimmed and the body mount reshaped, with spacers giving about +35 mm effective offset. The LX is easier to fit than a Land Cruiser because it doesn't have the KDS

t: How much can an LX 570 tow?
x: Up to 8,500 lb at launch. The 2016-on owner's manual lists 7,000 lb (with trailer brakes) for the facelifted truck, so check the manual for your year. The hitch receiver is built into the frame.

t: What fuel economy should I expect, and does it need premium?
x: Yes, the EPA lists premium fuel. The six-speed 2008 is rated 12 city, 18 highway and 14 combined. The eight-speed 2016 is rated 13 city, 18 highway and 15 combined.

The US LX 570 has a lockable Torsen center differential plus A-TRAC, Crawl Control and, from 2013, Multi-Terrain Select. It has no factory front or rear axle lockers. Owners who want them fit aftermarket units such as ARB Air Lockers.

t: Is the AHC going to bankrupt me?
x: Probably not, if you buy a healthy one. One long-time IH8MUD poster wrote that after ten years in service the LX 570's AHC had turned out to be well engineered, without the expected horror stories. But leaks at line junctions and actuators are expensive, so inspect the system carefully before you buy.

They share the same frame, V8, transmission and transfer case. The LX swaps coil springs and KDSS for AHC, adds more luxury equipment and 20-in wheels, and over time got its own styling, with unique front and rear ends from 2016. DrivingLine noted that used LX 570s were typically priced below comparable Land Cruisers.

The 2008–2010 trucks have the most radiator-crack reports, and owners say 2008s had water-pump issues. The 2013–2015 trucks add Multi-Terrain Select and Turn Assist. The 2016 and later trucks get the eight-speed and a new interior. There is no 2012 model year in the US.

t: Is it a timing belt or a chain?
x: A chain. The 3UR-FE is a chain-driven DOHC V8, so there's no 90k belt service like the LX 470's.
Not in the US. Production of the 2011 model ran late and the 2013 started early, so the 2012 model year was skipped.

t: What does Crawl Control actually do?
x: It works like an off-road cruise control. It controls throttle and brakes to hold a slow, steady speed over obstacles, forward or in reverse. From 2013 you can choose from five speeds, and Turn Assist brakes the inside rear wheel to tighten low-range turns.

t: Rock Sliders — Metal Tech 4x4 (LX 570 sliders), Slee Off-Road
x: The aluminum running boards and AHC lines live along the rockers. Real sliders protect both.

t: Bumpers & Swing-Outs — Dissent Off-Road (LX570 front, LC200/LX570 rear), Slee Off-Road
x: The LX has its own front end, so it needs an LX-specific front bumper. The rear is shared with the Land Cruiser.

t: Skid Plates & Guards — BudBuilt (LC200 / LX570 cat guard), Slee Off-Road
x: The factory plastic won't stop a rock. Bash plates and a catalytic-converter guard protect the expensive parts underneath.

t: Rear Links — Metal Tech 4x4 (200 Series / LX570 links)
x: Adjustable links let you re-center the rear axle and correct pinion angle once ride height changes.
US trucks came without axle lockers. Air lockers add front and rear locking without touching the AHC.
Nearly three tons of truck needs a winch on a proper bumper and recovery points rated for the job.

Not a fault. The factory 22s limit you to low-profile tires that dislike rocks. Lug wrench · torque wrench · hub-centric wheels in the right offset · TPMS sensors

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: The factory size on 22s is 265/50R22, about 32 in. Owners on aftermarket 20s run 275/60R20 (about 33 in) and 285/55R20 without rubbing, and 275/70R18 fits on Toyota TRD 18-inch wheels. 285/50R22 on factory wheels needed cutting and spacers. Without a lift, plan on about 33 in.

t: Is my LX 600 part of the engine recall?
x: If it's a 2022–2024, possibly. Recall 24V-381 covered 3,524 LX 600s built from July 30, 2021 to November 25, 2022, with engine replacement as the remedy. Recall 25V-767 (Lexus 25LA07) covers 9,895 LXs built from February 26, 2022 to April 2, 2024. Check your VIN at lexus.com/recall or nhtsa.gov. The 25V-767 remedy is a No. 1 main-bearing inspection, with engine replacement if needed.
8,000 lb with trailer brakes, per the owner's manual (1,650 lb without). KBB lists the same 8,000-lb rating for every 2027 LX.

t: Is the LX 600 just a 300 Series Land Cruiser?
x: Underneath, yes: same GA-F platform and 112-in wheelbase. Toyota didn't sell the LC300 in North America, which made the LX 600 the US version.

There's a lockable center diff, but no US LX 600 has front or rear lockers. The F Sport gets a Torsen limited-slip rear. Triple locks came on Japan's LX Offroad grade and, in the US, on the LX 700h Overtrail.

t: How do I use 4L and the diff locks?
x: Owners say the center diff lock can be engaged while moving slowly in Drive. Shifting into 4L requires the truck to be stopped and in neutral. On trucks with axle lockers, the front and rear lockers need 4L and the center lock engaged first, at very low speed. If you switch off the engine in 4L, MTS won't come back on automatically.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: The EPA rates the 2025 LX 600 at 17 mpg city, 22 highway and 19 combined, on premium fuel.

t: How much lighter is it than the LX 570?
x: Lexus says 441 lb (200 kg) lighter, with a frame it calls 20 percent more rigid.
At normal ride height, 25° approach, 23° breakover and 20° departure. Lexus hasn't published figures for the Hi1 and Hi2 heights. Maximum wading depth is 700 mm (27.5 in).

t: Why does it clunk into first gear?
x: Owners report a clunk into first on rolling stops, and sometimes on 6–5 downshifts, in 2022–2024 LX 600s. There's no known fix. Gentle throttle while the transmission decides helps, and larger tires make it less noticeable. Owners say the LX 700h hybrid doesn't do it.

t: Should I buy one without AHC?
x: If you plan to lift it, maybe. Slee Off-Road's LX 600 build was a Premium custom-ordered without AHC so it could run Dobinsons suspension. AHC trucks keep the adjustable ride heights but limit your lift choices.
